title: AFRY Netherlands awarded contract to support future Dutch offshore wind development
content:
AFRY Netherlands awarded contract to support future Dutch offshore wind development TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
AFRY Netherlands awarded contract to support future Dutch offshore wind development
The Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs has awarded a contract to AFRY Netherlands
B.V. to provide consultative engineering services supporting the development
of future offshore wind sites in the Netherlands.
The three year contract will focus on delivering cost effectiveness studies
and business case analyses to support offshore wind planning and investment
decisions.
Key areas of work include assessing economic and technical performance
indicators, such as Levelised Cost of Energy (LCOE), as well as evaluating
the main cost drivers of offshore wind projects, including capital expenditure
(CAPEX), operating expenditure (OPEX), and annual energy production (AEP).
AFRY will also undertake offshore wind farm layout and zoning optimisation
studies, alongside analyses of projected energy yields and export cable
utilisation, helping to inform future site development strategies.
The contract has an estimated maximum value of €900,000. AFRY Netherlands
B.V. was officially selected as the winning bidder on 29 July.

title: Four organisations sign MoU to support offshore wind readiness
content:
Four organisations sign MoU to support offshore wind readiness TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Four organisations sign MoU to support offshore wind readiness
Four offshore wind organisations have signed a memorandum of understanding
to support offshore wind readiness activities in Atlantic Canada. The agreement
was signed during WindEnergy Hamburg 2026.
The partnership involves the Carbon Trust, France Energies Marines, Stiftung
OFFSHORE-WINDENERGIE and Net Zero Atlantic.
The organisations will cooperate on offshore wind market development, research,
innovation, engagement and coordination.
The collaboration draws on expertise in offshore wind market development,
policy, procurement, technical research, supply chains, stakeholder engagement
and industry growth and more.
Atlantic Canada is advancing offshore wind readiness through work involving
governments, regulators, researchers, Indigenous organisations, industry
and communities to support the offshore wind sector.
Initiatives including Wind West and the Atlantic Canada Offshore Wind Readiness
Program are supporting research, transmission planning, regulatory pathways
and investment planning that are vital to the long term success of the
industry.
Potential areas of collaboration identified in the memorandum include offshore
wind resource assessment, environmental and permitting support, transmission
and cabling analysis, energy-system modelling, marine surveys, and capacity
building and knowledge exchange.

title: Montrose Port selected for Berwick Bank B offshore wind operations base
content:
Montrose Port selected for Berwick Bank B offshore wind operations base TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Montrose Port selected for Berwick Bank B offshore wind operations base
SSE has selected Montrose Port, located on Scotland's Angus coast, as the
preferred location for an operations and maintenance base for the 1.4 GW
Bank offshore wind farm.
As part of this arrangement, 100 new full time jobs are expected to be
created, including technician and engineering roles responsible for the
wind farm's day to day operations throughout its projected 35 year lifespan.
A further 30 construction roles are also expected, supporting SSE's commitment
to creating highly skilled jobs in the offshore wind sector.
First Minister John Swinney said the decision "strengthens Scotland's
offshore wind supply chain and will create more jobs, as well as investment
in skills, infrastructure and local communities."
Adding: "Scotland's ports are critical enablers of our offshore wind
ambitions and key economic assets for surrounding communities, with the
Port of Montrose set to become one of the world's largest offshore wind
operations and maintenance hubs."
Stuart Hood, director of offshore wind operations at SSE Renewables, said:
"Scotland has built a world-class offshore wind industry, and today's
announcement shows the economic opportunities that can follow when that
expertise is matched with long-term investment."

title: Saint-Gobain signs renewable electricity purchase agreement with Total Energies
content:
Saint-Gobain has signed a renewable electricity purchase agreement with
TotalEnergies for 60 GWh of electricity per year.
The agreement will supply renewable power to the group's industrial sites
in the United Kingdom. It is set to begin in April 2027 and will run for
five years.
The contract marks an important milestone, as it is Saint-Gobain's first
agreement of its kind in the UK. It also forms part of the company's wider
decarbonisation strategy and is expected to cover 20% of its annual electricity
consumption in the country.
The long-term agreement is backed by guarantees of origin from local renewable
energy assets.
"Saint-Gobain is committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions
production processes around the world," said David Molho, senior vice
president and CEO of Saint-Gobain's Northern Europe Region.
"Thanks to this agreement, Saint-Gobain in the UK is taking a major
step forward toward this objective with a reliable and continuous supply
of renewable electricity."

title: Vattenfall completes thermal camera bird monitoring trial
content:
Vattenfall has announced the completion of a year long trial of new thermal
camera technology at the
Hollandse Kust Zuid offshore wind farm.
The technology uses thermal cameras and artificial intelligence (AI) to
assess whether bird movements and potential collisions can be detected
and monitored.
The trial involved the installation of 16 thermal cameras supplied by Wildlife
Imaging Systems (WIS) on a single wind turbine, with the system covering
a range of angles over a 24 hour period.
AI was used to detect and analyse bird movements during both day and night,
and across a range of weather conditions. Researchers from Wageningen University
also assessed the system's performance in greater detail.
"At sea, it is extremely difficult to verify fatalities because there
are no remains to recover. With this study, we are adding real observations
to improve our understanding of the actual risks," said Jesper Kyed
Larsen, bioscience expert at Vattenfall.
The trial covered two migration periods, during which around 22 potential
bird collisions were identified. Two collisions were confirmed, with one
confirmed with a high degree of confidence.
The data is now being used to support a new study. The next phase will
focus on testing the technology under different conditions and at additional
locations, while further refining the monitoring system.

title: CWP, Mauritanian government progress AMAN mega-project
content:
CWP, Mauritanian government progress AMAN mega-project
Long-term contractual framework signed for multiple project phases
Renewable developer CWP Global and Mauritania’s Ministry of Energy and Petroleum signed a comprehensive agreement in Nouakchott this month, pushing forward development of the AMAN mega-project. The long-term contractual framework covers the different phases of the AMAN project and sets out the financial, economic, and developmental aspects related to its implementation. CWP expects the project to produce 1.2 million tons of renewable hydrogen and 6.6 million tons of renewable ammonia every year, with the potential for iron ore reduction in collaboration with Société Nationale Industrielle et Minière (SNIM) – Africa’s second largest producer of iron ore, based in Mauritania.
This agreement reflects the trust international investors place in Mauritania’s energy sector and establishes a comprehensive framework for project development. It is a major step toward achieving Mauritania’s ambition to become a global hub for renewable energy and green hydrogen.
H.E. Mohamed Ould Khaled, Minister of Energy and Petroleum, in his organisation’s official press release, 16 Sept 2026
This is a historic moment for our company, for Mauritanians, and for the future of the global green molecules industry. We thank the Mauritanian government for its strategic vision. Mauritania is ideally positioned to supply global markets with clean energy. The project has now reached the Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) stage, and we are targeting a Final Investment Decision before 2030.
Mark Crandall, Chairman of CWP Global, in the Mauritanian Ministry of Energy and Petroleum’s official press release, 16 Sept 2026
GreenGo Energy, Shuangliang to partner for FEED, tech deployment
Also developing a mega-project in Mauritania, Denmark-based GreenGo Energy has signed a new partnership with China-based Shuangliang for development & FEED work, engineering services, and supply of green power-to-hydrogen systems (including electrolysers). GreenGo and Shuangliang will work together on the Megaton Moon project in Mauritania, as well as a renewable ammonia project in Namibia. Shunagliang previously delivered sixteen of its electrolysis units to ACME for the first stage of ACME’s renewable ammonia project in Duqm, Oman.

title: Battery Technology’s Role in AI Growth and Innovation
content:
Stationary Batteries
Design & Manufacturing
Industry Outlook
Explore how NVIDIA, Hitachi Energy, and LG Energy Solutions are advancing AI growth with innovative, scalable battery technology solutions.
September 28, 2026
3 Min Read
LG Energy Solution's BESS and Hitachi Energy’s BESS recently qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready BESS.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming industries at an unprecedented pace. From powering advanced AI models to enabling real-time data processing, AI factories are becoming the backbone of this transformation. However, behind the scenes, these facilities face a growing need for reliable, scalable energy infrastructure that can stabilize dynamic AI workloads, which often place unpredictable demands on power systems.
Battery energy storage systems (
) are emerging as a critical solution to address these demands, and recent developments highlight their pivotal role in supporting AI growth.
LG Energy Solution
's BESS and
Hitachi Energy
’s BESS recently
qualified
as NVIDIA DSX Ready BESS, marking a significant milestone in integrating energy storage technologies with AI factory infrastructure.
As Marco Berardi, Head of Grid & Power Quality Solutions and Service at Hitachi Energy, stated, “As AI factories continue to scale, customers need power systems that can be deployed, integrated, and expanded quickly while maintaining reliability and resilience.”
Related:
La Verne Battery Fire Evacuates 500—New Tech Could Stop the Next One
Waratah Super Battery Australia, image supplied by Akaysha Energy.
What is NVIDIA DSX?
NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform is a comprehensive framework that supports and brings together all aspects of AI factory design and operations. This includes compute, networking, power, cooling, facilities, and software. According to NVIDIA, the platform addresses the unique challenges of AI factories, such as high energy consumption, scalability, and operational efficiency.
To support this vision, NVIDIA has introduced the
DSX Ready
program, a qualification initiative that helps AI factory builders identify products that meet the platform’s reference design requirements. The program initially focuses on two critical categories:
Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
:BESS solutions are essential for providing resilient and flexible power to AI factories. They help stabilize dynamic AI workloads, optimize energy costs, and integrate renewable energy sources. Qualified BESS products ensure compatibility with NVIDIA DSX requirements, reducing deployment risks and enhancing operational reliability.
Cooling Distribution Units (CDUs)
: CDUs are vital for managing the heat generated by high-performance computing systems. Efficient cooling is critical to maintaining the performance and longevity of AI factory hardware.
As Vishal Ganeriwala, a senior leader at NVIDIA, explained, “Every AI factory needs power and cooling that fit its computing architecture. As AI infrastructure expands, power, cooling, water, site, and grid constraints are shaping what builders can deploy. Choosing products that fit the complete factory design helps builders turn computing capacity into useful AI output.”
Related:
Fail-Safe BESS Technology Prevents Thermal Runaway at Single-Cell Level
The role of BESS in DSX
Battery energy storage systems are a cornerstone of the NVIDIA DSX platform. As AI factories consume vast amounts of energy, BESS solutions provide the resilience and flexibility needed to keep operations running continuously. They enable:
Dynamic power balancing
: BESS can rapidly absorb or supply power to stabilize AI workloads.
Energy cost optimization
: By storing energy during off-peak hours and supplying it during peak demand, BESS reduces operational costs.
Renewable energy Integration
: BESS supports the use of renewable energy sources, aligning with sustainability goals.
Grid code compliance
: These systems help AI factories operate within grid constraints, ensuring reliable and compliant operations.
Innovation in battery technology
The qualified solutions from the companies mentioned above show how advanced battery technologies can meet the unique demands of AI workloads, providing a reliable, scalable power solution. Hitachi Energy's qualified solution combines energy storage, power conversion, automation, and digital technologies in an integrated architecture designed to support the dynamic energy requirements of AI-driven operations.
Related:
How AI is Driving the Fastest Shift in Stationary Battery Applications in Decades
Meanwhile, LG Energy Solution's BESS meets the applicable NVIDIA DSX Ready requirements for AC energy storage solutions, helping customers bring capacity online faster while addressing critical power management challenges such as AI load smoothing, voltage ride-through, and enhanced power reliability.
Such advancements demonstrate how battery technology is evolving to meet the unique demands of next-generation
AI data centers
. The ability to seamlessly connect energy storage systems to data centers' electrical infrastructure reflects the adaptability and innovation of modern BESS solutions.

title: EV Insurance Drops: 6 Models Saving Owners Up to $917 in 2026
content:
Automotive & Mobility
After years of higher costs, electric and hybrid vehicles are getting cheaper to insure—with savings up to 19% annually on these popular models.
September 28, 2026
6 Slides
Start slideshow
The 2026 Hyundai IONIQ 5 compact electric SUV.
Insurance has been a persistent sticking point for electric vehicle ownership. For most of the past decade, EVs carried higher premiums than comparable gas cars because of structural and maturity factors. Some factors that have historically raised EV insurance include
Structural:
battery packs often sit low in the chassis, where even minor collisions can cause catastrophic damage
Immaturity:
As many OEMs roll out their first-generation EVs, certified repair networks are still few and far between
Lack of Historical Data:
As EVs have been mainstream for less than a decade, insurers have almost no claims history to price against.
However, this narrative is starting to change. Market demand has expanded repair networks, battery replacement costs have fallen alongside cell prices, and carriers now have several years of loss data on high-volume electric models. As actuarial guesswork gives way to real claims history, premiums are being repriced downward, and the vehicles the most popular vehicles are the first ones benefiting from this correction.
Related:
Volkswagen Previews 321-HP ID.3 GTI Concept as Most Powerful GTI in Brand's 50-Year History
Recently, Compare.com published
a study of more than 58 million rate quotes covering 2025 and 2026 model-year vehicles
. In it, they found that six of the ten models with the largest year-over-year insurance decreases are electric, hybrid, or offered with an electrified trim. The national average annual full-coverage premium for these model years is now $2,879, and most vehicles on the list are even lower.
We've put together a list of the six electric vehicles with the biggest insurance rate drops. Read on to learn which models are getting cheaper to insure in 2026.

title: Can Supercapacitors Smooth AI’s Power Swings?
content:
AI workloads can create load swings far sharper than steady-state compute, producing hard power spikes that conventional architectures struggle to absorb.
Supercapacitors, also called ultracapacitors, sit between conventional capacitors and batteries. They store energy as a surface charge rather than through a battery’s chemical reaction, which gives them higher power density than batteries but lower energy density. That trade-off suits short, frequent bursts rather than sustained runtime. Operators are testing supercapacitors alongside batteries and
uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems
rather than replacing them. Batteries and UPS systems still support the sustained load and provide a longer backup window.
September 2026 report
Related:
Solid-State Transformers Power Next-Gen AI Data Centers
Market Outlook: Small Today, Growing Fast
IDTechEx projects the data center supercapacitor market will reach
$950 million by 2037
, a 40.9% compound annual growth rate from 2026. That growth rate stands out against the wider category. A separate IDTechEx report
puts total global supercapacitor revenue across automotive, grid, and industrial uses at $4.86 billion by 2036, growing 15.3% annually.
Three Designs Vying for the Rack Slot
IDTechEx groups data center supercapacitors into three categories, based on how they store charge and where they fit:
EDLCs (electric double-layer capacitors).
The most commercially mature of the three, EDLCs store charge electrostatically at the electrode surface, much like a conventional capacitor.
Hybrid capacitors.
These are usually
lithium-ion (Li-ion)
hybrids, combining an EDLC’s surface charge storage with the “rocking chair” lithium-ion chemistry in which ions shuttle back and forth between electrodes during charge and discharge.
Pseudocapacitors.
These store charge through fast, reversible chemical reactions at the electrode surface rather than purely by electrostatic storage, delivering higher energy density than an EDLC but lower power density.
Backup power is the narrowest application across all three. Typical EDLC deployments sustain output for approximately 2 minutes, while some hybrids can last up to 10 minutes – enough to prevent data corruption during brief outages but not enough to replace a UPS system. IDTechEx frames supercapacitors as a complement to backup infrastructure, not a substitute.
Related:
How Power Electronics Cut Generator Run Hours in AI-Scale Data Centers
The market for supercapacitors in data centers is still in its early stages, but growing.
“The market is transitioning from early evaluation to meaningful deployment, although adoption rates vary by technology type and supply chain maturity,” said Chris Butler, president of embedded and critical power at Flex, in an interview with
Data Center Knowledge
. “Instantaneous load transients can reach more than 150% of a power shelf’s rated capacity during certain AI compute events.”
Rack designers are building in flexibility rather than committing to one architecture. “Rack designs typically include dedicated slots that can accommodate BBUs (battery backup units), CBUs (capacitor backup units), or mixed configurations, providing deployment flexibility,” Butler said. “Supply chain concerns remain a major hurdle, particularly for newer hybrid supercapacitor technologies with limited qualified suppliers.”
Parag Nathaney, principal quantitative engineer for energy policy and power markets at Exelon, tied the pace of adoption to the reliability bar data centers operate under. He told
Data Center Knowledge
that the technology must meet 99.999% reliability for the power supply, which is why he sees the market as in its early stages.
Related:
Battery Storage Moves Closer to Data Centers, but Challenges Persist
“Supercapacitors are advancing toward greater deployment, but the current state is characterized by pilot and early commercialization,” Nathaney said.
Ian Wright, chief technology officer at DIMAAG, which builds battery systems designed to avoid supercapacitors, argued that the
DC-to-DC conversion stage
determines the response time, not the device alone. “The response speed to load changes is then determined by the DC/DC, which will be slower than either caps or batteries,” Wright told
Data Center Knowledge
. “If supercaps have been tried and not observed to get hot, that’s probably because they are not actually absorbing the cyclic loads.”
What’s Next and How Operators Decide
Whether IDTechEx’s forecast for supercapacitors plays out remains to be seen. Wright expects directly connected batteries, not supercapacitors, to become the primary tool for smoothing AI power swings.
Nathaney reached a different conclusion, tied to reliability rather than economics. “I think the application of supercapacitors for data centers is novel, but the long track record of the technology in other applications could lower the barrier for adoption by data centers,” he said.
Butler is somewhat more optimistic. As rack power levels scale from hundreds of kilowatts toward multi-megawatt designs, he expects CBUs to see growing use in managing transient peak demands. Over time, he anticipates workload-driven optimization will determine the mix of batteries and capacitors, with supercapacitors playing an increasingly important role in handling high-cycle, peak-power events.
“I expect capacitor-based energy storage to become a mainstream element of next-generation AI power architectures,” Butler said.

title: Australia’s 850 MW Waratah battery reaches full operations - Energy Storage
content: The more-than AUD 1 billion ($700 million) Waratah super battery built by Akaysha Energy on the site of the former Munmorah coal-fired power station on the New South Wales Central Coast has reached full commercial operations. With a total capacity of 850 MW and storage of 1,680 MWh, the Waratah battery energy storage system (BESS) is set to play a key role in the state’s energy transformation, supporting the growing volume of renewable energy entering the grid and helping to deliver reliable electricity as aging coal-fired power stations retire. NSW Energy Minister Penny Sharpe has confirmed that the battery has now received approval to operate at full capacity from the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO). “The Waratah Super Battery is a game changer for NSW,” she said. “As aging coal-fired power stations retire, this project will help keep the lights on for homes and businesses while enabling more renewable energy to flow through the grid.” The BESS forms the foundation of the Waratah Super Battery Project, that also includes a 700 MW/1,400 MWh system integrity protection scheme (SIPS) control system delivered by transmission company Transgrid. Together, the battery and control system are designed to act like a giant shock absorber for the grid, helping keep the system secure when major transmission lines are disrupted. At maximum output, the facility is capable of powering up to 340,000 NSW households at peak demand. Transgrid CEO Brett Redman said the SIPS control system is the “largest and most innovative” in Australia, capable of detecting network issues in real time and responding in real time, ensuring continuity of power supply for households and businesses. “The delivery of the Waratah Super Battery provides an additional level of safeguard as coal plants retire and critical transmission infrastructure is built to connect more renewable energy into the Sydney, Illawarra and Hunter load centres,” he said. The battery was due to commence full operations in late 2025 but a “catastrophic” failure of one of three giant transformers just days from final testing caused a major delay. Akaysha CEO Nick Carter said the Waratah battery has been a “complex and demanding” project. “This project tested us in many ways, but the team kept going, solved the problems in front of them, and delivered,” he said, adding it is a test testament to the grit, perseverance, and problem-solving capability of the Akaysha team. “We are proud, grateful and humbled to reach this point, and focused now on the important role Waratah will play in supporting a more reliable, secure and renewable NSW electricity system.” From pv magazine Australia The post Australia’s 850 MW Waratah battery reaches full operations appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: California home batteries set VPP dispatch record during heat wave - Energy Storage
content: Some batteries across California discharged at a peak of more than 580 MW on the evening of Sept. 9, which Tesla and Sunrun said it was the largest residential VPP dispatch on record. The California Energy Commission (CEC) called on the batteries as a heat wave pushed up demand and wholesale prices. Tesla Powerwalls accounted for 517 MW, while batteries from other manufacturers added 63 MW. About 110,000 Powerwalls took part, 55% of them owned and operated by Sunrun. Sunrun also dispatched more than 30,000 non-Tesla batteries in its fleet. On the evening of the peak event, the CEC’s Demand Side Grid Support (DSGS) program triggered when the California Independent System Operator’s (CAISO) day-ahead price exceeded $200/MWh. The following evening, Southern California Edison requested its own three-hour dispatch, and the two companies delivered more than 140 MW. Had both calls landed on the same night, Sunrun and Tesla said in a press release, the fleets could have delivered more than 720 MW. During a statewide test on July 29, 2025, greater than 100,000 batteries sustained 539 MW of output for two hours . The Tesla units supplied 459 MW of that. A Brattle Group analysis of that event, commissioned by Sunrun and Tesla, found the program had enrolled 700 MW of battery capacity and could deliver up to $206 million savings by displacing gas peaker output during the highest-priced hours of the year. Residential VPPs are scaling the ConnectedSolutions program to add EVs in Massachusetts. The Clean Peak Program runs in parallel to ConnectedSolutions, and is specifically designed to offset gas peaker plants in the state and region. The announcement lands as two virtual power plant bills await action in Sacramento. SB 913, from Sen. Josh Becker, would direct the California Public Utilities Commission to establish a valuation methodology for customer-sited batteries exporting power during periods of system stress and allow aggregated behind-the-meter resources to count toward resource adequacy. Companion bill SB 905 would create a grid utilization metric to measure how much of the distribution system’s capacity is actually used. Both cleared the Legislature this month. Last October, Newsom vetoed three VPP and load-flexibility bills  citing budget constraints. Newsom’s administration also cut funding for DSGS , the program that triggered the Sept. 9 dispatch. title: EnerVenue lands first megawatt-size order for its non-lithium, aqueous metal cell storage tech - Energy Storage
content: EnerVenue has signed its first multi-megawatt-hour commercial order, covering 11 MWh of non-lithium battery storage for an operating oilfield in northern China. California-headquartered EnerVenue said an unnamed major Chinese oil and gas producer ordered 26 Energy Prism containerized units for one of its existing production sites. The systems will store electricity from an onsite solar array and discharge it when the facility requires power. The first three units are scheduled to ship in December 2026, with the remaining 23 due in March 2027. EnerVenue has not disclosed the project’s power rating, discharge duration, contract value or end user. The Energy Prism systems will be delivered as complete DC-side containerized units ready to connect to the site’s power conversion equipment. They will use EnerVenue’s fourth-generation Aqueous Metal Cell, or AMC, technology. The AMC is based on nickel-hydrogen chemistry, a technology with a long history in spacecraft including the Hubble Space Telescope and International Space Station but re-engineered by EnerVenue for stationary storage using lower-cost materials. The company’s current cell has nominal energy of 3 kWh, a 30,000-cycle design life, 100% depth-of-discharge capability and peak round-trip efficiency above 90%. EnerVenue specifies a 30-year design life and an operating temperature range of -20 C to 60 C without active thermal management. Safety was a central factor in the oilfield project, according to EnerVenue. The cell uses a water-based, non-flammable electrolyte and contains no lithium. The company says its chemistry does not produce the sequence of reactions associated with lithium-ion thermal runaway, while UL 9540A testing showed no fire propagation at cell level. The order marks a step up from EnerVenue’s first fourth-generation AMC deployment, a 150 kWh system commissioned with Towngas in Jintan, Changzhou, in 2025. That installation combines onsite renewable generation with electric-bus charging. pv magazine Germany covered the company’s $300 million in its Series B preferred stock financing in March 2026 . Cells for the new oilfield project will be manufactured at EnerVenue’s newly opened high-volume production line in Changzhou. The first phase is rated at 250 MWh of annual capacity and is designed to reach around 300 cells per day at full automation. EnerVenue plans to increase capacity to 1 GWh in 2027 and to multiple gigawatt-hours by 2028. EnerVenue is positioning the technology around lifetime economics rather than upfront battery cost. In a media roundtable, CEO Henning Rath declined to disclose to ESS News the system’s current capital cost, saying only that its average cost over 30-year operating life is already competitive. The company argues that the economics benefit from avoiding scheduled battery augmentation, active cooling and, where regulations permit, dedicated fire-suppression systems. The Chinese oilfield contract is significant. That is not due to its overall 11 MWh size, but for EnerVenue’s first move from pilot deployment into a multi-MWh commercial installation to further prove its position in the market. Its longer-term competitiveness will depend on whether the promised cycle life, safety characteristics and lifecycle cost advantages are demonstrated on a commercial scale. title: First stage BESS at Mortlake Energy Hub grows to 1,449 MWh as EPC deal signed - Energy Storage
content: While Origin Energy in Australia has just completed a battery energy storage project at the Mortlake Power Station in western Victoria, the Mortlake Energy Hub is separately progressing with the first stage (MEH-1) toward construction with major contracts signed. Yanara, formerly BrightNight Asia Pacific, has signed an A$790 million engineering, procurement and construction contract with Gamuda Engineering for MEH-1. The companies had already worked together during an early contractor involvement phase covering design, procurement and construction planning. It will be Gamuda’s first major project in Victoria, with its parent company based in Malaysia. The first stage pairs 435 MWp of solar with a 1,449 MWh battery. That is an increase from the 1,200 MWh specification Gamuda previously gave for Stage 1. Gamuda’s announcement also describes the battery as 300 MW with a 4.5-hour duration, although those figures do not reconcile with the 1,449 MWh capacity in the contract disclosure. ESS News has contacted Gamuda for clarification. The project will connect to Victoria’s 500 kV network through the Mortlake Terminal Station. Gamuda expects it to be energized in April 2028 and begin operations in the first quarter of 2029. The wider energy hub has been described as a 450 MW solar farm with a 600 MW / 2,400 MWh battery across two stages, and that scope changed in December 2025, with the solar plant upgraded from 350 MW. The latest first-stage duration for the BESS therefore also leaves the eventual capacity split between the stages unclear. The deployed fleet of ultra heavy-duty trucks and mining equipment assets powered by Volvo Autonomous Solutions reached a major milestone last week, hauling their 3

Volvo CE
deployed its first pilot-ready autonomous hauling solutions with customers Boliden Garpenberg in Sweden and Brønnøy Kalk in Norway back 2023, with a milestone of 1 moving million tonnes (~1.1 US tons) of Earth autonomously by 2025.
Sharp readers will note that it is now 2026, and Volvo has blown past the original pilot’s goal, crossing the three million ton mark at Boliden’s Garpenberg mine earlier this summer. Volvo Autonomous Solutions (VAS)

and scale autonomous hauling in real-world environments
Be seen doing good work
FMX truck, excavator with drill arm; via Volvo CE.

title: Omoda & Jaecoo confirm Canada launch in late 2026: here's the EV lineup
content:
Chery Automotive
Fred Lambert
| Sep 28 2026 - 7:51 am PT
Jaecoo E5 (Image: Jaecoo)
Chery’s Omoda and Jaecoo brands have launched a Canadian website confirming that their “premium electric SUVs” will arrive in Canada in late 2026.
The site doesn’t name a single model, price, or dealer yet. But the Chinese automaker’s global lineup gives a pretty clear idea of what Canadians could get, and it’s heavy on plug-in hybrids.
A launch page with no cars on it
Omoda & Jaecoo Canada website
is a teaser at this point. It tells visitors that “the wait is almost over” and that the brands are “coming late 2026,” with a sign-up form for updates.
The retailer locator is empty too. The company says it’s “building a network across Canada” and will announce locations ahead of the launch.
The site does include one telling bit of fine print: vehicles shown are intended for other markets, and some may not be available in Canada. In other words, Chery hasn’t picked its Canadian lineup yet, or at least isn’t saying.
On its “About” page, Omoda & Jaecoo claims it’s now sold in more than 75 countries and has exported over 1.2 million vehicles in about three years. The brand is growing fast in Europe. In the UK alone, it registered 6,238 vehicles in August for a 6.62% market share, according to the company.
Why now: Canada’s Chinese EV quota
This is a direct result of
Canada slashing its 100% tariff on Chinese EVs to 6.1%
back in January. The deal lets in up to 49,000 Chinese-made electrified vehicles per year at the lower rate, rising to 70,000 by 2030. Anything outside the quota still gets hit with the 100% surtax.
And for Chery, the quota covers plug-in hybrids and hybrids, not just battery-electric vehicles. That matters a lot given what Omoda and Jaecoo actually sell.
Chery has been preparing for a while. As
we reported in May
, it filed Canadian trademarks for Omoda, Jaecoo, and several other sub-brands, and Jaecoo E5 prototypes were spotted in Ontario on manufacturer plates.
It won’t be alone.
BYD plans to open 20 Canadian dealerships
in its first year, also targeting a late 2026 start. And Tesla is already using the quota to sell a Shanghai-built
Model 3 at a record-low C$39,490
Omoda & Jaecoo’s current electrified lineup
We don’t know which of these will make it to Canada. Here’s what the brands currently offer in markets like the UK, Australia, and Indonesia, based on their official spec sheets.
Jaecoo E5 (J5 EV)
Jaecoo E5 (Image: Jaecoo)
The Jaecoo E5 is the most likely candidate to lead a Canadian launch, since it’s the one Chery was caught testing in Ontario. It’s a compact electric SUV with a 60.9 kWh battery, a 155 kW front motor, and 248 miles (399 km) of WLTP range. It does 0-100 km/h in 7.7 seconds.
It’s also cheap. The E5 starts at £27,505 in the UK and A$36,990 driveaway in Australia.
The catch is charging. Jaecoo UK lists an 80 kW DC peak, with 30-80% taking 27 minutes. That’s slow by 2026 standards.
Omoda E5
Omoda E5 (Image: Omoda)
The Omoda E5 is the sportier sibling on the same basic hardware: a 61 kWh battery, 155 kW motor, and 267 miles (430 km) of WLTP range. It charges from 30-80% in 28 minutes and starts at £33,065 in the UK.
Omoda 4 (O4 EV)
Omoda 4 (Image: Omoda)
The newest EV in the family launched in Indonesia in July. The Omoda 4 gets a bigger 65.05 kWh LFP pack, a 160 kW motor, 553 km of range on the optimistic NEDC cycle, and a 119 kW DC peak with 20-80% in 22 minutes. Pricing hasn’t been published yet.
Jaecoo 7 SHS-P
Jaecoo 7 SHS-P (Image: Jaecoo)
This is the brand’s volume seller and it’s a plug-in hybrid. The Jaecoo 7 SHS-P pairs a 1.5-liter turbo engine with an 18.3 kWh battery for 56 miles (90 km) of WLTP electric range. Power is 150 kW (204 PS), and it starts at £35,170 in the UK. Australia now also gets an AWD version with a second, rear motor.
Jaecoo 8 SHS-P
Jaecoo 8 SHS-P (Image: Jaecoo)
The Jaecoo 8 is a three-row, six- or seven-seat PHEV with three motors and AWD. It has a 34.46 kWh battery for 83 miles (134 km) of WLTP electric range, 315 kW (428 PS), and a 0-100 km/h time of 5.8 seconds. It starts at £45,500 in the UK.
Omoda 9 SHS-P
Omoda 9 SHS-P (Image: Omoda)
The Omoda 9 is the brand’s flagship. It uses the same 34.46 kWh battery as the Jaecoo 8, rated at 90 miles (145 km) of WLTP electric range, with 449 PS and 700 Nm from an AWD setup. It does 0-100 km/h in 4.9 seconds and starts at £44,995 in the UK.
Omoda 7 SHS-P
Omoda 7 SHS-P (Image: Omoda)
The Omoda 7 is a newer mid-size PHEV with 150 kW (204 PS), 56 miles (90 km) of electric range, and a UK starting price of £32,005.

title: Tesla warns weather could delay Roadster demo, and the forecast is ugly
content:
Tesla Roadster
Fred Lambert
| Sep 28 2026 - 6:50 am PT
Update 9/28:
Tesla has since confirmed that it’s rescheduling the Roadster event to October 15, citing “severe conditions predicted.”
We have more on the two-week delay here
Tesla is warning guests invited to its October 1 Roadster event that the long-delayed demo could get pushed back again, and this time it’s the weather.
In an email to invitees, Tesla says the event “must be held outdoors” and may need to be rescheduled. And the forecast for central Texas on Thursday calls for an 82% chance of rain, with thunderstorms.
Tesla’s email to Roadster event guests
The email, titled “Important: Roadster Event Weather,” was shared by one of the invitees. Tesla tells the guest it’s “looking forward to hosting you” on October 1, 2026, then adds that “there is a possibility we may need to reschedule due to weather.”
According to Tesla, the event “features a unique experience that must be held outdoors,” and the company is “continuing to monitor weather reports.” There’s no backup date in the email, only a promise to “reach out with additional details as soon as possible.”
teased the October 1 reveal earlier this month
with a “Go for launch” image. As we
reported in August
, the centerpiece is a hover demonstration using a SpaceX-developed cold gas thruster package, code-named A71, at SpaceX’s rocket test site in McGregor, Texas, just outside Waco. The car is expected to run remotely with nobody inside, and spectators are to be kept several hundred yards back because the thrusters are loud enough to damage eardrums.
So “outdoors” isn’t a stylistic choice. You don’t fire thrusters in a tent.
The forecast for McGregor
Open-Meteo forecast data for McGregor, pulled Monday morning, shows an 82% chance of precipitation on Thursday, October 1, with thunderstorms in the forecast and wind gusts up to 32 mph.
Friday isn’t much better on rain at 75%, but the wind drops to gusts around 13 mph. By Saturday, the chance of rain falls to 42%.
Forecasts three days out can still move. But thunderstorms and 30+ mph gusts are about the last conditions you’d pick for making a car hover on cold gas thrusters in front of a crowd.
Nine years of Roadster delays
Tesla unveiled the next-gen Roadster prototype in November 2017 and promised production in 2020. The timeline has slipped at least eight times since.
The demo alone has moved repeatedly. Musk
said last October
a “flying” demo was coming by the end of 2025. A week later,
Tesla pushed it to April 1, 2026, and production to 2027 or 2028
. April became “maybe in a month or so” on the Q1 earnings call, then
, then October 1.
Reservation holders put down $50,000 for a standard Roadster and $250,000 for the Founders Series. Nearly nine years later, nobody has a car.
Electrek’s Take
While this would be delay number 12 after 9 years, at least this one isn’t on Musk. Tesla can’t control thunderstorms in Texas, and if the forecast holds, postponing a remote-controlled hover stunt with a crowd nearby is the responsible call.
But it tells you a lot about the Roadster program that the biggest risk to its launch event is wind and rain. A car you can actually buy and drive doesn’t need clear skies to be shown off. A stunt with SpaceX hardware does.
If Tesla does have to push it, we expect days, not months. The real question is what shows up when it finally happens: a production-intent car with final specs, a price, and a delivery date, or another flashy video that resets the clock?

title: Volkswagen's best-seller is going electric in 2027 to replace the ID.4 and ID.5 [Images]
content:
Volkswagen is taking its best-seller electric. The ID. Tiguan will replace the ID.4 and ID.5 as part of Volkswagen’s revamped lineup in 2027.
When is Volkswagen launching the ID. Tiguan?
With more than 950,000 models sold since they went on sale in 2021, the ID.4 and ID.5 have been among Volkswagen’s best-selling electric vehicles.
As part of Volkswagen’s revamped lineup, the ID.4 and ID.5 are next in line for an overhaul that brings more than just a new name.
Following the ID. Polo and ID. Cross, the ID. Tiguan will go on sale in 2027 as a “True Volkswagen,” bringing a new look, updated tech, and a refined interior.
“The all-electric model builds on the strengths of the bestseller and offers premium design, generous space, intuitive operation, and innovative technologies,” Volkswagen Brand CEO Thomas Shafer said.
In the past year, Volkswagen delivered over 1 million Tiguan and Tayron models globally. Both are available in petrol, diesel, and plug-in hybrid (PHEV), so adding an all-electric option makes sense.
The ID. Tiguan will go on sale in early 2027, starting in Europe, replacing the ID.4 and ID.5 in Volkswagen’s lineup. The US and other global markets will follow shortly after.
Volkswagen released several images of a camouflaged ID. Tiguan prototype, offering a sneak peek at the new look.
Although it’s still covered, the new images confirm the changes we’ve seen in recent spy images. The ID. Tiguan will adopt a boxier, more traditional SUV-like design that’s nearly identical to the gas-powered version.
You can see the prototype has pop-out door handles, replacing the flush style used on the ID.4 and ID.5.
Top comment by Dan B
"The ID. Tiguan will adopt a boxier, more traditional SUV-like design that’s nearly identical to the gas-powered version."
This is exactly what would keep me from going into this vs the ID.4 like I had. Since I don't really like SUV's and hate the looks of most of them, but also since getting a sedan EV that fits into my budget is not really possible at this time, I have migrated to the ID.4 (2024) and now my 2026 Equinox EV. Both these vehicles look more wagon like than SUV, so that's good on my part. But this new ID.Tiguan is going all in on the SUV craze, and that turns me off. So for now I will continue with my Equinox wagon looking SUV until such time that I can buy a proper sedan EV. And since I recently picked up a clean 2017 Ford Focus EV sedan/hatch, I've been driving that more than my Equinox and will probably continue to until my daughter gets her DL. I purchased this Focus EV for her after all, but I love driving it. haha.
Volkswagen didn’t reveal any interior images, but the ID. Tiguan is expected to feature Volkswagen’s new interior design. Like the ID. Polo and ID. Cross (shown below), it will likely include VW’s new infotainment system, including the return of physical buttons.
We will have to wait until closer to launch for specifics, but with VW’s recent battery and drivetrain updates, the ID. Tiguan is expected to offer improved range, faster charging, and better cold-weather performance.
The current ID.4 uses an 82 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 291 miles in the RWD version. The AWD model offers around 263 miles. Under WLTP conditions, the 2026 VW ID.4 has a range of up to 351 miles (566 km).
Volkswagen said the ID. Tiguan will make its official debut in “early October,” but didn’t reveal a specific date. We should learn more soon. Check back for the latest.

集邦光储观察获悉，9月24日，亿纬锂能公告称，公司拟将持有的湖北恩捷新材料科技有限公司（以下简称“湖北恩捷”）45%股权，以11.5亿元的价格转让给上海恩捷新材料科技有限公司（以下简称“上海恩捷”）。
需要注意的是，此次受让方为上海恩捷，而非其母公司恩捷股份。资料显示，恩捷股份是上海恩捷的母公司，湖北恩捷则是上海恩捷与亿纬锂能此前共同设立的合资公司。交易完成后，上海恩捷将持有湖北恩捷100%股权，亿纬锂能退出湖北恩捷。
公告显示，本次交易不构成关联交易，也不属于重大资产重组，仅需经亿纬锂能董事会审议，无需提交股东大会审议。交易价款采取分期付款方式，具体交割日以湖北恩捷完成本次股权转让工商变更登记为准。
此次股权转让价格以资产评估机构出具的评估结果为参考，经交易各方协商确定。
湖北恩捷成立于2021年12月29日，注册资本16亿元，注册地址位于湖北荆门。公司成立之初由上海恩捷和亿纬锂能共同投资，规划建设16条锂电池隔膜生产线。在此次交易前，上海恩捷持有湖北恩捷55%股权，亿纬锂能持有45%股权。
从经营情况来看，湖北恩捷2026年上半年实现营业收入10.4亿元，净利润2.26亿元；2025年度公司净利润为-476.98万元。对比来看，湖北恩捷今年上半年已实现扭亏。
截至2026年6月30日，湖北恩捷资产总额约47.55亿元。对于此次出售股权，亿纬锂能表示，主要是为了优化资产结构，集中资源发展主营业务，同时回收投资资金并实现部分投资收益。
亿纬锂能同时指出，本次交易完成后，公司合并报表范围不会发生变化，对财务状况不存在重大不利影响。此次交易涉及的主要是湖北恩捷股权结构调整，公告未披露交易完成后双方隔膜产品采购等合作安排是否会发生变化。
交易完成后，湖北恩捷将结束与亿纬锂能的合资状态，转为上海恩捷旗下全资子公司。

title: 奔驰取得辉能Gen4固态电池优先使用权，合作迈向量产验证
content:
9月24日，辉能科技（ProLogium）与梅赛德斯-奔驰签署联合测试协议。根据协议，奔驰将获得辉能科技最新的第四代超流化全无机固态电池（Gen4锂陶瓷电池）的优先测试权，并对相关电芯开展电气、热性能及安全性测试，以评估其未来应用于车辆的可行性。
据辉能介绍，Gen4电池采用全无机超流态电解质体系，并结合不可燃无机电解质、陶瓷隔膜及主动安全机制，目标是在安全性、能量密度、倍率性能、低温性能及快充等方面实现平衡，同时兼顾规模化制造和成本。
此次测试是奔驰与辉能近十年合作的延续。双方自2016年起开展固态电池技术合作，合作内容已从早期的电芯开发与验证，逐步拓展至不同锂陶瓷电池形态及技术路线。此前，双方已验证软包电芯、下一代方形电芯以及Bi-Polar技术等。
在量产方面，辉能表示，其位于中国台湾的桃园厂已完成GWh级制造验证，可支持C样品生产及示范车辆项目。2026年9月，辉能还宣布Gen 3.5锂陶瓷电池进入量产，其185.4Ah大尺寸电芯经TÜV测试，能量密度达到381Wh/kg、903Wh/L。
海外产能方面，辉能位于法国敦刻尔克的电池工厂一期已于2026年2月动工，一期规划年产能4GWh，并计划逐步提升产能；整个项目远期设计产能最高可达44GWh。辉能表示，该工厂将复制中国台湾桃园厂的制造模式，为欧洲客户提供本地化电池供应。
值得注意的是，辉能在今年5月与Translational Development Acquisition Corp.（TDAC）达成业务合并协议，并已向美国证券交易委员会提交F-4注册声明。按照目前交易安排，在完成相关交易及监管、上市条件后，辉能计划于纳斯达克上市，拟用股票代码为“PRLG”。

title: 通威股份收购丽豪清能获批
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月24日，国家市场监督管理总局发布公告，依法无条件批准通威股份收购青海丽豪清能股份有限公司股权经营者集中案。
据公开资料显示，本次交易最早由通威股份于2026年2月24日披露，通威拟通过发行股份及支付现金方式，收购丽豪清能100%股权，并同步募集配套资金。
从业务范围来看，丽豪清能主营业务为太阳能级多晶硅生产，配套建设电子级多晶硅项目。通威股份业务覆盖工业硅、多晶硅、硅片、电池片、光伏组件等光伏全产业链环节。
市场监管总局在审查公告中说明，审查阶段调研了光伏产业链，听取行业协会及上下游企业意见。审查认定，虽然交易完成后双方在国内及全球太阳能级多晶硅市场合计份额较高，但当前太阳能级多晶硅市场产能充足、市场竞争者较多，集中后实体仍面临有效竞争约束，交易不会对相关市场产生排除、限制竞争效果，因此作出无条件批准的决定。
根据通威此前发布的公告，本次交易审计、评估等基础工作已初步完成。受预案披露后行业环境变化影响，交易各方仍在协商交易方案条款，公司无法在原定时限内发出股东大会通知。交易各方将继续推进收购，待方案协商一致后，重新召开董事会审议方案，并按监管要求履行后续审批与信息披露。
反垄断审查通过仅为本次重组前置审批事项之一，交割还需完成上市公司内部决策、证监会相关审核、资产过户等流程，交易最终落地仍存在不确定性。

title: 阳光电源、鹏辉能源等企业成立7家新能源公司
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，华能、宁德时代、鹏辉能源、易储数智、深圳能源、三峡集团、阳光电源等企业相继成立新能源相关公司，业务覆盖光伏、风电、储能及水电等领域。
华能联合宁德时代成立西藏新公司
9月21日，华能澜沧江古学（芒康）水电有限公司在西藏自治区昌都市芒康县完成工商注册，公司注册资本56亿元，法定代表人为郭建文。
股权穿透显示，该公司由宁德时代、华能水电全资子公司华能澜沧江上游水电有限公司共同持股。其中华能澜沧江上游水电有限公司认缴出资额49.84亿元，持股比例89%；宁德时代认缴出资额6.16亿元，持股比例11%。
工商登记的经营范围具体条目为：水力发电；太阳能发电技术服务；风力发电技术服务；储能技术服务；电动汽车充电基础设施运营等。
鹏辉能源成立能源科技公司
9月21日，广州智坤辉能能源科技有限公司正式成立，注册资本为200万元，法定代表人为焦健。
公司经营范围为新兴能源技术研发；太阳能发电技术服务；机械电气设备销售；新能源原动设备销售；集中式快速充电站；光伏发电设备租赁；光伏设备及元器件销售；储能技术服务等方面。
企查查股权穿透显示，该公司由鹏辉能源旗下广州鹏辉智慧能源技术有限公司和华建坤能（上海）能源科技有限公司共同持股，双方持股比例分别为70%、30%。
易储数智再成立两家能源科技公司
9月21日，深圳易储数智能源集团有限公司成立两家新公司，深圳通源新盛能源科技有限公司与深圳明汇能源科技有限公司。
两个公司的注册资本均为500万元，法定代表人为石磊，注册地址位于深圳市南山区粤海街道。
两个新公司经营范围均包括：新兴能源技术研发；光伏设备及元器件制造；风力发电技术服务；储能技术服务；电池销售等方面。
深圳能源成立新能源公司
9月18日，深能（北京）新能源合伙企业（有限合伙）成立，注册地位于北京丰台，注册资本为22.14亿。
公司经营范围包含发电业务、输电业务、供（配）电业务；太阳能发电技术服务；风力发电技术服务；储能技术服务；发电技术服务等。
合伙人包括天津市旭星新能源科技发展有限公司、深能北方能源控股有限公司、深能（天津）能源科技有限公司，均为深圳能源集团全资子公司。
三峡集团青海成立新公司
9月16日，三峡集团青海能源投资有限公司正式成立，位于青海省西宁市城西区，注册资本10亿元，法定代表人为王清伟。
从股权结构看，中国三峡新能源（集团）股份有限公司认缴出资3.4亿元，持股占比34%。中国长江电力股份有限公司、长江三峡投资管理有限公司分别认缴出资3.3亿元，持股占比分别为33%。
公司经营范围包括，风力发电技术服务；太阳能发电技术服务；储能技术服务；新兴能源技术研发；资源再生利用技术研发；再生资源加工销售等。

title: 25,000-hour SOEC stack durability results published | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
The 70-cell SolydEra stack operated with continuous hydrogen production for almost three years using DynElectro’s patented AC:DC operation. The test was conducted at 750°C and −0.5 A/cm².
After an initial conditioning period, stack performance stabilized. Over the remaining 22,000 hours, stack voltage rose by 0.05% per 1,000 hours, compared with the EU’s 2030 target of 0.5% per 1,000 hours for solid oxide electrolysis. The average across the full 25,000 hours, including conditioning and periods of conventional DC operation, was 0.23% per 1,000 hours.
During conventional DC operation, degradation reached about 11.5% per 1,000 hours. With AC:DC operation, it fell to under 1% during run-in before stabilizing at 0.05% per 1,000 hours during long-term operation. The AC:DC principle periodically reverses stack polarity from electrolysis to fuel cell mode.
The authors said that, to their knowledge, the test represents the longest SOEC operation and lowest degradation reported for a full stack. They cited a previous full-stack record of about 9,500 hours.
DTU Energy carried out impedance analysis and post-mortem microstructural characterization. Its analysis found that nickel migration, loss of electrical contact in the nickel network, silica contamination, and cracking at the electrode interface had not developed to a measurable extent. All eight monitored cell groups behaved uniformly throughout the test.
Søren Højgaard Jensen, Founder and CTO of DynElectro and professor at Aalborg University, said: “This result shows that durability is not only a question of materials but of how the stack is operated. With AC:DC operation, we can make existing, industrial SOEC stacks last long enough for hydrogen from solid oxide electrolysis to become competitive. For DynElectro, the publication is an important milestone on the way to commercialising our Dynamic Electrolyser Units,”
DynElectro has integrated the AC:DC technology into its Dynamic Electrolyser Units used in pilot and commercial projects in Europe. The company said it will soon add a 1 MW unit in the Netherlands.

title: A Diesel Plug-In Hybrid Pickup Truck? This Company Thinks It Can Make It Work
content:
A Diesel Plug-In Hybrid Pickup Truck? This Company Thinks It Can Make It Work
The Chery Stockman has two tanks, a high-voltage battery, four-wheel drive, and plenty of towing capacity.
- A plug-in hybrid vehicle is already plenty complicated with a gas engine.
- Using a diesel engine would complicate things even more, but Chery thinks it can crack the code.
- The Chery Stockman is the world’s first diesel plug-in hybrid pickup truck, and it promises ultra-low fuel consumption, 62 miles of electric range, and good towing capacity.
A little over a decade ago, Volvo had the bright idea to make a diesel plug-in hybrid. On paper, everything looked great: the low fuel consumption of a diesel paired with the benefits of all-electric cruising around town. In practice, though, running a diesel engine for short bursts doesn’t do it any good, so Volvo scrapped the oil-burning PHEV after a few short years to focus on gas alternatives.
Now, though, Volvo’s idea from the early 2010s is making a comeback in the form of the world’s first diesel plug-in hybrid pickup truck. It’s a solution that, in theory, could help boost the electrification rate of America’s gas-guzzling pickup truck market. Mercedes-Benz is doing diesel PHEVs in Europe, so clearly there’s still some life left in this solution.
As is the case with a lot of news about electrified cars nowadays, this one comes from China, but it’s not for China. The Chery Stockman, the mid-size pickup that earns the “first of its kind” badge, was developed specifically for the Australian market, where some road trips seem like they would never end, towing is a big part of daily driving, and low fuel consumption is increasingly important due to rising prices at the pump.
It’s a highly competitive market where 20% of all new car sales are pickups, so the stakes are very high, but the Chinese automaker reckons it has a chance. And to its credit, the spec sheet looks very promising.
The Stockman has a proper four-wheel drive system with a solid rear axle, three locking differentials, a low-range transfer box, and a maximum towing capacity of 7,716 pounds (3,500 kilograms). That’s on par with some of the best competitors, but where the Stockman ups the ante is in the fuel consumption department.
Powered by a 2.5-liter turbo-diesel lump and an electric motor of some sort, Chery’s PHEV pickup promises an outstanding efficiency of 117.6 mpg (2 l/100 km), a combined system output of 469 horsepower, and 590 pound-feet (800 Newton-meters) of torque. Of course, there’s an asterisk in there, and that’s because the fantastic fuel efficiency only happens if the 34-kilowatt-hour battery is fully charged, in which case the Stockman can drive up to 62 miles (100 kilometers) on electricity alone, on the NEDC cycle.
That’s roughly 45 miles (73 km) on the EPA cycle, which isn’t great, but even with the advertised NEDC figure, things aren’t looking great, with a calculated average efficiency of 1.82 miles/kilowatt-hour (34 kWh/100 km).
Chery didn’t reveal how the electric motor is integrated into the powertrain, but considering the traditional 4WD layout, it’s likely that the e-motor is sandwiched between the diesel engine and automatic transmission, resulting in rather high transmission losses.
On the comfort front, Chery is offering heated and ventilated front seats, leather upholstery, a dual-zone climate control system, a premium sound system, two large screens, and a generously sized color head-up display. Vehicle-to-load (V2L) is also part of the pack, with a pair of household sockets in the bed offering energy straight from the high-voltage pack.
The Stockman is expected to debut in Australia soon, where it will go up against household names like the Toyota Hilux, Ford Ranger, and Mitsubishi Triton (L200 in other markets). That’s the same crowd where the BYD Shark 6, a Chinese gas plug-in hybrid, is trying to make a name for itself.
It’s a solid proposition, but in the end it comes down to the price and the potential reliability issues of such a complicated setup. Like any modern diesel truck, it uses diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) to keep emissions low, but that whole system comes with pumps and lines that can get clogged over time, especially if the engine doesn’t start up for weeks on end.

title: BYD’s $10,000 EV Is Getting A Huge Upgrade, With 5-Minute Charging
content:
BYD’s $10,000 EV Is Getting A Huge Upgrade, With 5-Minute Charging
The second-generation BYD Seagull, also known as the Dolphin Surf, flips the script in the specs department.
- One of China’s best-selling EVs is getting a makeover.
- The new BYD Seagull (Dolphin Surf in Europe) is larger, more powerful, and now features a front trunk.
- The original Seagull is currently priced from roughly $10,000.
Everybody knows that China’s EV landscape is vastly different from what we get in the United States, and the main difference is just how cheap cars can get over there. One such example is the BYD Seagull, which now retails for the equivalent of roughly $10,000.
Thanks to its low price and more than decent equipment, the Seagull, sold as the Dolphin Surf in Europe, was once China’s best-selling car, and now there’s a brand-new one that promises to offer more of everything.
The second-generation BYD Seagull is still properly small, measuring 165.5 inches (4,205 millimeters) long, 71.2 in wide (1,810 mm), and 61.8 in (1,570 mm) tall, but the new body is 16.7 in (425 mm) longer than the outgoing model, while the wheelbase has been increased by 5.9 in (150 mm), for a total of 104.3 in (2,650 mm)
All of this should make for a roomier interior, an area where the old Seagull struggled to offer enough room for four adults.
Besides giving the second-generation EV a larger body, BYD also flipped the way the Seagull is powered. While the old model had a front-mounted 73-horsepower electric motor, the new Seagull gets a 127 hp lump at the rear, making it rear-wheel drive. It’s a big leap in terms of power, and it also means that the new Seagull gets a front trunk that seems quite generously sized, whereas the outgoing EV didn’t get a frunk at all.
Wider, 205-millimeter tires mounted on 16-inch wheels make for a wider stance, while the updated suspension with an independent multi-link setup at the rear should make for a more engaging drive. As a reminder, the first-gen Seagull had a torsion beam at the rear, which is one of the cheapest suspension arrangements, though switching to rear-wheel drive likely forced BYD to go with an independent setup on the new EV.
The new Seagull gets power from an 800-volt lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery that features BYD’s Flash Charging capabilities. There’s a 30-kilowatt-hour pack and a 39.2-kilowatt-hour option, with BYD claiming that a top-up to 70% can be made in as little as five minutes, while a 97% charge can be done in nine minutes. The base battery enables a CLTC-rated range of 199 miles (320 kilometers), while the longer-range model is good for 260 miles (420 km). On the EPA cycle, that would translate to roughly 140 miles and 183 miles, respectively.
On the technology side, the new EV will be available with a lidar-based advanced driver assistance system. Inside, there’s now room for five people instead of four, and a huge central touchscreen acts as the infotainment system’s interface.
Pricing is anyone’s guess, though it’s clear that the new Seagull will try its best to attract as many buyers as it can in the sub-$15,000 segment in China, where its recent performance has been lukewarm at best. It’s also unclear if the new Seagull will make its way to Europe, where BYD currently sells a modified version of the China-spec model to comply with safety regulations.

title: The Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Is Coming To Replace The ID.4
content:
The Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Is Coming To Replace The ID.4
The updated electric crossover is expected to keep its predecessor’s bones while adding more buttons and better tech.
- The Volkswagen ID.4 is officially being replaced by a new electric crossover.
- The German brand is going with a name that’s known across the world.
- The updated ID. Tiguan is also coming to the U.S., where the ID.4 has recently been discontinued.
The Volkswagen ID.4 is dead. Long live the new Volkswagen ID. Tiguan. Just six years after its introduction, the German automaker is retiring the compact electric crossover’s name, but its replacement is nearly finished and ready to right all of the ID.4’s wrongs.
The new Volkswagen ID. Tiguan will be revealed early next month, with the first European deliveries set for early next year. And yes, the ID.4’s successor is coming to the United States, though we don’t have a date for its debut here yet.
2027 Volkswagen ID. Tiguan camouflaged prototype
“The ID. Tiguan is planned to succeed the ID.4 in the North American market,” a company representative said. “Following its European launch in early 2027, Volkswagen will share North American timing and additional market-specific details in due course.”
As a reminder, Volkswagen’s factory in Chattanooga stopped assembling U.S.-spec ID.4s in April to make room for more gas-powered SUVs, leaving potential customers with whatever is left in dealers’ inventories. To sweeten the deal, VW is offering discounts of up to $12,500 for a new ID.4, transforming the perfectly average crossover into a fantastic deal.
But the ID. Tiguan isn’t just a new name—it’s Volkswagen’s chance to make its Tesla Model Y fighter a force to be reckoned with. The original ID.4 was riddled with software issues, and parts of the interior felt like an exercise in cost-cutting. To VW’s credit, the software problems were ultimately ironed out, but the lack of physical controls was never fixed. An electronic door latch recall that prompted a stop sale also dented the car's reputation.
2027 Volkswagen ID. Tiguan camouflaged prototype
Here’s where the updated electric Tiguan comes into play. Despite using the same underpinnings as the ID.4, the new EV is set to receive the same interior treatment as the ID.3 Neo and ID. Polo. In other words, proper buttons for all four electric windows, volume control, and the climate system. VW’s latest Android Automotive OS-based infotainment system is also expected to make an appearance, enabling owners to download and install native apps for audio streaming.
The exterior also gets a comprehensive overhaul, with a new light signature akin to that of VW’s latest electric offerings. Plus, the Tiguan name should help with sales—that’s what the company hopes, at least.
There’s no word on what powers the ID. Tiguan yet, but if Volkswagen follows the same route as with the ID.3 Neo, we can expect slightly larger battery packs, faster charging, and more powerful electric motors. For context, the outgoing ID.4 can be had with a single rear motor that makes 282 horsepower or with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup with 335 hp. Battery-wise, the 2026 model only came with a 77-kilowatt-hour (usable) pack that enables 291 miles of range on the RWD version and 263 miles on the AWD variant. Older ID.4s could also be had with a 58-kWh pack.

title: Manus：正组建团队开发面向国内市场的产品，与国产模型厂商合作稳步进行中
content:
IT之家 9 月 28 日消息，北京蝴蝶效应科技有限公司公众号今日发文，宣布面向海外用户发布 Manus 2.0 版本，并推出面向个人生活场景的智能助理 Cue。
Manus 表示，公司正在组建团队开发面向国内市场的产品，与国产模型厂商及生态伙伴的合作也在稳步进行，后续将分享更多进展。
IT之家注：Cue 被定位为面向个人生活场景的智能助理，Manus 2.0 面向海外用户发布，国内版本仍在筹备中。
Manus 2.0 已在网页端、桌面端和移动端上线，Cue 同步上线，iOS 版本将在通过 App Store 审核后推出。
据介绍，Manus 2.0 采用自研 Agent 框架 Cascade。官方称，该框架让项目保持轻量，仅在需要时引入专业能力。在一项测试配置中，Cascade 的 Token 消耗减少 23.2%，任务完成时间缩短 28.2%，运行成本降低 32%。
云电脑功能允许用户购买专属运行环境，用于多人游戏服务器或长期运行的自动化流程。项目可在用户合上笔记本后继续在线运行。
自动化能力从定时任务扩展至事件触发。新邮件、广告数据波动、日历事件、Slack 消息、Notion 更新等，均可触发 Manus 执行预设工作流。
桌面应用升级为 Manus Studio，定位为人与 AI 共享的工作空间。Studio 按项目需要引入能力，本次升级覆盖文档、表格、PDF、幻灯片、网站、代码、游戏和视频。
视频编辑器可生成初剪版本，并将时间线交给用户。片段、图片、文字、动态图形和音频以独立素材呈现，用户可替换配乐、素材和动画，也可交还 Manus 继续修改。
该编辑器面向 30 至 60 秒短篇产品广告、AI UGC、数据动态图表、教程、Vlog 及动效视频。Alchemy 模式由 Manus 接手创意指导，调用视频生成与代码生成能力。
游戏开发环境调用视频、图像和编程模型。Max Ultra 模式下，官方称游戏画面、玩法和手感有所提升。用户可从模板起步，在编辑面板中管理素材、修改代码和调整场景。
游戏完成后可发布为网站，也可配置多人联机。用户选择云电脑并购买后，Manus 负责托管、网络和运维。竞速、对战、竞技和 3D 游戏均支持多人联机。
远程控制与 Computer Use 功能允许用户通过 Manus 操作远程电脑。在已授权会话中，Manus 在独立可见的工作区操作，仅使用用户批准的文件、浏览器和应用。
Cue 是一款独立应用，支持手机和桌面，与 Manus 基于同一套基础设施构建。每个 Agent 拥有自己的邮箱、电话号码、钱包和电脑，可发消息、在预算内付款并完成任务。
多个 Agent 可加入同一群聊，围绕共同目标互相接力，分别负责调研、整理名单和起草文稿。Cue 还可对接日常服务，例如在餐厅扫码后由 Agent 点餐或排队取号。
Cue 目前处于抢先体验阶段，凭邀请码免费使用。官方提供邀请码 MEETCUE（限前 1000 位用户）。获得体验资格的用户还将收到可分享给他人的邀请码。

title: 央视起底手机弹窗广告乱象：“快应用”被滥用，违法成本远低于收益
content:
感谢IT之家网友
软媒用户908747
9 月 28 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，深圳一名女士因邻居家起火报警，接警员发短信要求上传现场视频，点击后却弹出手机浏览器开屏广告，误触跳转耽误约一分钟。消防部门称，短信链接本身无广告，弹窗来自手机浏览器。
类似情况并非个例。大量网友反映老人手机通话、拍照等功能遭弹窗霸屏。安徽黄山一老人拍摄鱼灯表演，半分钟内弹窗跳转近 20 次。广西一网友家人使用微信时，不停弹出伪装成“女儿来电”的广告视频，且无法关闭。
央视援引专家的话表示，弹窗广告常与“快应用”技术有关。快应用原为系统内置的免安装应用形态，被滥用后可在后台生成悬浮窗，覆盖在其他应用上方。
IT之家注：快应用是系统内置的无需下载安装即可使用的应用形态，现被部分开发者滥用于推送弹窗广告。
弹窗设计暗藏陷阱。关闭键常被放置在屏幕左上角或右上角不易点击区域，或做成浅灰色小字，尺寸小于设计标准。部分弹窗设置虚假关闭键，用户稍有误碰即跳转。
法规方面，广告法、互联网广告管理办法要求弹窗广告显著标明关闭标志，确保一键关闭。工信部 2021 年发布的适老化规范明确禁止适老模式出现广告弹窗，并对关闭按钮位置大小作出限制。
弹窗广告背后是完整流量变现链条，涉及广告主、广告平台和 App 开发者。据奇安信安全专家陈锦添介绍，千次展示约 30 元，每次点击约 2.5 元。日活 100 万的应用每天触发三次弹窗，月收益可达 150 万元以上。
违规处罚方面，违反广告管理办法的罚款一般为 5000 元以上、3 万元以下。专家指出，违法成本远低于收益，是弹窗广告屡禁不止的主要原因。
监管面临技术挑战。开发者在上架前不触发弹窗，通过后台跟踪用户机型、区域，在特定时间地点突然触发，导致监控方难以取证和复现。
中国政法大学教授郭旨龙建议，对以弹窗广告为主要营业目标的主体，可设定罚款为违法所得或经营数额的 1 至 2 倍，并给予用户及时投诉举报渠道。今年 6 月，工信部已发文指导规范 App 信息窗口跳转行为。
专家提醒，若急需拨打求救电话却遭遇弹窗广告，大部分手机可快速连按侧边键 5 次，启动应急模式进行紧急呼叫。

title: 消息称《GTA6》发售后 R 星将转战开发《黑色洛城 2》 ：瞄准 2030 年发售，以旧金山为背景
content:
9 月 28 日消息，4chan 匿名用户爆料称，Rockstar Games 将在《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）发售之后开发《黑色洛城》续作《黑色洛城 2》，并以 2030 年发售为目标。这一消息随后被 GTAForums 用户 Shahanshah 转发并引起激烈讨论。
爆料内容显示，《黑色洛城 2》将把故事背景从原作的洛杉矶转移至旧金山，并围绕美国历史上著名的“十二宫杀手”案件展开。爆料还称，Rockstar 计划进一步改进 MotionScan 面部捕捉技术。
该匿名爆料者此前曾准确披露《GTA 6》的部分开发信息，包括角色关系、犯罪侧写系统等内容，但这些说法并不足以证明此次《黑色洛城 2》消息属实，还请大家谨慎看待。
目前能够确认的是，Take-Two 首席执行官 Strauss Zelnick 在 2026 年 4 月谈及《黑色洛城》时曾表示，公司未来会继续考虑旗下所有 IP 的新项目，但当时没有公布任何具体作品。
另一个值得关注的背景是，Rockstar Games 于 2025 年 3 月正式收购了澳大利亚开发商 Video Games Deluxe，并将其更名为 Rockstar Australia。该工作室此前曾参与《黑色洛城》2017 年重制版、《黑色洛城：VR 档案》等项目，其创始人 Brendan McNamara 此前还创办了原《黑色洛城》开发商 Team Bondi。
因此，Rockstar 目前确实拥有一支与《黑色洛城》有直接开发经历的团队。不过，Rockstar 官方并未表示 Rockstar Australia 正在开发《黑色洛城 2》，也没有确认游戏名称、故事背景或发售时间。
IT之家注：原版《黑色洛城》由 Team Bondi 开发、Rockstar Games 发行，于 2011 年推出。Team Bondi 随后停止运营，其后续人员和项目经历了多次重组，而 Video Games Deluxe 则长期与 Rockstar 合作。

title: 美国 FBI 确认遭黑客袭击：员工姓名、住址及社安号码等信息被泄露
content:
IT之家 9 月 28 日消息，据 MS NOW，美国联邦调查局（FBI）已向员工通报一起“网络安全事件”，确认其求职网站 FBIJobs.gov 遭入侵，包括员工的社会安全号码、住址、职位等信息都已被泄露。
当地时间 9 月 22 日，黑客组织 ShinyHunters 声称窃取了大量 FBI 员工及求职者数据。
FBI 于当地时间 2026 年 9 月 23 日公开表示，已注意到 ShinyHunters 声称入侵 FBIJobs.gov 并影响 FBI 员工个人身份信息（PII）的说法。当时 FBI 表示，尚无法确定攻击入口究竟位于第三方服务还是 FBI 自有系统，并正在与相关第三方供应商合作调查和降低风险。
多家媒体进一步报道称，被盗数据还涉及部分医疗信息，包括血液、尿液样本记录以及精神科相关报告。
ShinyHunters 此前宣称从 FBIJobs.gov 获取了大量数据，并声称掌握“几乎所有 FBI 特工”的相关信息。该组织还表示，数据涉及现任、离职员工以及求职者，并包含人力资源、刑事司法和医疗相关系统的信息。
ShinyHunters 此前还向媒体展示了部分疑似被盗数据，其中包括员工住址、电话号码、电子邮箱、社会安全号码、职务以及所属办公室等信息。
ShinyHunters 表示，此次行动并非为了索要赎金，而是要求 FBI 修改或撤回 2026 年 5 月发布的一份安全通告。FBI 当时警告称，冒用 ShinyHunters 名义的攻击者可能夸大其访问权限，并通过骚扰、威胁甚至“Swatting”（诱骗警方前往无辜者住所实施高风险执法行动）等方式向受害者施压。
美国网络安全专家 Justin Sherman 撰文称，此次数据泄露可能使大量 FBI 员工面临个人画像、钓鱼攻击以及外国情报机构接触等风险。不过，这属于专家对事件潜在影响的判断，并非 FBI 对事件后果的官方结论。
目前尚不清楚 FBI 是否已经按照联邦政府相关规定，将此次事件正式认定为需要向国会报告的“重大事件”。美国联邦信息安全管理相关规定要求，在涉及个人身份信息泄露且可能对美国国家安全造成可证明损害等情况下，相关机构需要履行重大网络安全事件报告义务。
IT之家注意到，FBI 在今年 4 月还曾发生另一宗重大网络安全事件，当时有黑客入侵了 FBI 使用的一套监控系统，导致与 FBI 监控及调查对象有关的信息遭到暴露。
截至目前，FBI 仍在调查此次 FBIJobs.gov 入侵事件的完整范围，并与相关第三方服务提供商合作处理安全问题。FBI 尚未公布最终受影响人员数量及全部被盗数据类型。

title: 马斯克 SpaceX 成功完成星舰第 14 次试飞，首次入轨、返回、溅落并部署 26 颗卫星
content:
感谢IT之家网友 补药吖 的线索投递！
IT之家 9 月 28 日消息，北京时间 20 时 48 分，SpaceX 星舰在得克萨斯州星际基地开启第 14 次试飞，首次尝试将上级飞船送入地球轨道。
升空约 6 分 50 秒之后，超重型助推器 B21 按计划完成溅落。随着 S41 刚刚完成溅落，SpaceX 首次实现星舰轨道飞行，为此次任务划上了一个相对圆满的句号。
由于星舰一台真空发动机出现故障，因此 S41 在升空约 25 分钟后仅能通过单台猛禽发动机进行点火，但最终仍成功进入约 275km 的地球轨道。这也是它首次真正进入地球轨道。
此次任务原计划持续约 10 小时，但 SpaceX 宣布，飞行团队将在“星舰”进入轨道约 3 小时后，将其安全引导至预先划定的太平洋海域，任务将提前结束。
此次任务中，“星舰”首次成功进入地球轨道，并完成 26 颗星链 V3 卫星部署；SpaceX 表示，星链团队已与全部 26 颗卫星取得联系。这是星舰首次执行真正的轨道载荷部署任务，此前 13 次试飞均采用亚轨道轨迹。

title: 1,4 Millionen Social Media Beiträge rund um die Berliner Wahl: KI identifiziert 1.251 Narrative
content:
1,4 Millionen Social Media Beiträge rund um die Berliner Wahl: KI identifiziert 1.251 Narrative
Forschende von TU Berlin und JGU Mainz analysieren 1,4 Millionen X-Beiträge zur Berlin-Wahl. Das KI-System soll politische Debatten strukturieren und Analyseverfahren für kommende Wahlen verbessern
Die Forschungsgruppe XplaiNLP der TU Berlin und der Johannes Gutenberg-Universität (JGU) Mainz hat den deutschsprachigen Diskurs auf X zur Berliner Abgeordnetenhauswahl vom 1. bis 21. September 2026 automatisiert ausgewertet. Analysiert wurden 1.437.283 Beiträge von 118.280 Accounts. Ziel war es, zu erproben, wie sich große Mengen politischer Kommunikation mithilfe von KI strukturieren und Entwicklungen im Diskurs sichtbar machen lassen. Das System soll dabei unterstützen, Inhalte zu ordnen und Zusammenhänge zu erkennen – und nicht das menschliche Urteil zu ersetzen. Die Erkenntnisse fließen in die Weiterentwicklung des Analyseworkflows für kommende Wahlen ein. Das Besondere an der Analyse: Die Narrative wurden nicht vorab von Forschenden festgelegt. Das System extrahiert Aussagen aus einzelnen Beiträgen, bündelt inhaltlich verwandte Aussagen und lässt die entstandenen Gruppen durch ein Sprachmodell benennen. Auf diese Weise identifizierte es 1.251 Narrative. Das größte umfasst 85.534 Beiträge.
AfD prägt einen großen Teil des untersuchten Diskurses
109 der 1.251 Narrative beziehen sich in erster Linie auf die AfD. Auf sie entfallen 41 Prozent aller Beiträge, die einem Narrativ zugeordnet wurden. In einer zusätzlich geprüften Stichprobe kam die Partei in 13 Prozent der Aussagen vor. Davon positionierten sich 47 Prozent zugunsten der AfD oder stellten sie als Opfer dar, 28 Prozent äußerten sich gegen sie, 25 Prozent ohne erkennbare Positionierung. Die Zahlen beschreiben ausschließlich den untersuchten Diskurs auf der Social-Media-Plattform X. Rückschlüsse auf die Einstellungen der Berliner Bevölkerung insgesamt lassen sich daraus nicht ziehen.
Wenige Narrative und Accounts dominieren
37 Narrative waren an mindestens neun von zehn untersuchten Tagen präsent und vereinen 62 Prozent aller zugeordneten Beiträge auf sich. 540 Narrative tauchten dagegen nur selten auf und kamen zusammen auf 2,6 Prozent der Beiträge. Auch die Aktivität ist stark konzentriert: Ein Prozent der Accounts veröffentlichte ein Viertel aller Beiträge, 100 Accounts erhielten mehr als die Hälfte aller Retweets. Zugleich fanden die Forschenden keine Hinweise auf eine breit angelegte Copy-Paste-Kampagne: 81 Prozent der Beiträge waren Antworten, nahezu wortgleiche Kopien blieben selten. Nur 2,2 Prozent der Beiträge stammten von Accounts, die jünger als 90 Tage waren.
Manipulationsvorwürfe nahmen am Wahltag deutlich zu
Während der Öffnungszeit der Wahllokale am 20. September 2026 wurde der Vorwurf, eine Wahl werde manipuliert, 2,6-mal so häufig erhoben wie in den Tagen zuvor: 23,9 statt 9,2 von 1.000 Beiträgen mit einer identifizierbaren Aussage. Bei Aussagen, die ausdrücklich die Berliner Wahl betrafen, stieg der Wert auf mehr als das Achtfache: von 0,6 auf 5,0 je 1.000 Beiträge. Seit Beginn des Untersuchungszeitraums identifizierte das System 8.851 Beiträge mit Manipulationsvorwürfen und 834 Beiträge, die solchen Behauptungen widersprachen. Bei den Retweets lag das Verhältnis bei 23.909 zu 1.549.
62 Prozent der Beiträge mit Manipulationsvorwürfen nannten keinen konkreten Mechanismus. 28 Prozent bezogen sich auf die Briefwahl, neun Prozent auf die Auszählung und fünf Prozent auf das Wahlrecht. Dass reine Stichwortsuchen nicht ausreichen, zeigt ein weiterer Vergleich: 9.448 Beiträge enthalten Begriffe wie „Wahlbetrug“ oder „gefälscht“. Tatsächlich behaupten aber nur 6.648 davon eine manipulierte Wahl. Die übrigen widersprechen solchen Vorwürfen, berichten darüber oder verwenden die Begriffe in anderem Zusammenhang.
„Wir haben ein System getestet, das 1,4 Millionen Beiträge zu 1.251 Narrativen ordnen und deren Entwicklung beobachten kann, und haben es vollständig automatisiert. Entscheiden, welche davon relevant sind, welche Aussagen stimmen oder worin eine berichtenswerte Geschichte liegt, kann es nicht. Diese Einordnung bleibt Aufgabe des Menschen. Das System soll beim Sortieren helfen, nicht das Urteil übernehmen“, sagt Prof. Dr. Vera Schmitt, Leiterin der Forschungsgruppe XplaiNLP.
Grenzen der automatisierten Analyse
Die identifizierten Narrative wurden nicht nachträglich von Forschenden umbenannt oder redaktionell korrigiert. Der Bericht dokumentiert bewusst den Rohzustand der automatisierten Analyse. Untersucht wurde ausschließlich deutschsprachige Kommunikation auf der Social-Media-PlattformX. Die Vollständigkeit des Datensatzes lässt sich nicht bestimmen. Auch die Bezeichnungen der Narrative stammen von einem Sprachmodell. Ein Narrativ beschreibt damit ein Kommunikationsmuster im untersuchten Datensatz, keinen Tatsachenbefund. Aus den Daten lässt sich weder ableiten, ob eine Aussage wahr ist, noch ob Nutzer*innen sie geglaubt haben oder ob sie Wahlentscheidungen beeinflusst hat. Accountnamen, Links und vollständige Beitragstexte werden im Bericht nicht veröffentlicht.
Erkenntnisse für kommende Wahlen
Die Ergebnisse werden nun gemeinsam mit Partnern wie Gretchen.AI und dem Center für Monitoring, Analyse und Strategie (CeMAS) ausgewertet. Die Erkenntnisse sollen in die Weiterentwicklung des Analyseworkflows für kommende Wahlen, unter anderem in Brasilien und Frankreich, einfließen.
Forschungsprojekte hinter der Wahlanalyse
An der Analyse zur Berliner Abgeordnetenhauswahl waren mehrere Forschungsprojekte beteiligt, die unterschiedliche Bausteine für die automatisierte Untersuchung von Desinformation und politischen Narrativen entwickeln: DEEPGUARD, VeraXtract und FakeXplain, ein Agility Project des Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data (BIFOLD).
DEEPGUARD, geleitet von Prof. Dr. Sebastian Möller von der TU Berlin und Prof. Dr. Vera Schmitt von der JGU Mainz, baut auf dem dreijährigen Vorgängerprojekt „news-polygraph“ auf. Das Projekt entwickelt eine multimodale und erklärbare KI-Plattform, die Text, Bild, Video und Audio gemeinsam analysieren soll, um Desinformation, Deepfakes und koordinierte Manipulationskampagnen zu erkennen. Ein besonderer Fokus liegt dabei auf der Integrität von Wahlen; die Berliner Abgeordnetenhauswahl 2026 dient als Test- und Anwendungsszenario.
VeraXtract, ein BMBF-gefördertes Projekt der XplaiNLP-Gruppe an JGU Mainz und TU Berlin, erforscht Verfahren zur Verifikation und Extraktion von Desinformationsnarrativen und entwickelt individualisierte Erklärungen für die Ergebnisse. Dazu gehören unter anderem eine Vektor-Wissensdatenbank für Provenienzanalysen, NLP-Verfahren zur Erkennung von Narrativen sowie Methoden der erklärbaren KI auf unterschiedlichen Abstraktionsebenen.
FakeXplain untersucht im Rahmen eines BIFOLD Agility Projects, wie sich transparente und aussagekräftige Erklärungen für KI-gestützte Verfahren zur Erkennung von Desinformation entwickeln lassen. Damit ergänzen sich die beteiligten Projekte von der automatisierten Erkennung und Strukturierung von Narrativen bis hin zur nachvollziehbaren Erklärung der Analyseergebnisse.
An der Untersuchung beteiligt sind Max Upravitelev, Joao da Mata, Dr. Veronika Solopova, Dr. Jing Yang, Dr. Raphael Fischer und Prof. Dr. Vera Schmitt.

content:
Dateibenachrichtigungssysteme machen Windows, Linux, Android und macOS angreifbar
