title: Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and Gotion deepen strategic partnership - Batteries News
content:
Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and Gotion deepen strategic partnership
The companies are expanding their long-standing strategic partnership to include the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode active materials.
Accelerated development of a regional battery supply chain for Europe through the establishment of joint ventures at the Valencia (Spain), Šurany (Slovak Republic) and Kenitra (Morocco) sites.
Valencia to be developed into European production hub for LFP batteries.
Thomas Schmall: “Gotion has been a close partner of the Volkswagen Group for many years. We are now expanding our partnership into joint industrial production of LFP batteries to strengthen Europe’s battery industry. This marks a major breakthrough for both companies.”
Salzgitter/Hefei/Valencia. Volkswagen Group, PowerCo SE and Gotion High-tech have agreed to deepen their strategic partnership and jointly accelerate the development of a regional battery supply chain for Europe. Building on their cooperation since 2020, the partners agreed on establishing three joint ventures at the Valencia (Spain), Šurany (Slovak Republic) and Kenitra (Morocco) sites for the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode material. The agreement also covers joint procurement and sales activities in Europe. Separately, Volkswagen Group has announced that it has entered into definitive agreements to sell 5.3 % equity stake in Gotion to optimize equity structures and support long-term strategic synergies. Upon completion of the transaction, Volkswagen will continue to hold a significant stake in Gotion.
LFP batteries offer competitive costs, a long service life and high levels of robustness, making them a key technology for affordable electric mobility in the volume segment. Demand in Europe is expected to grow strongly in the coming years: According to forecasts, LFP’s market share could rise from around 10 percent today to between 40 and 60 percent by 2030. At the same time, Europe currently has no relevant LFP battery production capacity.
The partnership with Gotion strengthens Europe’s position in the global LFP battery market. Together, the partners will expand regional LFP battery production, diversify sources of supply for key cathode active materials, and thereby strengthen supply security and the competitiveness of the European battery industry.
Thomas Schmall,
Member of the Board of Management of Volkswagen Group for Technology and Chairman of the Supervisory Board of PowerCo SE:
I am delighted that we are expanding our long-standing partnership with Gotion into the joint industrial production of LFP batteries to strengthen Europe’s battery industry.
”This marks a major breakthrough for both companies and brings us one step closer to the forefront of electric mobility. Volkswagen is the first European automotive manufacturer to cover the entire battery value chain, from development and cathode materials through to production.”
Li Zhen,
Chairman of Gotion Hith-tech, said:
Six years of close collaboration between Volkswagen and Gotion have built deep mutual trust and a relationship that empowers both sides—one that has long since moved beyond ordinary business to become a partnership bound by a shared future.
”Today, together with Volkswagen Group and PowerCo, we are accelerating our global strategic cooperation. Through cross-shareholdings and three joint sites, we are anchoring our shared strategy to localise battery production in Europe, racing to seize the opportunities of global electric mobility, and jointly forging a new paradigm of world-class, win-win cooperation in the lithium battery industry.”
Frank Blome,
CEO of PowerCo SE, said:
Volkswagen and PowerCo are building Europe’s battery industry.
”The partnership with Gotion is the next milestone on this path: It strengthens the resilience of our value chain, accelerates industrialization and combines PowerCo’s capabilities with the strengths of a long-standing partner.”
Diversifying the battery supply chain
Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and Gotion have been working closely and successfully together since 2020. Gotion is both a cell supplier to the Volkswagen Group and a strategic partner of PowerCo.
With the new joint ventures, the partners are strategically expanding this proven cooperation into the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode active material. Across the three sites, they will also share investments and industrial responsibilities. The agreement therefore supports Volkswagen Group’s long-term plans to establish a European battery supply chain and strengthens PowerCo’s growth plan.
Valencia / Spain: LFP battery cells
The PowerCo gigafactory currently under construction in Valencia is envisaged to be transferred to a joint venture. The agreement provides for PowerCo to hold a 51 percent stake in the joint venture and to remain the majority shareholder. The joint venture is intended to be jointly managed by PowerCo and Gotion. One major goal is to develop the site into a European production hub for Unified Cells based on LFP technology. The planned investments and job creation measures remain as announced.
Šurany / Slovak Republic: LFP battery cells
The Gotion cell factory in Šurany is intended to be transferred to a joint venture. The agreement provides for Gotion to hold a 51 percent stake in the joint venture and to remain the majority shareholder. The joint venture is intended to be jointly managed by PowerCo and Gotion, with a focus on LFP cells for both EV applications and energy storage systems (ESS).
Kenitra / Morocco: LFP cathode material
The joint venture in Kenitra is planning to establish a new production facility to produce cathode material for LFP batteries. The facility is intended to contribute to the diversification of sources of supply for key cathode active materials, increase supply security and expand the regional value chain. Gotion will hold a 51 percent stake and be the majority shareholder of the joint venture. PowerCo and Gotion will manage the joint venture together.
Financial details
Under the terms of the agreement, PowerCo is expected to contribute in total around EUR 470 million to the Šurany and Kenitra sites by 2030 to acquire its 49 % stake. In return, the agreement provides for Gotion to invest around EUR 1.1 billion to acquire its 49 % stake in the Valencia site, reflecting the scale and strategic importance of the European production hub. The agreement remains subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, including approval by the Gotion shareholders’ meeting.
Furthermore, building on the long-standing partnership, and with the view to optimizing shareholding structures and supporting long-term strategic synergy, Volkswagen Group, through its subsidiary Volkswagen (China) Investment Co., Ltd. (VCIC), has entered into definitive agreements to sell 5.3 % equity stake in Gotion. As Volkswagen had previously agreed not to exercise voting rights for part of its shareholding, the targeted transaction will not reduce the voting rights in Gotion exercised by Volkswagen Group. Volkswagen Group’s Board of Directors representation in Gotion and other nomination rights remain unaffected by the targeted transaction. Following completion of the transaction, Volkswagen will continue to be engaged as a strategic investor in Gotion. The transaction is subject to all required regulatory clearances.

title: AMD’s World Labs Deal Signals Shift to Physical AI
content:
AMD has struck a deal to purchase AI research lab World Labs in an all-stock transaction valued at about $8.2 billion, the chipmaker announced Monday, Sept. 28. The deal aims to co-design hardware, software, and systems for emerging AI models and applications such as robotics and physical AI. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
San Francisco-based World Labs develops spatial intelligence “world models” that use text, images, and video to generate and simulate interactive 3D environments, AMD said.
AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li
, co-founder and CEO of World Labs, will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist. Upon closing, World Labs will continue to focus on AI model research, the company said.
“Building the compute platforms for the next generation of AI requires a deep understanding of how models are evolving,” said AMD CEO Lisa Su in a statement. “Fei-Fei and the World Labs team bring exceptional research leadership and model expertise. Together, we can use that insight to develop the hardware, software, and systems that will power the next generation of AI and strengthen the open AI ecosystem.”
Related:
Core Scientific Doubles AI Capacity to 1.1 GW in $14B AMD Deal
Why the Deal Matters for AMD
Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said the acquisition allows
to understand chip requirements better as AI advances. AMD’s purchase doesn’t come out of left field because it had invested in World Labs previously, he noted.
“This isn’t about AMD buying a model company. This is about being able to understand the requirements of compute and memory – and the relationship between the two as the next generation of AI emerges,” Kimball told
Data Center Knowledge
in an interview. “I like the move. To me, it is AMD looking a few years out and capturing those needs today – needs that get baked into low-level architectural decisions and designs.”
“This isn’t about AMD buying a model company. This is about being able to understand the requirements of compute and memory – and the relationship between the two as the next generation of AI emerges." – Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst, Moor Insights & Strategy
Brendan Burke, a research director at Futurum Group, said the purchase puts AMD in a stronger position in the emerging physical AI market, which AMD estimates could reach $200 billion by 2035.
“AMD identified a transformative category that has yet to produce a significant commercial impact, and shows the company is using its recent momentum to think long-term about the future of AI,” Burke said. “You can’t hire a more accomplished researcher than Dr. Fei-Fei Li, and access to talent is the biggest advantage in AI training.”
Related:
FLOPS vs Megawatts: Who’s Winning in 2026 Supercomputing?
has already moved into physical AI with its Cosmos world model, along with its Isaac and Omniverse platforms and Project GR00T robotics models, which give it an early lead in the market, Kimball said.
Burke said the acquisition gives AMD access to leading researchers in the field of physical intelligence. They could help AMD train useful models and inform the design of AMD’s rack-scale systems for those model architectures, potentially helping AMD gain market share.
Burke added that AMD increasingly sees itself as an AI research organization, having invested in internal generative AI training efforts and creating open-source models. Buying World Labs allows AMD to move deeper into the market. Co-designing with World Labs could help AMD “move toward leadership in fields that aren't yet captured by leading labs,” he said.
Building World Models
World Labs builds world models, not large language models (LLMs). While LLMs focus on the relationship between language, tokens, and information, world models are about environments – geometry, physics, objects, motions, and dynamics, Kimball said.
Related:
JPMorgan, OQC, and AMD Plan Quantum AI Data Center for Finance
“Think of it as a model for the physical world,” he said. “Any physical AI and robotics require all of this 3D modeling, geometric understanding, physics, etc., to work properly.”
For example, in training a robot to place a cup on a table, the model must account for the motions and contact dynamics so that the cup lands flat on the surface rather than half on and half off, he explained.
Talent and IP at the Core
Overall, World Labs is an acquisition of intellectual property, talent, and insights, Kimball said. The value of the deal extends beyond physical AI and into what comes next, he added.
“Fei-Fei is a rock star. You could argue that she is as much of the target as the company is. She and her team bring world-class talent to AMD, and this will enable the company to much more quickly find a competitive footing against Nvidia in this space,” he said.

title: Next-Gen AI Infrastructure Design Starts with Efficiency
content:
For years, data center design was driven by a straightforward goal: build enough capacity to meet demand. That approach made sense when workloads were more predictable, but AI is changing that equation.
Today’s infrastructure needs to
support higher-density, dynamic workloads
while making better use of power and resources. This shift is about more than efficiency for efficiency’s sake. Using infrastructure more effectively can help lower operating costs, improve resilience, and make it easier to adapt as workloads evolve.
With more than
1,500 data centers
in development in the United States, operators have an opportunity to build these advantages into infrastructure from day one rather than trying to retrofit them later. The next generation of AI infrastructure is therefore less about building with speed or relying on any single technology, and more about taking a systems-level approach that considers power, cooling, compute, and operations together.
Related:
Property Tax: The Value Driver that AI Data Centers Overlook
Why Efficiency Is Becoming a Design Priority
Growing workloads and shifting infrastructure requirements make data centers more complex to design and operate. As AI drives higher-density workloads, every infrastructure decision can have implications elsewhere in the system.
A change to the power architecture, for example, can affect cooling requirements. Cooling decisions can influence energy and
water consumption
, while compute utilization can change power and cooling needs. These interdependencies mean that efficiency cannot be addressed by a single team or discipline in isolation.
Teams must coordinate decisions and consider the upstream and downstream consequences of their choices. This helps operators balance the need for new capacity against how effectively they use existing infrastructure.
This has direct implications for both cost and resilience. Using resources more effectively can lower operating costs, while designing systems to work together reduces inefficiencies and potential failure points. Addressing these considerations during design can also reduce reliance on costly retrofits later.
A Systems-Level Approach to Efficiency
Power usage effectiveness (PUE) has long been a standard measure of data center efficiency, but it doesn’t capture every dimension of modern infrastructure. The industry’s expectations for what constitutes an efficient facility have changed. Average PUE has improved from
2.50 in 2007 to 1.52 in 2026,
while newer facilities routinely achieve
PUEs of 1.3 or lower.
A level of efficiency that would’ve been considered strong two decades ago is now well above what’s expected of modern facilities.
Related:
The Corrosion Blind Spot in the AI Buildout
This progress illustrates why operators must look beyond a single measure. A lower PUE is important, but AI infrastructure also needs to account for water, carbon, compute utilization, energy reuse, and interaction with the grid.
A broader framework can consider:
Power usage effectiveness: Energy efficiency across operations.
Water usage effectiveness (WUE): Water consumption tied to operations and cooling.
Carbon usage effectiveness (CUE): Carbon impact of IT energy consumption.
Energy reuse effectiveness (ERE): How effectively a facility reuses the energy it generates/consumes.
Compute power efficiency (CPE): IT equipment utilization relative to energy overhead.
Grid-aware operations (GAE): How workloads shift or reduce power consumption in response to grid conditions.
Together, these metrics give operators a fuller view of the trade-offs between capacity, demand, and utilization.
Designing Power, Cooling, and Compute Around Real Workloads
No single system determines infrastructure efficiency. Power, cooling, and compute all must work together, particularly as high-density AI workloads place new demands on data center environments.
That starts with designing infrastructure around how workloads behave day to day. From there, integrated power and cooling approaches can improve deployment reliability and make scaling more efficient, while modular approaches give operators the flexibility to adapt as requirements change.
Related:
Meeting AI Demand: Alternate Power, Design, and Site Strategy
As more AI infrastructure is deployed in the United States, this approach also supports a more responsive infrastructure supply chain and closer collaboration between technology providers. Growing investment in US-based manufacturing is bringing engineering, integration, and production capabilities closer together, helping the industry respond more quickly as infrastructure needs evolve.
Measuring Efficiency Through the Infrastructure Lifecycle
Efficiency is not a one-time design decision. It needs to be evaluated throughout development, deployment, and ongoing operations.
A balanced set of metrics shows operators how infrastructure is performing and where there’s room to improve. In turn, tracking energy, water, carbon, energy reuse, compute utilization, and
grid interaction
provides a fuller picture than any single measure.
As AI workloads and infrastructure requirements evolve, ongoing measurement provides operators with the visibility needed to adjust and maintain performance over time.
Building for What Comes Next
AI infrastructure will continue to scale, but capacity alone will not be enough. Operators need to design with efficiency, reliability, and adaptability in mind from the beginning.
Ultimately, successful AI infrastructure will be measured not simply by how much capacity it can deliver, but by how efficiently and reliably it can support evolving workloads.

title: The 200 GW Moment: Reinventing the Grid for the AI Economy
content:
Global data center power demand is
projected to exceed 200 gigawatts (GW)
Data Center World Power
conference in Dallas, held Sept. 21-23, leaders from utilities, power producers, hyperscalers, data center developers, operators, and supply chain partners discussed how to scale capacity while safeguarding grid reliability, protecting ratepayers, and accelerating economic development.
Bill Kleyman, executive chair of the Data Center World Power Advisory Board and CEO and co-founder of Apolo.us, opened an early session by laying out the realities of deploying Nvidia DGX-class servers. He noted that a standard rack can accommodate six such systems, each built around eight Nvidia H100 accelerators, with individual accelerator cards costing
up to $40,000
Related:
Rack Power Is Rising Fast. Here’s What It Means for Data Centers
“Sixty-nine percent of respondents to
AFCOM’s State of the Data Center 2026
survey expect that rack density is going to increase like nothing we've seen in the past,” Kleyman said. “In parallel, we are seeing 36% growth in liquid cooling adoption in data centers, and that's continuing to expand.”
Utilities Confront the Gigawatt-Scale Campus
Scott Hart, executive vice president of NRG Business, a major provider of retail electricity, natural gas, and demand response in North America, described how customer requirements have escalated. “Traditionally, data centers would be a grid-connected, 20- to 40-MW facility,” he said. “Then we saw the cloud campuses in the 100 MW range, but now conversations have pivoted to a gigawatt and beyond.”
With projects of that scale, it can be challenging for a utility to commit to constructing a power plant. Hart explained that there are two clocks running during data center development: a technology clock that operates on timelines of months or a few years, and a power infrastructure clock that operates on decades. That creates friction when customers want capacity on near-term timelines, but utilities must plan and finance assets over 15-30 years. “A utility needs a minimum 15-year time horizon and commitment with a secured [offtake agreement] that can pay for that entire period,” Hart said.
Some sites will remain grid-only. Increasingly, however, projects are pursuing hybrid arrangements that combine grid supply with on-site generation and storage, Hart noted. That can involve mixing technologies such as geothermal, gas turbine plants, and renewables.
Related:
AI Rack Density’s Real Limits: Power, Cooling, Failure Risk
Hart added that incorporating demand response – programs in which customers curtail load or shift to on-site resources during grid stress in exchange for incentives – is becoming more attractive. “Most of the data center projects we work on are excited about being part of a demand response program,” he said.
Site Selection: Power and Community
Alise Porto, vice president of sustainability and strategic initiatives at Switch, said the site selection calculus has changed. A few years ago, proximity to major metro areas and robust fiber connectivity often dominated decisions. Today, available and reliable power is paramount.
“Everything now revolves around power,” Porto said. “And more recently, the scope has expanded to both power and community – it is those two together that now coordinate where you go, how big you go, and what you do.”
“Everything now revolves around power.” – Alise Porto, vice president of sustainability and strategic initiatives, Switch
Utilities, initially surprised by multi-hundred-megawatt and gigawatt-scale requests, are increasingly engaging earlier and collaborating on flexible solutions, Porto noted. That can include agreeing to reduce power draw during peak conditions or temporarily switching to batteries or
backup generators
to support local grid reliability when needed.
Related:
Increase Data Center Density Without New Construction
To maintain optionality as chip roadmaps evolve, Switch is pursuing designs that accommodate both current and future cooling methods and densities. “Depending on the type of chips our customers have, they can deploy air cooling now and utilize liquid cooling later,” Porto said. She added that Switch’s “AI factory” design targets up to 2 MW per rack, with modularity to allow cabinet-level power draw to scale as denser server architectures enter the market.
Developer and Operator Economics
Dado Slezak
executive vice president of energy capital and strategy at QTS, emphasized the capital intensity of AI data centers, particularly when on-site power is part of the plan. “For every dollar you've got of generation, you've got multiple dollars of data center infrastructure,” he said. “With that scale of investment, there must be a decades-long financial return secured contractually.”
Slezak also cautioned against rigid long-term prescriptions. “There is no point when you can look three or four years in advance and know what you should build,” he said. “A lot can change in that time, and decisions keep shifting, each with a downstream impact.” He urged deep collaboration among partners to manage evolving technology targets and interconnection realities.

title: Australian home battery installs break more records - Energy Storage
content: Australian industry body the Clean Energy Council (CEC) has a new Rooftop Solar and Storage Report, which shows a record number of rooftop solar systems and home batteries were installed across Australia in the first six months of 2026 with solar installations on track to reach more than 300,000 this year. The bi-annual Rooftop Solar and Storage Report (Jan-Jun 2026) reveals that 180,878 rooftop solar systems were installed in the first half of 2026, a 35% increase on the same period in 2025 and the strongest six-month total since 2021. These systems delivered 1,894 MW of new capacity, up 41% year-on-year and the highest six-month period on record. A record 102,234 of these new rooftop solar installations, accounting for 1,079 MW of capacity, were delivered in the June 2026 quarter, making it the largest quarterly total on record. The CEC said the figures indicate rooftop solar installations are on track to reach more than 300,000 again this year after annual installations fell below that mark last year (273,672) for the first time since 2020. “Installation volumes have recovered sharply”, the CEC said, pointing to the success of the federal government’s Cheaper Home Batteries Program as a key driver. “Rather than displacing rooftop PV, battery incentives appear to be drawing new solar installations with them, with many households installing or upgrading solar at the same time as adding storage,” it said in the report. The report shows 276,011 home batteries were installed in the first six months of 2026, 52% higher than the previous six-month period. These systems added 8,691 MWh of storage, more than double the 4,221 MWh added in the second half of 2025. In total, 457,439 batteries with a combined 12.9 GWh of consumer storage capacity were installed in the first 12 months of the federal government’s home battery rebate program. Batteries are now being installed faster than solar systems, with the data showing 153 batteries were deployed for every 100 rooftop solar installations in the first half of 2026, up from 130 per 100 in the second half of 2025. “This indicates substantial retrofitting to homes with existing solar, alongside the new-build solar and storage packages driving the rooftop PV recovery,” the CEC said. CEC Chief Executive Jackie Trad said the record rollout of rooftop solar and batteries is a win-win for Australians, providing energy security and lowering bills at a time of global instability and economic uncertainty. “Australia is in the midst of household solar boom,” she said. “We now have more rooftop solar capacity in Australia than the capacity of all our remaining coal-fired power stations combined.” “The historic growth in household renewables is a win for both consumers and the country, delivering value and reliability for Australians and greater security for our nation’s energy supply.” The rollout of rooftop PV continues to be a reliable contributor to the nation’s energy mix, with a generation share of 12.9% in the first six months of 2026. Trad said the coming expansion of the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme (SRES) to support solar systems up to 1 MW in size will provide another boost for solar installations. Household and small business investment is already running well ahead of the Australian Energy Market Operator’s (AEMO) central planning scenario for both solar and energy storage. At current rates, rooftop solar in Australia’s National Electricity Market (NEM) is expected to reach 40.3 GW by 2029-30, about 4.5 GW or 13% above AEMO’s ISP Step Change scenario. title: Greece can install 8.6 GW of batteries by 2030 - Energy Storage
content: One of the main questions addressed at Solarplaza’s battery energy storage system (BESS) conference held last week in Athens was how much battery storage Greece will install by 2030. The answer depended on who was asked, with forecasts ranging from conservative to considerably more optimistic. Louiza Moutafi, senior research associate at Aurora Energy Research, a global consultancy with an office in Athens, said Greece will install around 4 GW to 5 GW of BESS by 2030. The first systems to become operational will include the 900 MW of standalone, front-of-the-meter systems selected through auctions in previous years. Of this capacity, 711 MW comprises two-hour batteries and the remaining 189 MW four-hour systems. Their construction and operation are supported by state subsidies. Moutafi told the Solarplaza conference that around 400 MW of the auctioned capacity has already been connected to the grid and that the entire 900 MW will be operational by the end of 2026. Aurora Energy Research estimates that additional storage capacity will comprise standalone batteries operating on a merchant basis, without subsidies, and batteries co-located with power generation, most notably solar PV. The first of these systems, totaling around 100 MW, could become operational this year, Moutafi said. However, the majority – around 3 GW to 4 GW – is expected to be installed between 2027 and 2030. By 2050, Aurora Energy Research projects a further 47.6% increase in this capacity. Both Moutafi and Stelios Psomas, policy officer at the Hellenic Association of Photovoltaic Companies (Helapco), who also presented at the Solarplaza event, identified the same main segments shaping Greece’s BESS market. Psomas added that around 100 MW of small-scale batteries connected to self-consumption PV systems, including systems operating under net metering, are already operational. For standalone batteries operating on a merchant basis without subsidies, Moutafi and Psomas highlighted the government’s ongoing 4.7 GW program . It comprises 3.8 GW of BESS seeking connections to the transmission system and 900 MW to the distribution network, for which the government has invited licensing applications. The co-located segment of the Greek storage market comprises several categories. One covers batteries installed alongside existing or new solar projects operated by small, medium-sized and large businesses. These systems are intended to increase self-consumption and reduce electricity costs. Greece’s Ministry of Environment and Energy recently published a list of 209 projects that will receive funding under this category. Psomas also outlined three other segments of the co-located market. The so-called 11A category comprises projects in which batteries can charge only from PV. Under the 11B category, batteries can charge from both PV and the grid but cannot discharge during hours when power curtailment may be required. The 11C category covers batteries serving clusters of PV plants. Discharge restrictions similar to those applying to 11B projects also apply to 11C projects, but only to the battery and not to the PV component. IRRs Aurora Energy Research ranks Greece among Europe’s 10 most attractive battery storage markets and among the top three in Southeast Europe, alongside Bulgaria and Romania. Moutafi said a two-hour standalone battery entering commercial operation in 2027 on a merchant basis and completing 1.5 charge-discharge cycles per day could achieve an internal rate of return (IRR) of between 9% and just under 12%. By comparison, co-located PV-plus-storage projects could achieve IRRs exceeding 11%, regardless of configuration, commissioning year, battery duration or cycling strategy. Asked by this publication whether such returns could prompt a wave of co-located projects to become operational in the near term, Moutafi said the Greek government has prioritized standalone BESS and that she therefore expects deployment of co-located systems to accelerate from 2028. She noted, for example, that the government announced the charging rules for the 11A, 11B and 11C categories only a few months ago. Such information is crucial for developers seeking to design project business models. Moutafi said several factors enable co-located PV-plus-storage projects to achieve higher IRRs than standalone BESS. These include savings on capital and operating expenditure, the ability to charge batteries directly from PV generation and opportunities for load shifting. Co-located projects can also participate in other electricity markets, including the balancing market. Aurora Energy Research estimates that a two-hour standalone merchant battery entering operation in 2027 and completing 1.5 charge-discharge cycles per day would derive 70% of its lifetime revenue from energy arbitrage and the remaining 30% from capacity payments for ancillary services. Greece’s balancing market is relatively small, however, and Moutafi expects price cannibalization to emerge relatively quickly in its shallower segments, particularly markets for balancing capacity reservation services. Optimism Helapco’s Psomas presented a considerably more optimistic outlook for Greece’s BESS market, arguing that the country could install 8.6 GW of battery storage by 2030. He cited two main reasons for the forecast. The first is the growing need for PV investors to deploy storage to mitigate renewable energy curtailment and exposure to negative wholesale electricity prices. Psomas said renewable energy curtailment remains high this year, although it has been lower than expected. The number of hours with negative electricity prices, by contrast, has risen sharply. Greece recorded only 11 hours of negative prices in 2024, rising to 115 hours in 2025 and 382 hours by Sept. 15, 2026. The second reason is what Psomas described as an “acceleration scenario.” Once the first BESS projects – whether standalone merchant batteries or co-located systems – are installed, businesses and financiers gain experience that can facilitate further investment. “Batteries at present are the real disruptive technology,” Psomas said, adding that he expects the sector to grow faster than many anticipate. As of August 2026, Greece had issued licenses for 55.3 GW/166.2 GWh of standalone BESS, 11.8 GW/28.1 GWh of co-located BESS in the 11B category and 16.7 GW/163.7 GWh of pumped hydro energy storage (PHES), according to Psomas. title: Statkraft signs 1.6 GWh tolling agreement for two Greenvolt battery projects in Poland - Energy Storage
content: One of Europe’s largest renewable companies, Statkraft, has signed a 10-year tolling agreement with global developer Greenvolt Power. The deal, which covers the two significant projects in Poland, namely the Ełk (200 MW/800 MWh) and Turośń Kościelna (200 MW/800 MWh) projects, is located in the north-east of the country in Nowa Wieś Ełcka and Turośń Kościelna, respectively. It marks one of the largest public BESS agreements in Europe, and is Statkraft’s first large-scale BESS contract in the Polish market. The structure of a tolling agreement gives “Statkraft the right to decide when the batteries charge and discharge across energy and flexibility markets,” the companies said. This toll structure provides Greenvolt with predictable long-term revenue, in addition to revenue from Poland’s capacity market which starts in 2028 for the Turośń Kościelna project. Tolling wasn’t required to finance the construction, build, and asset purchases, with Greenvolt securing financing from UniCredit comprising EUR 153 million in bridge facilities and a EUR 65 million guarantee facility back in August . Turośń Kościelna was inaugurated in July 2026, while Ełk is expected to reach commercial operation shortly. BYD Energy Storage supplied the actual battery energy storage systems, and while not specified, they appear in photos as the BYD MC-Cube T option. “Our partnership with Greenvolt shows our ambition in Poland. With the largest BESS transaction signed in the country to date, we continue to play an active role in supporting Poland’s energy transition … Having previously signed Poland’s largest cPPA and first subsidy-free utility-based solar PPA, we are proud to add another landmark transaction,” says Kornel Koronowski, Head of Origination Poland, Statkraft. “This agreement with Statkraft brings sophisticated market optimization to these projects, allowing the flexibility of the batteries to be monetised across different power markets and unlocking additional revenues. We have built strong capabilities in originating and developing utility-scale assets and, as we move further along the value chain, with projects now entering operation, choosing the right commercial structure is increasingly important”, says Łukasz Zagórski, Business Origination and Market Regulation Director, Greenvolt Power. title: Hyundai is launching two new EVs, the IONIQ 4 and IONIQ 7
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 29 2026 - 7:26 am PT
is preparing to introduce two new electric SUVs, the IONIQ 4 and IONIQ 7, filling two key gaps in its EV lineup.
Hyundai adds IONIQ 4 and IONIQ 7 to its EV lineup
The IONIQ 5 is about the size of the Tesla Model Y, while the IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating, but what if you wanted something in between?
Hyundai is launching two new electric SUVs as it expands into new segments. One will sit below the IONIQ 5, and the other between the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.
The IONIQ 7 is slightly bigger than the IONIQ 5 and aimed more at families, offering more interior space. The IONIQ 4, on the other hand, is a B-segment SUV that will offer an option between the
recently launched IONIQ 3
and the IONIQ 5.
Hyundai has yet to confirm specifics, but Chris McKinnon, Hyundai Europe’s VP of product, told
Auto Express
to “watch this space” and to keep an eye out for more information on the upcoming B-segment SUV.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 (Source: Hyundai)
When asked if it will be similar to the Kia EV3, McKinnon said: “I really can’t answer that question, to be honest,” but added that the market was “important” for the Hyundai brand.
Like the EV3, the Hyundai IONIQ 4 is expected to feature a boxier, more SUV-like design than the IONIQ 3 and IONIQ 5.
Inside, the electric SUV will feature Hyundai’s new interior design, like the IONIQ 3. It’s also expected to have Hyundai’s next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior with Pleos Connect infotainment system (Source: Hyundai)
We will learn more about the IONIQ 4 soon, but it’s expected to be available with similar battery pack options: 42 kWh and 61 kWh. The former provides up to 214 miles (344 km) of WLTP range. The latter gets up to 308 miles (497 km).
While the Kona Electric is still currently available in the UK, it is expected to be discontinued and replaced by the new IONIQ 4.
When it arrives, the Hyundai IONIQ 4 will likely start at around £25,000 ($33,000), or slightly more than the IONIQ 3.
Hyundai IONIQ 5 (Source: Hyundai)
The IONIQ 7 will fill the gap between the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 with two- or three-row seating options. It will be closer in size and price to
the IONIQ 5
, but with a boxier, SUV-like look. It will be available with dual- and single-motor powertrains.
No other details have been confirmed, but the IONIQ 7 is expected to offer a WLTP range of at least 400 miles and fast charging with an 800V architecture.
It will also be equipped with Hyundai Pleos and is expected to start at around £45,000 to £50,000 ($60,000 to $66,000) in the UK.
Will Hyundai bring either to the US? Don’t get your hopes up. Although Hyundai has not officially announced either model, the IONIQ 4 and IONIQ 7 are likely designed for the European market. We should learn more soon, with both set to launch in the next 12 to 18 months.

title: Tesla patents 'Electric Fan Car' with 4 ducted fans ahead of Roadster reveal
content:
Tesla Model S
Tesla Roadster
McMurtry Speirling
Fred Lambert
| Sep 29 2026 - 7:02 am PT
Tesla was just granted a patent for an “Electric Fan Car,” a system that uses four electric ducted fans in the rear diffuser to suck the car down to the road at any speed. The car in the drawings is a Model S, which Tesla stopped building in April.
It’s Tesla’s second fan car patent in just over a year, and it arrives two weeks before the company’s latest attempt at a Roadster demo.
Four fans in the diffuser
The USPTO granted
US 12,746,987 B1
today. Tesla filed it in January 2024, but it goes back to a provisional application from January 17, 2023. Eight inventors are listed, and all but one are based in the Los Angeles area, where Tesla has its design studio in Hawthorne.
The idea is simple. An inlet on the underbody, between the rear wheels, feeds a duct that sweeps up to a wide outlet in the rear diffuser. Four axial fans sit side by side in that outlet, split by three vertical strakes. When they spin up, they evacuate the air under the floor and exhaust it through the rear.
FIG. 1 from Tesla’s patent: air flows under the Model S, into the inlet (13), and out through the fans (10) at the rear. Credit: USPTO
That creates what Tesla calls a “suction region” under the floor. A vacuum. The rear end also gets a raked plate that acts as a second diffuser.
FIG. 2: four electric ducted fans (10) separated by strakes (15) in the Model S rear diffuser. Credit: USPTO
Tesla’s pitch is about speed independence. The filing notes that passive diffusers limit downforce at low speed and “often results in an excessive load at a high speed.” The fans, according to Tesla, “can produce a downforce independent of the vehicle velocity,” which helps with braking stability and cornering speed.
There’s one clever detail. A second version adds two smaller side inlets behind the main one, because Tesla says the central inlet tends to pull air forward from behind the car instead of from under the floor. That backwash adds no downforce, and Tesla says the fans end up “wasting power” on it.
FIG. 3B: the underbody, with the suction region (17), central inlet (13), and the side inlets (18) that stop the fans from sucking air back in from behind the car. Credit: USPTO
Power comes from the same high-voltage pack that drives the wheels, so there’s no separate motor or battery for the fans, and they’re tied into the car’s control system. The driver can switch them on with a button, or the car can do it automatically at certain speeds.
Drawn on a car Tesla doesn’t make anymore
You can’t miss the Model S in these drawings. The fastback roofline, taillights, lip spoiler and door handles are all there.
In early 2023, when Tesla filed the provisional, that made sense. The Model S Plaid was Tesla’s performance flagship, and a fan-assisted track version would have been a fun halo. But
Tesla ended Model S and Model X production
in April after 14 years, and it’s turning the Fremont line over to Optimus. So that’s not happening.
Which leaves the Roadster, the only performance car Tesla still has in the pipeline. Last week, we reported on
a Tesla patent for a hidden active rear wing
good for up to 700 kg of downforce, drawn on a car that looks just like the new Roadster. And in August 2025, Tesla got
another fan car patent
using underbody fans and deployable skirts. Fans plus an active wing is a full track aero package, and the Roadster is the only car left to put it on.
Fan cars are nothing new
None of this is new. Chaparral raced the 2J in 1970 with two fans driven by a separate snowmobile engine. Brabham’s BT46B won the 1978 Swedish Grand Prix with Niki Lauda and was withdrawn right after. Gordon Murray put a 400 mm fan on the back of the T.50 road car.
And on the electric side, McMurtry has been doing it for years. Its Spéirling
smashed the all-time Goodwood hill climb record in June 2022
, about seven months before Tesla filed its provisional. It makes 2,000 kg of downforce at a standstill, has
driven upside down
, and McMurtry
started production of the $1.36 million Spéirling PURE
earlier this year. Its fans also run off the main battery.
Tesla’s main twist is that its design doesn’t need skirts sealing the car to the ground. The filing says the fans can work “without use of additional elements below the vehicle,” and packages them into a normal-looking diffuser.
Electrek’s Take
It’s a neat patent, but electric fan cars exist; they’re on sale, and McMurtry got there first by a wide margin. Putting the fans in the diffuser without skirts is a packaging choice. And without skirts, it’s hard to see Tesla getting anywhere near the 2,000 kg the Spéirling makes.
The Model S drawings say more than the claims do. Somebody at Tesla was clearly working on a track-focused Model S in 2023. That car is dead, and the idea has nowhere to go but the Roadster. Between this, last year’s skirted fan patent, and last week’s 700 kg wing, Tesla has built up a real track aero toolbox. That’s a lot more useful than making a car hover on SpaceX thrusters.
But patents aren’t products, and Tesla patents plenty of things that never ship. The Roadster was unveiled in 2017, promised for 2020, and is now
slated for “2027 or 2028” with a demo pushed to October 15
. If it finally shows up with fans in the back, great. We’d take that over a hover stunt any day.
Will we see fans on October 15, or just thrusters?

title: Two Silverado EVs and a 150 kWh battery powered this entire concert tour
content:
Chevrolet
Chevy Silverado EV
Fred Lambert
| Sep 29 2026 - 8:01 am PT
Photo: © arbourphoto.com
A five-stop concert tour in Quebec ran entirely on two Chevrolet Silverado EVs and a 150 kWh mobile power plant this summer. No diesel generator, and no hookup to the grid.
I went to the final show, held in a grocery store parking lot in Montreal’s Saint-Henri neighborhood, and everything from the speakers to the stage lights to the kitchen was running off batteries.
A free tour powered by EV batteries
The tour, called “Le goût du paysage” (roughly “a taste of the landscape”), was put together by
Papillons
. That’s the Quebec company behind the RechargÉco fast-charging network, which it operates across Quebec and New Brunswick.
The idea was simple: bring Québécois artists Émile Proulx-Cloutier and Dumas, along with chef Oli cooking free corn dishes made with regional ingredients, to scenic spots across the province. Admission was free.
It ran from August 15 to 22 with stops in Trois-Pistoles, the Vallée Bras-du-Nord in Saint-Raymond, Parc Éco-Laurentides in Mont-Blanc, and Île-aux-Castors in Berthierville (that one sold out). The tour wrapped up with both artists on stage in the IGA parking lot in Saint-Henri.
Papillons billed the whole production as “100%” powered by EV batteries, with “zero emissions from start to finish.” Based on what I saw on site, that’s accurate.
One of the two Chevy Silverado EVs on the tour. Photo: © arbourphoto.com
Two pickups running the stage
The two Silverado EVs handled the stage: the sound system, the lighting, and the site lights once the sun went down. In Saint-Henri, I could follow the cable straight out of the power outlet in one truck’s bed to the stage.
A cable running from the Silverado EV’s bed outlet to the stage in Saint-Henri. Photo: Fred Lambert/Electrek
It’s a good job for the truck. The Silverado EV can be had with up to a 205 kWh battery pack, one of the biggest you can buy in a consumer vehicle, and GM rates its onboard power at 7.2 kW to 10.2 kW depending on the trim. We’ve already seen
GM run an entire mansion off a Silverado EV
when it launched its GM Energy products, and the
2026 Silverado EV
only pushed range further.
For comparison, Ford’s F-150 Lightning tops out at 9.6 kW of onboard power. And Tesla only just
added 2.4 kW of vehicle-to-load to the Model Y Premium
, and you need an $80 adapter for it.
Dumas on stage during the tour. Photo: © arbourphoto.com
The kitchen ran on a 150 kWh mobile power plant
The kitchen is the hard part. Cooking equipment pulls a lot of power, and it runs for hours.
For that, Papillons used a trailer-mounted mobile power plant with 150 kWh of energy capacity. It powered chef Oli’s kitchen at every stop.
Full disclosure:
my company,
, was involved in this project. We helped Papillons engineer the mobile power plant. Papillons isn’t ready to share more details about the system just yet, so I’ll leave it at that for now, but you can
reach out to them
if you are interested in such a product.
At the Saint-Henri stop, the trailer was parked right next to the kitchen tent, feeding full-size electric ranges topped with giant stockpots.
The trailer holding the 150 kWh mobile power plant, parked beside the kitchen tent in Saint-Henri. Photo: Fred Lambert/Electrek
The kitchen ran on electric ranges, all fed by the battery trailer. Photo: Fred Lambert/Electrek
Why bother with batteries in the city?
The show I attended was in the middle of Montreal. There’s power everywhere in Saint-Henri: the grocery store, the buildings around the lot, the streetlights.
The stage in the IGA parking lot in Saint-Henri, Montreal. Photo: Fred Lambert/Electrek
But having power nearby and being allowed to use it are two different things. Getting a temporary connection for an event usually means dealing with the utility or the property owner, hiring an electrician, and paying for all of it, often for a single evening. Plenty of organizers skip the headache and rent a diesel generator instead.
With batteries, you roll in, plug in, and you’re done. And on a stage where people are there for quiet acoustic songs, the lack of a rumbling generator behind the crowd matters.
But the real advantage showed up at the other four stops. A riverside island in Berthierville, a valley in Saint-Raymond, a park in the Laurentians. There’s no grid access at those spots, period. Normally, that’s where the diesel generators come out, if the show happens at all.
The Île-aux-Castors stop in Berthierville, with no grid power in sight. Photo: Papillons
And the energy itself is about as clean as it gets. The trucks and the power plant recharge on Quebec’s grid, which Hydro-Québec says is over 99% renewable, mostly hydro.
Electrek’s Take
Events are a great fit for mobile power supply. Festivals, outdoor concerts, film shoots, and construction sites burn a lot of diesel in rented generators, and they do it right next to people. A big battery on wheels does the same job silently, with no fumes, and it can be recharged at a charging station between stops. It helps that Papillons runs a fast-charging network.
The limit right now is output. Even the Silverado EV caps out around 10 kW per truck, which is plenty for sound and lights but not enough for everything.
But the concept works. I saw it work. It’s a great use case example for bidirectional charging, which I think is going to become an increasingly important part of the EV revolution.

title: 亿纬锂能、海辰储能等5企海外储能订单及项目落地
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，中国储能企业加速拓展海内外市场，接连完成项目的签单与交付。
海辰储能首批长时储能系统出口海外
近日，海辰储能山东菏泽基地首批长时储能系统完成发运，并经青岛港出口海外。这也是该基地今年8月实现量产后，首次向海外批量发货。
此次出口产品为∞Power 6.25MWh 4h长时储能系统预制舱，单舱容量6.25MWh，搭载1175Ah长时储能电芯，可根据项目需求配置4至8小时储能时长，主要用于新能源并网、电网调节等场景。
亿纬锂能完成菲律宾户储订单交付
近日，亿纬锂能向菲律宾本土品牌NSS Solar Philippines（NSS）交付首批18kWh户用储能系统，产品主要面向菲律宾户用储能市场。
此次交付的产品搭载亿纬锂能356Ah电芯，单套容量18kWh，采用磷酸铁锂技术，循环寿命达8000次。产品支持壁挂和落地两种安装方式，还可通过并机扩大系统容量。
晶科签220MWh德国混合型储能项目
近日，晶科储能在德国签下总规模220MWh的混合型储能项目群。项目包括绿电储能和市场化储能两类系统，同时配套光伏装机，用于支撑混合型购电协议（hybrid PPA）。
项目采用晶科储能Tera液冷储能系统，单套容量为5.01MWh。其中，绿电储能与可再生能源发电配套使用，市场化储能则参与电力系统调节和市场交易。
冠隆电力112kWh储能系统落地斯洛伐克
9月，冠隆电力一套112kWh All-in-one储能系统在斯洛伐克投入运行，产品型号为LES-112W50-PS，应用于欧洲工商业储能场景。
该产品采用一体化柜体设计，电池PACK、BMS、PCS、EMS、温控、除湿及消防系统均集成于单台储能柜内，单柜容量112kWh，最大可接入100kW光伏，同时支持多机并联以及并离网运行。
宁德时代签署918MWh储能项目合作协议
近日，宁德时代与罗马尼亚可再生能源集团Renovatio旗下EPC公司Renovatio Solar达成战略合作，双方将共同推进罗马尼亚东北部摩尔多瓦地区的Borzești 918MWh储能电站项目。
该项目由Borzești Energy Storage SRL开发，RNV Infrastructure和Greenvolt Power共同持股。Renovatio Solar承担EPC总包工作，包括项目设计、设备采购、施工以及调试并网，预计建设周期为12个月。

title: 国轩高科投资126亿建三大海外电芯及正极材料基地
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月28日，国轩高科披露两份公告，拟与大众汽车集团共同在西班牙、斯洛伐克及摩洛哥布局锂电池和正极材料项目；同时，国轩高科旗下子公司拟承接大众汽车集团西班牙29.1GWh锂电池项目一期、二期工程总包，合同金额合计10.94亿欧元（约合人民币86.4亿元）。
拟投建三大海外生产基地
根据公告，国轩高科及旗下Gotion High-Tech(HK)Limited、Gotion GmbH、Gotion Power Africa S.A.S.将与大众汽车集团及其旗下PowerCo SE、Power Holdco Lux S.A.分别在西班牙瓦伦西亚、斯洛伐克苏拉尼和摩洛哥肯尼特拉组建三家合资公司，投资建设锂电池和正极材料生产基地，项目总投资约32.22亿欧元（约合人民币254.5亿元），其中国轩方投资约15.98亿欧元（约合人民币126.2亿元），出资来源为自有资金及自筹资金。
具体项目规划如下：
西班牙瓦伦西亚基地：
双方拟以瓦伦西亚合资公司为主体，投资建设年产29.1GWh锂电池项目，该项目总投资金额约22.62亿欧元（约合人民币178.7亿元），项目建设周期预计不超过5年。瓦伦西亚合资公司由香港国轩下属拟设欧洲主体对PowerCo Spain进行增资。本次投资事项完成后，国轩方占合资公司49%的股权，PowerCo方占合资公司51%的股权。该合资公司为PowerCo方控股子公司。
斯洛伐克苏拉尼基地：
双方拟以苏拉尼合资公司为主体投资建设年产8.4GWh锂电池项目，该项目总投资金额约4.8亿欧元（约合人民币37.9亿元），项目建设周期预计不超过5年。苏拉尼合资公司由Gotion GmbH在斯洛伐克苏拉尼新设公司主体后接受PowerCo Lux增资。本次投资事项完成后，国轩方占合资公司51%的股权，PowerCo方占合资公司49%的股权。该合资公司为国轩方控股子公司。
摩洛哥肯尼特拉基地：
双方拟以摩洛哥合资公司为主体投资建设年产10万吨磷酸铁锂正极材料项目，该项目总投资金额约4.8亿欧元（约合人民币37.9亿元），项目建设周期预计不超过5年。摩洛哥合资公司由Gotion Power于摩洛哥肯尼特拉新设公司主体后接受PowerCo Lux增资。本次投资事项完成后，国轩方占合资公司51%的股权，PowerCo方占合资公司49%的股权，该合资公司为国轩方控股子公司。
苏拉尼合资公司和瓦伦西亚合资公司生产的电芯，优先支持大众汽车在欧洲的市场需求，摩洛哥合资公司生产的正极材料优先供应上述两个合资公司。
签署10.94亿欧元工程合同
除了股权合作，国轩高科还将直接参与上述西班牙电池项目的工程建设。
根据公告，国轩高科全资子公司Gotion Spain Green Energy,S.L.拟与西班牙合资主体PowerCo Battery Spain,S.A.U.分别签署两项总承包合同，合同总金额达10.94亿欧元（约合人民币86.4亿元）。包括：
《一期干燥房总承包合同》：
合同总价款为2.95亿欧元（约合人民币23.3亿元）。工程范围为一期动力电池产线中洁净干燥房的设计施工、设备的采购及安装调试项目的总承包。建设周期为自开工日后472天。
《二期工程总承包合同》：
合同总价款为7.99亿欧元（约合人民币63.1亿元）。工程范围是对二期动力电池产线工程的设计施工、设备的采购及安装调试项目的总承包。建设周期为自开工日后1181天。

title: 理想汽车：固态电池或最快2027年小批量上车
content:
9月22日消息，据财联社报道，理想汽车内部人士透露，理想汽车固态电池预计将在2027年或2028年具备小批量上车能力。
理想汽车动力电池高级总监柳志民表示，目前理想汽车持续推进固态电池技术布局，已有多个相关项目处于开发阶段，并已在眼镜产品上完成固态电池原型验证。不过，在整车实现成熟量产并保证用户体验的确定性，预计仍需要约5年时间。
柳志民指出，目前固态电池在同时满足使用寿命、充电性能和成本方面仍存在挑战。理想汽车相关负责人此前也提到，从技术成熟度来看，固态电池距离大规模量产仍有一定距离。
今年以来，理想汽车加快电池自研布局，9月宣布自研电池将逐步覆盖全系车型。目前，理想自研电池已经搭载于L8、L6和i8等车型，后续将继续扩大搭载范围。其中，新一代理想MEGA计划在自研5C三元锂电池完成生产爬坡后切换，2026款理想i6则计划搭载自研5C电池和自研马赫芯片。
今年9月，理想汽车还进一步加码电池产业链布局。公司与欣旺达动力的合作持续深化，并以26.5亿元战略投资欣旺达动力，理想表示，此类投资主要围绕技术和战略合作展开。
欣旺达自身也在推进固态电池产业化。2026年8月，欣旺达披露半年报称，公司固态电池样品线已经完成贯通，计划年内启动中试生产，并同步推进全尺寸电池验证。目前，固态电池产品处于验证送样测试阶段；320Wh/kg和360Wh/kg半固态电池产品已经实现小批量量产，并已应用于低空飞行器等场景。
今年4月，欣旺达动力中央研究院院长徐中领曾透露，公司已贯通0.2GWh固态电池样品线，计划在2026年完成全尺寸电池开发，达到装车验证要求。

title: 隆基/晶科/天合等6企签约交付多项组件订单
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，光伏组件企业海外订单与国内项目供货持续推进，其中，隆基为罗马尼亚项目供应315MW组件，晶科能源中标220MW组件订单，天合光能签署450MW东南亚组件订单，琏升科技为72MW光伏项目供应异质结组件，正泰新能获得400MW组件订单，极电光能钙钛矿组件则进一步拓展海内外多个市场。
隆基为罗马尼亚项目供应315MW组件
近日，由Nofar能源集团开发的罗马尼亚Iepureşti和Ghimpati两座光伏项目正式并网投运，项目合计装机规模超过315MW，全部采用隆基高效光伏组件。
两座项目均位于罗马尼亚久尔久县，建成后预计年发电量约430GWh，项目后续还规划配套建设电池储能系统。
此次315MW项目为隆基与Nofar能源集团合作的一期项目。双方自2023年起累计合作规模约900MW，其中一期315MW已完成交付并网，其余项目预计于2026年内完成交付。
晶科能源中标220MW光伏组件订单
近日，连云港青口盐场渔光一体化发电项目光伏组件设备中标结果正式公示，晶科能源中标该项目组件采购订单，供货规模为220MW，将供应项目全部N型高效光伏组件。
青口盐场渔光一体化项目位于江苏省连云港市，项目装机容量220MW，采用渔光一体化模式建设。此次中标产品为晶科能源飞虎3（Tiger Neo 3.0）N型组件，单片功率最高670W，组件正面效率最高超过24.8%。
天合光能签450MW东南亚组件订单
近日，天合光能在东南亚市场连续获得光伏组件订单，分别为菲律宾Bugallon光伏电站和越南达田5号漂浮光伏项目供应至尊N型700W+组件。
其中，天合光能与菲律宾PetroGreen Energy Corporation签署供货协议，为Bugallon光伏电站供应至尊N型700W+组件。项目位于菲律宾班诗兰省，投运后预计年均发电量约51GWh。
在越南市场，天合光能与春桥控股旗下DT5.1能源股份有限公司达成合作，为达田5号漂浮光伏项目供应至尊N型700W+组件，项目装机容量450MW。该项目位于越南西宁省达田湖，已于2026年8月开工，预计2027年12月并网。
正泰新能获400MW光伏组件订单
近日，正泰新能披露，其高效光伏组件将应用于甘肃省甘南藏族自治州碌曲县“十四五”第二、三批光伏发电项目，供货规模合计400MW。
据介绍，该项目总装机容量400MW，其中第二批300MW、第三批100MW，项目位于碌曲县海拔约3500米的高原地区，采用“牧光互补”模式开发。项目组件全部采用正泰新能ASTRO N系列产品，正泰电源提供组串式逆变器，正泰新能源负责EPC建设，项目计划于2027年6月建成并网。
琏升科技为72MW光伏项目供应HJT组件
近日，四川省巴中市通江县分布式屋顶光伏发电项目加快推进，项目规划装机规模72MW，琏升科技参与项目建设，并提供G12-0BB“琏升天王星PRO”高效异质结（HJT）组件。
该组件量产最高功率可达765W，组件转换效率24.63%以上，最高双面率近95%，采用多分片、高密度封装及UV转光胶膜等技术，主要面向工商业屋顶、公共建筑等分布式应用场景。
极电光能钙钛矿组件交付国内外项目
近期，极电光能钙钛矿光伏组件陆续交付四川、浙江、福建、青海等国内项目，并首次进入欧洲、沙特等海外市场，交付产品包括“创势”标准组件和“极曜”系列BIPV产品。
其中，“创势”组件已批量发往四川、福建、青海等项目地，并首次进入沙特市场，应用场景覆盖不同气候环境；“极曜”系列BIPV产品则持续交付浙江等地项目，应用于厂区改造、围栏、幕墙、屋顶、车棚等场景。
此外，极电光能柔性钙钛矿组件也已实现海外市场出货，此次欧洲项目为该类产品首次海外交付。

title: Arcadia eFuels selects Plug Power for Danish e-SAF project | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
Project ENDOR is Arcadia eFuels’ flagship facility, located at the Port of Vordingborg on Denmark’s south coast. The plant will use renewable grid power to run 280 MW of Plug’s GenEco electrolyzers, producing approximately 110 tons of renewable hydrogen per day. Arcadia eFuels plans to combine that hydrogen with captured carbon dioxide to produce synthetic jet fuel compatible with standard aircraft engines.
The supply agreement follows three years of joint engineering work. Deliveries are set to begin after the project issues a notice to proceed. Project ENDOR is advancing toward a final investment decision (FID).
The strategic cooperation agreement extends the relationship to four additional Arcadia eFuels projects, with priority access to Plug’s manufacturing capacity as each project advances.
“Signing the ENDOR supply agreement alongside a strategic cooperation agreement positions Plug not only as the electrolyzer supplier for Arcadia eFuels’ flagship project, but as their preferred partner across a pipeline of e-SAF developments in Europe and the Americas,” said José Luis Crespo, President and Chief Executive Officer of Plug. “This reflects continued confidence in our GenEco technology, our manufacturing capacity, and Plug’s ability to deliver complex, high-capacity projects at scale. Europe remains our most active electrolyzer market, and e-SAF is one of the fastest-growing segments of demand as aviation fuel mandates take effect. Producing that fuel from European electricity and European carbon rather than imported oil also strengthens the continent’s energy security.”
“Project ENDOR is on the path to final investment decision, and this supply agreement from Plug signifies one of the many project documents that have been finalized,” said Amy Hebert, Chief Executive Officer of Arcadia eFuels. “Sustainable aviation fuel made from renewable hydrogen and captured carbon is what will get aviation to its decarbonisation targets, and Plug gives us a proven and bankable electrolyzer partner at the scale this project demands.”
The EU’s ReFuelEU Aviation mandate requires a rising share of SAF at European airports, including a sub-target for synthetic fuels from 2030. Plug said it is executing multiple European projects with combined capacity in the multi-gigawatt range, including a 100 MW GenEco installation at Galp’s refinery in Sines, Portugal.

title: Metacon launches 20 MW alkaline electrolyzer module
content:
The module uses a multi-level steel-frame arrangement, with electrolyser stacks on the lower level and gas-handling equipment and cooling units positioned above. This layout reduces the required plot area and shortens process, utility, and electrical interconnections. The design also eliminates the need for a conventional factory building around the hydrogen generation system.
Compared with conventional building-based installations, Metacon said calculations indicate cost reductions of up to 30% on steel structures, up to 50% on piping materials, insulation, pipe supports, and related items, and up to 70% on area-related infrastructure costs. The company noted that the exact magnitude of savings will depend on site conditions, project scope, and final design.
The 20 MW module is based on the same modular principles as Metacon’s existing 10 MW module. Units can be installed individually or in parallel as plant capacity increases, reducing on-site construction and assembly work. The repeatable design is intended to simplify transport, installation, and future capacity expansion.
Christer Wikner, President and CEO of Metacon, said: “Metacon continues to innovate for driving hydrogen production cost down and now look beyond the electrolyser stacks. We have identified great opportunities to improve the complete plant design by addressing other major cost drivers. By using less space and reducing the amount of steel, piping, cabling and other infrastructure required, this module will serve as a super-efficient building module for large hydrogen production plants. At the same time, this is also a standardisation initiative where repeatability of core components drives both cost reduction as well as overall quality.”

title: Nel to supply PEM stacks for US Navy submarines
content:

Todd Cartwright, Chief Commercial Officer of Nel ASA, said: “We are pleased to receive another order from Collins Aerospace. It extends a long-standing cooperation built around reliable oxygen generation for demanding submarine applications.”

title: A ‘Roller Coaster Ride’: What Toyota Got Right (And Wrong) About EVs, According To An Executive
content:
A ‘Roller Coaster Ride’: What Toyota Got Right (And Wrong) About EVs, According To An Executive
Toyota's North American product planning boss is feeling vindicated right now.
The product planners at Toyota Motor North America headquarters in Plano, Texas, are feeling pretty hot right now. As competitors slash EV plans—and as longtime rival Honda suffers through its first-ever loss as a public company—Toyota’s hybrid-heavy lineup is printing cash. The company is, as ever, the most profitable automaker in the world. After years of criticism for its tepid embrace of pure electric vehicles, it looks vindicated.
So Cooper Ericksen seemed to be riding high when I walked into his office. Ericksen is TMNA’s senior vice president of product, battery electric vehicles, and mobility planning and strategy, giving him a wide remit and a tough gig. But for now, at least, his plan seems to be paying off. Americans can’t seem to get enough Toyota hybrids, and the company’s EV lineup is finally expanding and improving to boot.
The Toyota RAV4—the world's bestselling vehicle—has gone hybrid-only for 2026. That's a big part of Toyota's strategy.
(Full Disclosure: Toyota flew me to its North American headquarters in Plano, Texas, to sit in on its Electrification 101 employee education program. While I was there, I got the opportunity to sit down with Ericksen.)
Getting that timing right wasn’t easy.
“EVs have been a roller coaster ride in many, many ways,” Ericksen told me in a recent interview. “I'm product planning. So, I'm looking at five to 10 years out and five to 10 years back, trying to figure out when's the right time to enter the market. When is it too soon? When is it too late?”
Those aren’t easy questions. Most automakers overshot demand, banking on a quick transition that didn’t materialize. They may not have had a choice: Regulators were putting the squeeze on emissions, and if you didn’t have hybrids to help, you probably needed to build a lot of EVs. Now the U.S. regulations have been rolled back, giving automakers more maneuvering room. Most of them are scrambling; Toyota isn’t, Ericksen said.
“We're sticking to our strategy, and it's gratifying that the strategy is working well,” he told me. “The basic customer benefits of our portfolio is we have a little bit of something for everybody, and right now the big winner is our hybrid powertrains.”
The Camry is also only available as a hybrid. Toyota now says that half of its sales in the U.S. are electrified, with the vast majority of those electrified models being traditional hybrids.
Getting The Demand Picture Right
Toyota has taken a lot of heat over the years for its slow-moving approach to EVs. The company has said that it is pursuing a “multi-pathway” approach to electrification, focusing on widely deploying hybrids while investing in EVs and hydrogen for the future.
That means it’s been less aggressive in pushing EVs to date, and less bullish on their outlook in the marketplace. That’s for a simple reason, according to Ericksen: Customer demand isn’t there yet, and “we follow the customer.”
He rejected the idea that “everyone wants a BEV” right now, saying “lies in the marketplace” underestimated practical concerns and real consumer resistance. Based on the real-world data of the last few years, he said, it’s clear that consumers are still hesitant. And while EV fans point to sales that—until the tax credit and regulatory rollback last year—were rapidly growing, he argues those were driven heavily by incentives from both the government and automakers.
He said that in the tax-credit days, many car companies were spending between $10,000 and $20,000 per EV on incentives. Combine that with $7,500 from the federal government, or more if you factor in incentives on the manufacturing side, and these were heavily subsidized vehicles. Ericksen says in total, many EV sales involved $20,000 to $30,000 in manufacturer and government incentives.
Automakers piled incentives onto EVs in the last couple of years to meet emissions targets, leading to some crazy deals.
“The actual customer demand can't be looked at through that lens,” he told me. “We sell 450,000 RAV4s a year at $36,000 each. If we put $30,000 of incentive money on RAV4, we could probably sell 5 million.”
Even still, market penetration peaked at 9%, a sign, he argues, that few customers are willing to buy these vehicles at a profitable price point. The reality, he says, is that customers have real practical concerns.
They don’t know about the reliability of EVs, they don’t know how to handle charging, and they don’t want the price premium. Toyota has been through this before, as consumers had many of the same concerns about hybrids when they first arrived, he noted. The company solved that through methodical improvement and consistency, but it’s taken over 20 years for hybrids to go from super niche to 16% of the market. EVs have a long road, too, and it starts with addressing the customer concerns, he said.
The new Toyota bZ Woodland is a lot more practical than its competitors, with far more cargo space than the similarly sized Chevy Blazer EV and Honda Prologue (RIP).
“What does the product need to be? Products are an art of compromise, right? You can never have everything you want in a vehicle. So what are you willing to compromise on? And where are the customers at?,” he said. “So from that perspective, yeah, EVs have been a huge challenge. I've read your company's articles over the years, and I've questioned my own sanity if we were doing the right thing or not.”
These days, he seems much more sure of it. But that doesn’t mean the road has been easy.
Not Getting The Product Right
Critics have piled onto Toyota for being slow to roll out EVs, and for lobbying against policies that would accelerate EV adoption—all while claiming to highly value reducing carbon emissions. But more than the pace and the politics, InsideEVs and countless other outlets have criticized the company for delivering EVs that feel underbaked. The company’s first modern, mass-market EV, the bZ4X, had lackluster range, bad charging performance, missing features for EV life, and little competitive edge. The company was already late to the party; showing up underdressed didn’t help.
Even Ericksen admits that it wasn’t the brand’s finest moment.
The original Toyota bZ4X was pretty uncompetitive. It had low range, bad charging specs, and few EV-specific features.
“You know, the first bZ didn't have as much product power as we wanted it to,” Ericksen said. “Your articles documented that quite fairly. Frankly, I might not have liked to read them, but you weren't wrong.”
The process taught Toyota that, while there’s a relatively small proportion of the customer base that’s ready to go fully electric, it’s a passionate group. EV buyers tend to love their cars, and love the fuel savings. Thanks to steady improvements, too, the products have gotten a lot better. The new bZ goes farther, charges faster, and has better software. The company may still be lagging on that last point; its latest cars still lack EV route planning, which has become pretty much industry-standard. But with a bunch of new EVs on sale and more in the hopper, it’s looking more serious than ever in this space.
Putting It All Together
Toyota always planned to ramp up EV production. But because it was more conservative, it’s not having to massively rewrite its plans in this new policy landscape. Most competitors can’t say the same. Toyota just launched the new C-HR and bZ Woodland EVs, along with the refreshed bZ and the new Lexus ES EV. Three-row Toyota Highlander and Lexus TZs are slated to arrive soon, and Ericksen said those large SUVs will “create another plateau” for Toyota’s EV business.
“The next few years will be exciting,” Ericksen said. “By 2030, are we going to be 7, 8, 9, 10% BEV? Somewhere around 10%? Yeah, probably. Which for us is not a small number.”
That’s perhaps a less optimistic timeline than many of Toyota’s competitors. But Ericksen and Toyota are used to that. They have proven out their theory that being cautious can pay off. Toyota has profitably weathered a situation that has utterly battered most of its peers. Executives have every reason to feel good.
The 2027 Lexus TZ and Toyota Highlander will be Toyota's first three-row EVs. They're built in America, too.
But the job isn’t done. Toyota has proven that it can maintain its position as the world’s most profitable car company through hundred-year storms. But if it wants to keep that title in decades to come, it needs to eventually match and surpass EV offerings from startups, Chinese automakers, and other legacy brands alike. Toyota executives project confidence that the company can pull it off. Now the company has to prove it.

title: BYD Will Put Solid-State Batteries In An EV Next Year: Executive
content:
In a recent interview, BYD's Stella Li said that the company will "have one model" with solid-state batteries next year.
Photo by:
3:15pm ET
Solid-state batteries are poised to be the next big leap in battery technology. They're lighter and safer, with greater energy density and faster charging capability. So why hasn't every automaker switched over? Companies are still working out the kinks and figuring out how to mass-produce
solid-state batteries
However, BYD is apparently making strides. BYD Executive Vice President Stella Li said recently that the company will make its first solid-state vehicle next year.
"Talking about solid-state batteries, BYD is in the leading position," Li told
. "So to prove that, next year we will have one model, the first model, with this technology."
It wasn't clear whether she was referring to an actual retail launch or a demonstration vehicle. Given how quickly Chinese automakers—and BYD in particular—move to integrate new tech, it very well could be the former. Showing off a prototype and waiting years to put it into production doesn't seem to be the company's style.
Photo by: BYD
Li didn't say which model might get such a battery, or exactly when it will launch. However, sources for
CarNewsChina
claim that BYD will launch its solid-state tech in its recently teased Yangwang flagship sedan. The monster sedan BYD showed off in camouflage last week is said to be massively luxurious, something with Rolls-Royce levels of opulence. Given that it's as long as a school bus and has a Phantom-like silhouette, I don't doubt the claim. That would be a fitting vehicle with which to launch solid-state tech, given its cost in these early days.
The latest and greatest tech has always been introduced in pricey flagship models, so if BYD doesn't use the new Yangwang sedan, expect it to still be in something expensive, like the
Denza Z9
BYD Great Tang
BYD may have competition relatively quickly, though.
plans to launch an EV with solid-state tech in 2027 or 2028.
says it'll have the same tech closer to 2030, and the same goes for Mercedes.
Hyundai continues to work on it
, too. Either way, American customers will likely have to wait for a non-Chinese automaker to bring solid-state batteries to market.

title: EVgo Is Supercharging Its Network With 750 kW EV Chargers
content:
EVgo Is Supercharging Its Network With 750 kW EV Chargers
The new stalls will support dynamic power sharing, and the company wants its new stations to feature more NACS ports.
- EVgo, one of the biggest EV charging networks in the U.S., is working on deploying more powerful chargers.
- The company’s next-generation system will be capable of delivering up to 750 kW of power.
- The new stalls will dynamically allocate power to connected EVs.
EVgo, one of the largest public EV charging networks in the United States, is gearing up to install fast chargers that are twice as powerful as its current offerings. The company’s next-generation system will be capable of delivering up to 750 kilowatts, up from the current maximum of 350 kW.
The operator, which is one of the few in the country that has the facilities and expertise to build its own hardware, is currently designing, developing, and testing the new chargers at its Innovation Lab in El Segundo, California.
A teaser for EVgo's new 750 kW EV charger
There’s still a lot we don’t know about EVgo’s newest DC fast chargers, including their design, but the company has let a few details slip between its fingers. First, the new stalls will feature a touchless payment interface, enabling drivers to pay for charging without having to download a smartphone app.
Second, the new hardware will integrate dynamic power sharing, which means that each connected EV will get the most power it can handle. In other words, if a Lucid Gravity and a Tesla Model 3 share the same stall, both of them should get the maximum output, with 400 kW going to the Gravity and 250 kW going to the Model 3.
It also means that EVgo is future-proofing its network. Right now, there are precisely zero EVs sold in the United States that can accept 750 kW, but times are changing, and there are plenty of electric cars overseas that can take in 1,000 kW or more without skipping a beat. Until that happens, EVgo’s new chargers should be a good fit for electric trucks, which need massive amounts of power to replenish their huge batteries in a relatively short amount of time. Whether or not the stations will be built to accommodate big rigs is another story, though.
That being said, EVgo will boost the deployment of NACS ports at its new stations, as it looks to double its addressable market in the near future.
It’s all quite impressive, but what does it actually mean for America’s EV drivers? Well, according to the company, its new 750 kW system is expected to enable 10-minute charging sessions for the fastest charging vehicles in the country.
This is all good news. Even though America has fallen behind the rest of the developed world in terms of vehicle electrification, there’s still a solid selection of fast-charging EVs being offered, all of which can benefit from EVgo’s new high-powered stalls.
We’ll know more about the 750 kW system next year, when the final design will be unveiled, and the first deployments will go online.
EVgo operates nearly 2,000 DC fast charging stations across the United States, offering over 5,300 individual ports, according to the Department of Energy's Alternative Fuels Data Center (AFDC).

title: Fuel Economy Rollback Will Burn Billions More Gallons Of Gas, Trump Administration Says
content:
Fuel Economy Rollback Will Burn Billions More Gallons Of Gas, Trump Administration Says
The public health and environmental costs of the revised fuel economy standards could be colossal.
- The U.S. Department of Transportation has sharply reduced the fuel economy targets for automakers.
- Car companies now have to hit 34.9 mpg across their fleets by 2031.
- It's the latest moved aimed at reversing Biden-era policies that were addressing climate change.
The Trump administration dealt America’s electric vehicle industry another setback Monday, finalizing far less stringent Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) rules than those set during the Biden era. The ruling comes at a time when Europe, China, and much of the developing world are racing forward with EV adoption, leaving the U.S. in the rearview mirror.
Under the new standards, set by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), automakers must hit 34.9 miles per gallon across their light-duty fleets by 2031, down from the 50.4 mpg benchmark set under Biden. That's only a slight increase from the 2024 target of 30.4 mpg. Many hybrids and plug-in hybrids on sale today are already much more efficient than the new figure.
The NHTSA said the new CAFE standards would reduce the average up-front vehicle cost by $1,290, since automakers could pivot to using less expensive engine tech rather than efficiency-improving innovations and EVs. It added that the 34.9 mpg target is only an estimation and it expects real-world fuel economy to be 20-30% lower, depending on the mix of powertrain automakers actually end up selling by that time.
In an 892-page rule, the agency also acknowledged that the revised standards would dramatically increase fuel consumption and result in more harmful emissions getting pumped into the atmosphere.
The environmental and public-health impacts could potentially be catastrophic, judging by the Trump administration's own analysis. The NHTSA said the final rule could cause an increase in emissions by 2035 equivalent to about 17 million additional vehicles on the road.
“Adverse health outcomes from criteria pollutant emissions are expected to increase nationwide in 2035 and 2050 under all action alternatives relative to the No-Action Alternative,” NHTSA said.
The agency added that the emissions of a harmful chemical called fomaldehyde could increase by as much as 12.6%. NHTSA also included comments from other organizations in the ruling, saying the National Resources Defense Council and some other agencies project CO2 emissions to increase by one billion metric tons by 2050.
“Higher emissions would be expected to lead to an overall increase in adverse health effects while lower emissions would be expected to lead to a decrease in adverse health effects,” NHTSA said. It added that the final ruling will cause surface temperatures to rise, in addition to higher CO2 concentrations, and rising sea levels. The impact wouldn’t just affect the U.S. but would also “occur on a global scale.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy argued that the new rules will make cars cheaper.
“Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, we have finally ended the illegal mandate that forced automakers to produce more expensive electric vehicles that American families didn’t want," Duffy said.
The stricter rules did not amount to an EV mandate. But they would have nudged automakers to sell a mix of EVs, hybrids, plug-in hybrids, and more efficient combustion cars, reducing the effects of air pollution and helping car buyers save money at the pump. Transportation accounts for the largest share of greenhouse gas emissions in the U.S., and it’s directly linked to respiratory illnesses, lung disease, and other adverse health impacts.
Under the new CAFE rules, automakers are now incentivized to continue selling more gas cars, trucks, and SUVs over fuel efficient models and EVs. They join a string of other anti-EV measures the Trump administration has enacted, including terminating the $7,500 federal tax credit and eliminating the penalties automakers historically had to pay for not complying to CAFE standards. Practically speaking, the CAFE rules were already defanged before today's rollback.
The Alliance For Automotive Innovation, the lobbying group representing major automakers in the U.S. including Ford, GM, and BMW, praised the revised CAFE rules. "The standards finalized under the previous administration effectively required a switchover to electric vehicles that was out of step with market realities and customer demand," John Bozzella, the organization's president and CEO, said in a statement.
Katherine Garcia, director of the Sierra Club's Clean Transportation for All campaign, slammed the new rules. "Less fuel-efficient cars mean more gas burned, spending more at the pump, and dirtier air in our communities," Garcia said. "Americans need relief from high costs, but instead Trump is giving automakers a free pass on pollution and handing families the bill—at the pump and with their health."
The potential outcomes noted by the NHTSA are not guaranteed. Automakers could choose to sell more fuel efficient vehicles and EVs anyway, especially if demand rebounds in the coming years. There is clearly strong interest in hybrids, in particular, which hit a record share of 16.3% of the vehicle market in the second quarter despite the looser regulations.
A future administration could also reinstate more stringent fuel economy rules that encourage more EV adoption. But that could take years, and cars sold under the weaker standards will be around for decades. All the extra fuel burned and pollution created in the interim can't simply be reversed when the political tides shift.
