title: Juniper Green adds 100 MWh of storage in India on existing grid link - Energy Storage
content: Juniper Green Energy has expanded the Bikaner-II project in Rajasthan, India, with 100 MWh of additional BESS capacity, bringing the site’s commissioned storage capacity to 201 MWh. The additional capacity was commissioned through the company’s wholly owned subsidiary, Juniper Green Cosmic, within the project’s existing grid connectivity. The company said the recently issued regulatory clarity from the Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. allows addition of storage capacity without increasing the grid connectivity quantum, thereby ensuring optimal utilization of existing transmission infrastructure. This allows the company to add incremental storage capacity in a capital-efficient manner. The capacity will initially operate on a merchant basis, enabling Juniper Green to participate in India’s evolving energy storage market and capture value from the growing requirement for flexibility and grid balancing. “Commissioning an additional 100 MWh of BESS within the existing grid connectivity at Bikaner-II is a strong example of how we are looking to maximise the value of our existing infrastructure,” said Ankush Malik, whole-time director and CEO of Juniper Green Energy. “Taking the project’s commissioned storage capacity to 201 MWh gives us additional merchant capacity without requiring incremental grid connectivity, creating a new avenue to participate in the power market. We see this approach as an important part of building a more commercially flexible storage portfolio alongside our long-term contracted renewable assets.” Juniper Green Energy Ltd. is an independent renewable energy power producer in India, focused on the development, construction, and operation of utility-scale solar, wind, hybrid, and firm and dispatchable renewable energy projects. It has an operational capacity of approximately 2.7 GWp and 603 MWh BESS and a total portfolio (including operational, under-construction, contracted, and awarded projects) of more than 11 GWp and 8.9 GWh BESS. title: Promigas advances 2.2 GWh of solar-linked storage in Chile - Energy Storage
content: Regional environmental commissions in Chile have approved two solar-plus-storage projects. Pampino, in the northern Tarapacá region, pairs 170 MW of solar capacity with 1,020 MWh of storage, while Monterrico Solar, in the Ñuble region, combines 248.73 MWp of solar with a 200 MW/1,200 MWh lithium-ion battery providing six hours of storage. The two projects have a combined declared investment of $569 million. Both were developed by Zelestra, whose Latin American business was acquired by Colombian energy company Promigas in May. The Tarapacá Environmental Evaluation Commission approved Pampino at its ordinary session. The project, held for permitting purposes by Pampino Solar, will be built in Pozo Almonte, in the province of Tamarugal. According to its environmental impact declaration, Pampino has a declared investment of $263 million and will occupy 467 hectares. It will connect to Chile’s National Electric System (SEN) through two 1.5 km, 220 kV lines to a new PAM1 switching substation, which will section the existing Lagunas-Collahuasi transmission line. Construction is scheduled to begin on June 1, 2028, and the project has an estimated operating life of 37.1 years. It is expected to employ an average of 600 people during construction, peaking at 800, and an average of seven during operation, with a maximum of 30. Pampino entered Chile’s environmental assessment process in September 2025. The Ñuble Environmental Evaluation Commission approved Monterrico Solar at its ordinary session the same day. The project, held for permitting purposes by Unión Solar SpA, will be located in the municipalities of Coihueco and Chillán. Monterrico Solar will have 248.73 MWp of installed solar capacity and 200 MW of nominal capacity, using 404,433 bifacial monocrystalline silicon modules rated at 615 Wp each. Electricity will be exported through a 12.3 km, 220 kV line energized at 154 kV to the Monterrico substation. The project has a declared investment of $306 million. Construction is scheduled to begin on Dec. 1, 2026, with connection to the SEN expected in June 2028 and an estimated operating life of 35 years. It is expected to employ an average of 150 people during construction, peaking at 400, and an average of 10 during operation, with a maximum of 20. Zelestra submitted Monterrico Solar for environmental assessment in March 2025. Zelestra completed the sale of its entire Latin American business to Promigas on May 28, 2026, in a transaction valued at about $1.1 billion. The deal covered operating, under-construction, and development assets in Chile, Peru, and Colombia, with a total portfolio of about 3.5 GW. Promigas said the platform included 1,273 MW of projects in operation and under construction and about 2,250 MW in development, spanning solar and energy storage. title: A gas utility is picking up the upfront tab for geothermal
content:
Geothermal
Michelle Lewis
| Oct 1 2026 - 5:00 am PT
Photos courtesy of Dandelion Energy (c) 2026
Geothermal’s upfront cost can be a dealbreaker for affordable housing. A Vermont gas utility is helping get past that hurdle by paying for the underground infrastructure at a new development.
Vermont Gas (VGS) and Dandelion Energy are bringing geothermal heating and cooling to Riggs Meadow in Hinesburg, Vermont. The development will include 44 townhomes and apartments for low- and moderate-income renters and owners.
VGS will pay upfront for and own the underground pipes, known as ground loops. That takes a substantial installation expense off the affordable housing developers’ plate. Dandelion will handle the geothermal work, including system design and drilling.
Champlain Housing Trust and Evernorth, Riggs Meadow’s affordable housing developers, explored heating and cooling options with VGS before bringing Dandelion into the project.
April announcement
, VGS said geothermal would serve four multifamily buildings containing 36 of the development’s homes. Each building would have its own ground loop.
Here’s how it works
: Electric ground-source heat pumps use fluid circulating through underground pipes to move heat between the ground and the buildings. In winter, they bring heat from the ground indoors. In summer, they send heat from the homes underground. Temperatures below ground stay relatively steady, helping the system work efficiently through Vermont’s cold winters and hot summers.
The interesting part is who’s picking up the upfront tab. Developers would typically have to find the money for that underground infrastructure themselves. In this case, VGS is taking on the expense, making geothermal easier to include in affordable housing while giving the gas utility a way to offer all-electric heating and cooling.
“This partnership with utilities like VGS helps us expand geothermal access and continues to help us make this a standard, mainstream solution for developers and builders,” said Dan Yates, CEO of Dandelion Energy. “Utility-owned ground loops are a practical, immediate solution to decarbonize housing. We are proud to support and validate this model that aligns utility infrastructure investment with equitable, clean energy access.”
Under VGS’s broader geothermal offering through
Clover Energy
, the utility owns and maintains the underground infrastructure. Customers own the equipment inside the buildings and pay a monthly fee to use the ground loops, but what that fee will be at Riggs Meadow or how much residents can expect to pay for heating and cooling hasn’t yet been disclosed.
“Geothermal is one of the best solutions we have to make cost-effective, renewable heating and cooling options accessible to more Vermonters,” said Neale Lunderville, president & CEO of VGS. “We are thrilled to partner with Dandelion Energy to demonstrate ways geothermal can be scaled to meet community needs. As Vermont looks to rapidly build housing to meet demand, our teams are eager to incorporate geothermal into our product portfolio to give more choices to homebuilders and customers.”
Drilling is scheduled to begin in early 2027, and residents are expected to move into the homes in late 2027.

title: Aptera (SEV) now says it needs $25M to start production, stock drops 15%
content:
Aptera (SEV) now says it needs only about $25 million to start production of its Solar EV, down from the $40 to $45 million it quoted just seven weeks ago.
It’s good news on paper. But the market didn’t buy it: Aptera’s stock fell about 15% on the announcement, leaving the solar car startup with a market cap of roughly $69 million.
A smaller number, same problem
In its Q2 2026 results in August, Aptera said it needed $40 to $45 million to launch low-volume production at its Carlsbad facility, plus another $140 to $160 million to reach high volume.
The new plan, published today, is a lot leaner:
- About $25 million to start production, with the first 40 vehicles built starting by the end of 2026
- $40 million more to ramp to 500 vehicles per month, which Aptera calls self-sustaining
- $50 million more for high-volume tooling, targeting about 20,000 vehicles a year
That’s roughly $115 million all-in, compared to $180 to $205 million before. Aptera credits its recent partnership with Launch Design, design-for-manufacturing changes, international suppliers, and a bill of materials updated with actual supplier quotes.
“This is a fundamentally leaner path to getting Aptera into customers’ hands,” said co-CEO Chris Anthony.
Customer deliveries are now pegged for early 2027, “subject to financing.”
The goalposts keep moving
We’ve heard versions of this before. In late 2024, Aptera was trying to raise $60 million to reach low-volume production and called its delivery timeline a “moving target.” Back then, the first 60 Launch Edition cars were supposed to ship in 2025.
In January, after a $9 million public offering at $2 per share, the company was still targeting customer deliveries in 2026. That’s now 2027.
And the cash position is thin. Aptera had $10.1 million in the bank at the end of June and burns $2 to $2.2 million a month on baseline operations, according to its 10-Q, which carries a going-concern warning. It raised another $6 million through a warrant deal in July and has a $75 million equity line of credit, though drawing on it means selling shares into a market that keeps marking them down.
So even $25 million is a big ask. It’s more than a third of what the entire company is worth on the stock market today.
The product is still the good part
None of this changes what makes the Aptera interesting. It’s a two-seat, three-wheeled EV so efficient that the solar panels on its body actually matter. TÜV Rheinland measured up to 4.75 kWh a day from the integrated solar in sunny conditions, which works out to around 40 miles of daily driving without plugging in.
Top comment by Beario
In the beginning I had hopes that this concept would take off. I still have hopes that it will somehow survive, but it is looking less and less likely. It is a great concept for a super efficient vehicle, but looking at what it is up against as time goes on and as other models come to market makes the likelihood seem more and more out of reach. Still a compelling concept though that still has a possibility and hopefully things can get off the ground.
Aptera also got its EPA Certificate of Conformity in June and has ordered bodies and chassis for the first 40 vehicles. It reports about 49,300 reservations.
Electrek’s Take
We love the Aptera concept. Make a car efficient enough and rooftop solar goes from a gimmick to a real fuel source. Lightyear and Sono Motors both tried and ran out of money before getting there. Aptera is the last serious attempt standing, and the TÜV numbers back up the concept.
But a cheaper plan is only good news if someone funds it. Aptera has struggled to raise money at almost any amount for two years now, and every raise dilutes shareholders further. The market’s 15% reaction tells you investors read today’s update as Aptera having no other way than dillute their ownership in order to get to production.

content:

forklifts
Jo Borrás

A fresh batch of battery-electric forklift reveals from Hyundai completes the brand’s heavy forklift range, allowing Hyundai dealers to confidently offer a high-voltage electric counterbalance forklift in 4-to-18 tonne capacities, extending electric forklift availability into applications traditionally reserved for big, diesel-powered trucks.
Hyundai launched its B-X line with 4-9 tonne models back in 2025
, but the latest additions, comprising the 100B-X, 120B-X, and 130B-X LC600 models come together with the 16-tonne (about 18 short ton) class 160B-X and 180B-X (shown, above, and shipping to customers now) to complete the range, and bring high-voltage battery electric forklifts solutions to applications requiring higher lifting capacities and intensive outdoor and
operation.
“Completing the B-X range means that electrification is no longer limited to the lower-capacity forklift segments,” explains Raymond Galavazi, Senior Product Manager at Hyundai Material Handling. “
Customers across a wide range of industries can now consider high-voltage electric trucks from 4-18 tonnes
, also for demanding outdoor applications where high capacity and intensive operation are required.”
Handle with care
Safety first; by Hyundai.
The 160B-X packs a massive 618V high-voltage lithium-ion battery and electrical system that probably pulls double-duty as part of the truck’s counterweight (Hyundai doesn’t say so,
but come on
), while delivering more than 7 hours of continuous operation on a single charge.
And, because moving 16
tonnes of
anything
around a jobsite makes keeping people alive a constant challenge, Hyundai has loaded up the B-X with intelligent safety tech that includes camera-based pedestrian detection, delicate load sensing, Blue Spot and Red Zone lighting, autonomous parking, and operator-presence protection that shuts down travel and mast functions whenever the driver leaves the seat.
Hyundai is light on capacity and specs, but promises, “rapid charging capability,” which leads me to believe this is intended to be less of a warehouse EV and more of a hefty-style, heavy-duty electric workhorse.
To that end, Hyundai says its big B-X trucks were developed, “specifically for sectors where diesel forklifts remain widely used, including ports, shipbuilding, timber processing, metal production, construction materials,
manufacturing and logistics operations

all environments where EVs have been able to outperform diesel

title: Ford's $30,000 Fathom EV pickup production launch faces uncertainty [Update]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 1 2026 - 7:37 am PT
Ford Fathom
is expected to go on sale in early 2027, starting at $28,350. Ford CEO Jim Farley admitted, “It’s going to be a heck of an effort to launch this at scale, at cost, on time.”
Ford Fathom production still faces hurdles
After Ford said just last month it was
on track to begin Fathom production
in 2027, that timeline is now facing uncertainty.
Speaking at the
2026 Automotive News Congress
this week, Ford CEO Jim Farley explained how its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform could be the automaker’s answer to Chinese brands like BYD, which are rapidly gaining market share in Europe and other key global markets.
Farley said the company realized at one point that a BYD EV would have roughly a 20% cost advantage over Fathom’s battery.
To stay competitive, the team modified the motors, gearboxes, and inverters, enabling smaller batteries than BYD’s.
While it sounds promising, Farley admitted that “It’s going to be a heck of an effort to launch this at scale, at cost, on time.”
Ford Fathom EV pickup prototype (Source: Jim Farley)
Farley added that “We haven’t landed the plane on mass production of UEV yet.” Ford previously said the first Fathom prototypes are scheduled to roll off the assembly line at its 3-million-square-foot Louisville Assembly Plant (LAP) in 2027.
Ford is investing $5 billion between its Louisville Assembly Plant and BlueOval Battery Park in Michigan to prepare for UEV production.
Covered Ford Fathom vehicle (Source: Ford)

title: Gazelle just made its premium electric bikes a lot more affordable
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 1 2026 - 5:38 am PT
Gazelle has spent much of its recent e-bike development pushing its premium Ultimate platform
toward faster Class 3 commuters
, but now the Dutch bicycle maker is filling out the other side of the family.
The company has launched three new Class 1 versions of its Ultimate e-bike: the Ultimate T10, Ultimate C5, and Ultimate C380. All three are limited to pedal assist and are aimed more at recreational riders and everyday commuters who don’t necessarily need the higher speeds of Gazelle’s Ultimate Speed models.
And perhaps most importantly, they bring the Ultimate platform down to a slightly more approachable starting price of $3,499.
That still isn’t exactly bargain e-bike territory, but
has never really played in the race-to-the-bottom end of the market. These are Dutch-built e-bikes using Bosch drive systems, backed by a large dealer network, and designed more as long-term transportation than something that arrives in a cardboard box with a baggie of mystery bolts. Their high-end models have traditionally been a fair bit pricier, so these new figures are actually on the much more affordable end for anything nice enough to be badged a Gazelle.
All three new bikes use the same redesigned Ultimate platform and geometry found on the Class 3 Ultimate Speed models introduced earlier this year. That includes an active-but-upright riding position, wider tires, a suspension seatpost, and an air-sprung suspension fork. There’s also an internally mounted 540Wh Bosch battery, with the option to upgrade to an 800Wh battery or add Bosch’s PowerMore 250 range extender.
The bikes also get Bosch Smart System integration, either Kiox or Purion displays depending on the model, and Gazelle’s Intellimount system for mounting a smartphone to the stem. Integrated brake lights brighten automatically under deceleration in another nod to safety.
The $3,499 Ultimate T10 serves as the new entry point. It uses a Shimano CUES 10-speed drivetrain paired with Bosch’s latest Active Line Plus mid-drive motor, now producing 60 Nm of torque – 10 Nm more than before.
Spend another $500 and you get the $3,999 Ultimate C5, which is a new model for the North American market. This one swaps the conventional derailleur drivetrain for a Gates carbon belt drive and Shimano Nexus 5-speed internally geared hub. That’s a combination I generally prefer on utility-focused e-bikes: fewer greasy components hanging off the rear wheel and less maintenance to worry about.
At the top of the new Class 1 range is the $4,499 Ultimate C380. It also uses a Gates belt drive but pairs it with an Enviolo continuously variable transmission, providing stepless shifting instead of traditional gears. The C380 also gets Bosch’s Kiox display with onboard navigation.
There’s an interesting broader trend here, too. While much of the North American e-bike industry seems obsessed with adding more motor power, bigger batteries, throttles, and increasingly motorcycle-ish designs, Gazelle is effectively moving in the opposite direction.
These are still fairly sophisticated machines, but the premise is refreshingly bicycle-like: you pedal, the motor helps, and the whole thing is designed to feel like a really nice bicycle rather than a lightweight electric motorcycle pretending to be one.
The new Ultimate T10, C5, and C380 are available now through Gazelle dealers in the US and Canada.

title: A Cheap BMW Neue Klasse EV Is Coming In 2028
content:
A Cheap BMW Neue Klasse EV Is Coming In 2028
The entry-level electric car is part of BMW’s turnaround plan, which also includes a big gas SUV for the U.S.
- BMW confirmed it will reveal a mass-market EV based on the Neue Klasse platform.
- The car doesn’t have a name yet, but it’s likely going to be called the i1.
- The entry-level EV is part of BMW’s plan to boost margins, which includes a high-end gas SUV for the American market.
BMW poured billions of dollars into the development of its Neue Klasse platform, and it’s not going to stop with just two models. After the iX3 and i3, an entry-level Neue Klasse EV is coming in 2028, the company confirmed yesterday.
The mass-market electric car, which is expected to be a compact hatchback wearing the i1 badge, will debut in Europe, where it will slot between the battery-powered Mini Cooper and the upcoming BMW iX1 crossover.
The upcoming i1 (name unconfirmed) is expected to borrow the same design language as the i3 pictured here.
Based on the same underpinnings as the long-range i3, the new i1 will probably stick to a rear-wheel-drive setup, but dual-motor configurations are also possible. That’s the same as the first two generations of the 1 Series. Speaking of the 1 Series, the latest generation, which is front-wheel drive, will reportedly stay in production until early next decade, so BMW will have two entry-level offerings with different powertrains.
The new electric five-door hatchback is known internally as the “NB0,” according to insiders quoted by BMW Blog. Despite being similar in size to the 1 Series, the two cars will be completely different under the skin. Technical specifications are nowhere to be found right now, but logic dictates that the upcoming i1 will have a smaller-capacity battery than the recently introduced i3.
The electric sedan is available with a 108.7- or an 82.8-kilowatt-hour battery, but with a shorter wheelbase, the i1 will probably have less space for a huge battery. But a smaller body and a smaller battery have a big upside: lower weight. Even with less energy capacity, the i1 should have enough usable range for daily driving.
Charging performance is also expected to take a hit compared to the i3, which can accept 300 or 400 kilowatts, depending on the battery size. That’s what usually happens with entry-level models, but we’ll know for sure when the official specs are released.
As much as I’d love to see an electric BMW i1 in the United States, that’s probably never going to happen. The German automaker was clear that the new mass-market EV is designed for the European market, which can’t get enough of affordable electric hatchbacks right now.
For America, BMW is studying a high-end SUV that’s expected to sit above the X7 and be powered by gas engines. Both the flagship SUV and the entry-level EV are part of the company’s plan to boost its margins to as much as 10% by early next decade.
But launching two new cars isn’t enough, so BMW is also making workforce cuts and plans to use more artificial intelligence across all areas of the company to boost efficiency.

title: FedEx Just Ordered 2,000 Electric Trucks That Will Save $40 Million Every Year On Fuel
content:
FedEx Just Ordered 2,000 Electric Trucks That Will Save $40 Million Every Year On Fuel
The package delivery company will deploy Harbinger’s American-made EVs in the United States and Canada.
- FedEx is replacing 2,000 diesel-powered trucks with brand-new EVs.
- The medium-duty electric trucks will be supplied by Harbinger, an American startup that builds its vehicles in California.
- The vehicles will be deployed in the United States and Canada by the end of 2027.
American package delivery giant FedEx will replace 2,000 of its combustion-powered delivery vehicles with all-electric trucks built by Harbinger in the United States.
The EVs will hit the road in Canada and the U.S. by the end of next year, with Harbinger estimating that they’ll save FedEx a whopping $40 million every year in fuel costs. The 2,000 medium-duty trucks, which cost over $200 million, are engineered for a 20-year service life, during which the total fuel savings should amount to $800 million, according to the California startup.
At the same time, by cutting down on diesel consumption, FedEx’s new trucks are expected to avoid over 1.7 million tons of carbon dioxide from going into the atmosphere over their operating lives.
This is FedEx’s biggest order of Harbinger electric trucks, after last year’s initial order for 53 Class 5 and Class 6 models. It’s part of the delivery company’s goal of electrifying its entire pickup and delivery fleet by 2040.
Assembled in California, Harbinger’s electric Class 5 and Class 6 trucks are available in three wheelbase lengths, from 158 inches to 208 inches. They’re powered by an all-in-one electric drive unit that houses the motor, transmission, and differential. Developed in-house by Harbinger, the EDU delivers 440 horsepower and 1,140 pound-feet of torque.
The startup also engineered a 35-kilowatt-hour battery pack rated at 800 volts that can be configured in four-to-six-pack setups, enabling a real-world range between 140 miles and 210 miles on a full charge. According to the truck maker, a 20-to-80% charge takes less than an hour on a DC fast charger.
Harbinger says the main selling points of its step-van are affordability, with prices starting at $103,000 before incentives, durability, and best-in-class 50-degree wheel cut and 42-foot turning diameter. The company also offers a range-extender setup with a 1.4-liter gas engine acting as a generator, which was recently selected as the U.S. Army’s next-gen uncrewed ground vehicle (UGV), but FedEx’s order includes a mix of models from the manufacturer’s all-electric vehicle lineup.
Rivian's electric van is cheaper, with a starting price of $79,900, but it's also smaller and has a lower 9,500-pound gross vehicle weight rating, whereas Harbinger's GVWR ranges between 16,000 and 26,000 lbs.
According to Harbinger, all 2,000 vehicles will be built and delivered in the next 18 months.

title: Ford CEO Thinks Its 'Too Late' For Europe To Take On Chinese Automakers
content:
Unsurprisingly, he still thinks Ford has a chance to compete. But he needs time.
Photo by:
3:53pm ET
Ford CEO Jim Farley wants the U.S. to approach Chinese automakers with caution. Farley claims we should take the opposite approach than what Europe has, and not allow Chinese automakers to sell here just yet. According to him, it's "too late" for Europe, as the massive influx of Chinese EVs has made it incredibly difficult for European brands to compete.
“I think it’s just important for us to take our time, to be considerate,” Farley said at the Automotive News Congress in Detroit, according to
. “I watch what’s happening in Europe right now, where that was not the case, and it’s really something that they have to deal with now, and it’s too late.”
There's no denying just how rapidly Chinese automakers are entering new markets and eating up market share. It's tough to compete with their impressive range figures and low price points. The global market share for Chinese EVs has reportedly risen 70%, per
. In Europe, Chinese EVs are said to make up 12% of the market and their market share is as high as 25% in Mexico, according to Farley.
Photo by: MIIT
It isn't just market domination, though. Farley mentioned that a massive influx of Chinese vehicles into the U.S. could pose national security issues, saying that they can "take videos of everything," according to
Autoblog
This comes after
Ford partnered with Chinese auto giant Geely
to build vehicles in Spain and took fire from the government for a
project with Chinese battery giant CATL
. But Farley claims that it can both work with Chinese automakers and compete against them. “Our answer is pretty simple. We’re going to partner with the Chinese where we don’t have [intellectual property], where we can be more capital efficient in places like Europe or Southeast Asia,” he said at the Automotive News conference. At the same time, Ford wants to compete with China.
This news also comes shortly after the
Trump administration
claimed that it could start to allow some Chinese EVs into the U.S., as long as they're built here. That goes against the bill approved by Congress that would ban any manufacturer with 15% of Chinese ownership or more. It's unclear how the U.S. is going to handle Chinese automakers, or how American automakers will respond to such potential competition. But Ford seems to be talking out of both sides of its mouth, in regard to Chinese EVs, so it will be interesting to see how they're handled in the future.

title: How Geely's New Battery Handles A Megawatt Of Charging Power Without Crazy Degradation
content:
How Geely's New Battery Handles A Megawatt Of Charging Power Without Crazy Degradation
The automaker has a novel solution to slow down battery degradation. Here's what we know.
- Geely Auto Group's new electric vehicle battery can handle charging speeds north of a 1,000 kilowatts.
- Such ultra-fast charging speeds can accelerate aging in an EV battery, if not properly engineered.
- The automaker said it had developed several solutions to prevent rapid aging in its new battery.
When it comes to fast-charging speeds, Chinese automakers are in the stratosphere, comfortably above everyone else. While 600 kilowatts is the peak we’ve seen from Western companies, with planned roll outs of 750 kW chargers, Chinese automakers like BYD and Geely Auto Group have already surpassed the 1,000 kW mark for passenger cars and are now locked in a battle to one-up each other.
Charging EVs at such monster speeds frequently can adversely impact the long-term health of the battery. That’s why battery companies try striking a balance between longevity and fast charging. Overly leaning in one direction can cause a disaster at the other end.
So when Chinese juggernaut Geely Auto Group revealed its absurdly powerful 2.2 megawatt charger last week at a launch event in Ningbo, China, the automaker spent a lot of time explaining how it was managing aging on its new battery.
While the charger can dispense 2.2 MW from a single gun, some high-end EVs under the Geely Auto Group will peak at around 1,100 kW. The company said it was the first in the world where two EVs can pull megawatt speeds from the same station.
Jerry Gan, the CEO of Geely Auto Group, did not downplay the potential effects of megawatt charging on battery health. “We do not advocate fast-charging technologies at the expense of lifespan,” Gan said. “If a battery frequently fast-charged is not maintained or repaired, its lifespan suffers irreversible decline,” he added.
The company’s new Ultra Short Blade Battery can peak at nearly 1,100 kilowatts. In a demo, the automaker showed a Lynk & Co 10 getting charged from 10-97% in just 8 minutes and 40 seconds. That’s comfortably faster than the fastest-charging EVs in the U.S., like the Lucid Gravity and the Porsche Cayenne Electric, which peak at 400 kilowatts. The upcoming Mercedes-AMG GT will peak at 600 kW. Most mass-market models in the U.S. average at around 30 minutes for a 10-80% charge.
Geely said it had incorporated several technologies to prevent accelerated aging in its new battery. It even increased the new battery’s warranty from eight years, 150,000 kilometers (93,205 miles) to eight years, 200,000 km (124,000 miles), as a show of confidence in its long-term health. Before diving into Geely's solutions for battery aging, it’s worth understanding what causes degradation in the first place.
How Fast-Charging Accelerates Battery Degradation
The automaker said aging comes down to two root causes: lithium plating and extreme temperatures. Megawatt speeds accounted for 60% of the heat generated in the battery, mainly because current pushed through the cells’ internal paths. About 35% came from electrochemical reactions and the rest from what the company called “entropic” heat, the kind that comes from electrode reactions.
A Geely executive explaining how lithium plating and dendrites affect an EV battery.
Lithium plating is another major cause of degradation. It happens when ions flood the anode, the part of the cell where electrons travel during charging. This rush can cause some ions to accumulate on the anode’s surface, as they don’t get properly absorbed. Excessive flooding causes lithium dendrites, tiny spikes that grow inside a cell, which can cause short circuits and permanently damage the battery.
How Did Geely Solve This Problem?
Ren Xiangfei, the chief engineering scientist at Geely Auto Group, said the company made changes to the cell, the raw materials inside, the manufacturing process, and introduced a new AI-powered charger management system to prevent the battery from crossing its thermal limits.
“In an ideal world, the ions settle into the graphite evenly and smoothly,” Xiangfei said.
The Ultra Short Blade Battery cell, for starters, comes in two main sizes: 395 mm and 370 mm in length. Both are smaller than Geely’s 580 mm cell and what the automaker claimed was common in the industry, around 960 mm. The smaller cell size reduces the migration path for the ions—distance traveled in simple terms—during charging and discharging. That shorter journey also lowers internal resistance and reduces heat generation.
The company also made structural changes to both the cathode and the anode to prevent lithium plating, Xiangfei said. On the cathode, “high entropy elements” allowed widening the pathways through which the ions move from the cathode to the anode. “Like turning a single lane into a multi-lane highway,” he added. The structural modifications to the graphite anode, he said, were equivalent to “building a flyover.”
To prevent ions from accumulating, a new “lithium pulse restoration” technology was implemented. A “micro amplitude pulse current” is injected into the anode at a specific frequency to reduce the ion accumulation at the anode surface. The process was like using a massage gun on muscles after a workout to relieve the tension, Xiangfei said.
The other big cause of battery aging is heat. To manage that, an “end-to-end five-point liquid cooling system” works in harmony across several components. Those include the on-site energy storage battery, power module, charger, charging port, and the EV battery. An AI-powered system called Xingrui PowerMind predicts battery temperatures 30 seconds in advance and adjusts speeds in real time.
The thermal management is designed to keep the battery’s average temperature at 55 degrees Celsius, with a ceiling of 65 degrees Celsius. The 65C threshold is a new national standard in China that went into effect this July to prevent batteries from overheating.
What Geely Isn't Telling You
As you can probably tell by now, the automaker went all guns blazing with the new battery and charging technology. However, it’s one thing to make big claims and another to have the technology truly democratized.
BYD's megawatt charging speeds triggered debates this spring when a blogger claimed to have ran independent charging tests on a Fangchengbao Tai 3 electric SUV. His recorded maximum temperature of 76.42 degrees Celsius was higher than what the vehicle displayed, around 71C. He said in a social media post that BYD had reported him to the police.
It could be years before we see the long term impacts of megawatt charging on battery health, since the technology only started getting commercialized at scale in China last year. However, if Geely's extended battery warranty is anything to go by, the company feels pretty confident about it. We’ll see in due time if customers feel the same.
It's also worth noting that degradation varies a lot depending on driving behavior, charging habits, climate, and the underlying technology itself. While some Western studies have indeed shown that fast-charging frequently accelerates battery aging, others have shown that modern EV battery tech has come a long way and can comfortably handle frequent fast-charging with minimal aging.
In other words, you don't need to worry about the impact of your neighborhood Tesla Supercharger on your battery. It's also advisable to follow the manufacturer-recommended charging practices for your EV to keep the battery in the best possible shape. Use a home charger for your daily driving needs if you can, and don't shy away from a public fast-charger on longer journeys. As technology progresses, you'll have less and less to worry about.

title: Mercedes Won't Be Banned In America: Senator
content:
About 20% of Mercedes shares are owned by Chinese investors. To be on the right side of a new law, though, Mercedes may have to get that number down.
Photo by:
Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
5:53pm ET
Chinese vehicles and automakers have been banned from the U.S. market for some time now, with the introduction of the Connected Vehicle Rule in 2025. It's why the Geely-owned
had to jump through so many hoops to keep selling cars here, and is said to be why Polestar is being kicked out (
even if there's some debate about that
However, U.S. lawmakers want to get even stricter, and with a Senate bill set to ban automakers that have 15% Chinese ownership or more. Despite that, if it passes, one of the lawmakers behind the bill says that Mercedes is safe, even though Chinese investors control about 20% of its shares.
"What we're not going to do, obviously, is ban Mercedes-Benz vehicles in ‌America," said Republican ​Bernie Moreno (R-MI), according to
. "There's ​concern that ​can they get ‌to 15% without debilitating ​their company?"
Between Tenaciou3 Prospect Investment Limited (9.69%) and BAIC Group (9.98%), Chinese companies own more than that 15% threshold Moreno mentioned. However, since that ownership is passive, and neither company has any involvement in daily operations, product planning, or any sort of development, it seems the U.S. government is ok with it, as long as the company can get it down below the 15% threshold.
Photo by: Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
This is a bipartisan bill, too. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) reportedly told
that 99 senators were in favor of the bill, with the only nay being Senator Rand Paul (R-KY). Rand, though, told
that his opposition to the bill is based on it putting Mercedes in jeopardy. If the bit about Mercedes is removed from the bill, then he'll be for it.
Mercedes isn't the only company with more than 15% Chinese ownership, either. Geely owns 17% of Aston Martin, so it will need to restructure if this bill passes, too. Volvo was previously able to work around the existing laws by proving it isn't using Chinese-made software, but Geely is still its parent company.
If this bill becomes law, we'll also likely lose Lotus in the U.S. entirely, given that the brand is also Chinese-owned. Lotus is tiny, though, and doesn't sell very well here, so that wouldn't be a huge blow. However, brands like Mercedes and Aston Martin might have to do some clever restructuring to get their Chinese ownership down. The U.S. market is obviously huge for both brands, so they'll have to find one way out or another.

title: Nissan Wants Hybrids To Be Its Primary Powertrain By 2030
content:
Nissan Wants Hybrids To Be Its Primary Powertrain By 2030
As hybrids grow in popularity, Nissan does not want to be left behind. More Hybrids, and even EREV models are coming.
- Nissan wants hybrid and EREV models to be its primary powertrain option in North America and Latin America by 2030.
- The brand also wants more localized production. The Rogue Hybrid will be made in Tennessee starting in 2028.
- Nissan also plans to bring a hybrid version of the subcompact Kicks crossover to the U.S. by 2028.
We’ve been telling you all for a long time now: the world is going to electrify, one way or another, even if it's not quite at the same speed or scale we’d like here at InsideEVs. Hybrid sales are up, thanks to the penetration of reasonably-priced options from brands like Honda, Toyota, Kia, and Hyundai. Those four brands have been rapidly expanding their hybrid offerings.
Nissan doesn’t want to be left behind.
Last week, it finally unveiled the U.S. version of its Nissan Rogue E-Power series hybrid, known simply as the Rogue Hybrid, This week, it's talking about just how serious it is about becoming a hybrid leader in the U.S.
In a conversation with Automotive News, Nissan Americas Chairman Christian Meunier emphasized the importance of not only making these models the star of Nissan’s show, but also localizing the vehicles for their key markets. The plan is for the Rogue E-Power hybrid to come from Japan initially,with Nissan’s Smyrna, Tennessee plant set to start making Rogue E-Power hybrids by 2028. Meunier wants the Rogue E-Power to account for 30 to 40% of total Rogue sales, “very quickly,” although no timeline was stated.
The Rogue E-Power won’t just be the only hybrid, nor are Nissan’s hybrid aspirations limited to just the U.S. Nissan sees its hybrids being the primary powertrain choice for both North America and Latin America by 2030. Also, the brand plans to introduce an E-power version of the gas-powered Kicks crossover to the U.S. by 2028.
On one hand, this is great to see Nissan catching up in the U.S., since its hybrid offerings have historically been piecemeal. Aside from the 2008-2010 Nissan Altima and short-lived hybrid versions of the Infiniti QX60, Nissan Murano, and Nissan Pathfinder, Nissan has been missing in action. In the meantime, Toyota has gone all-in with hybrids, even discontinuing ICE-only versions of popular models like the Sienna, Camry, and RAV4. We'll see if Nissan's aggressive catch-up plan works.
However, I hope this doesn’t come at the expense of full electrification. We should be getting drivers off of gas entirely, and as clever as they are, E-power hybrids use gas power. The batteries they use are small and can’t cover any sort of commute with engine-off, full-EV power. Nissan currently only makes one EV, the Leaf. It’s a swell car, but it’s unclear if there will be a follow-up anytime soon. The Ariya was canceled last year, and while it continues on in Canada (and updated with NACS), Nissan says it’s not coming back. Hopefully, Nissan continues to press onward and bring us more EVs alongside its EREV and hybrid future models.

title: The Tesla Model 3 Gets A Big Upgrade, But The U.S. Is Left Out
content:
The electric sedan is finally getting vehicle-to-load (V2L) functionality, but you’ll need to move out of the country to get one.
Photo by:
3:38am ET
Tesla has updated the Model 3 EV overseas.
The electric four-door sedan now finally comes with vehicle-to-load (V2L) functionality via an adapter.
The infotainment screen is also larger, and the headliner color has been switched to black.
Tesla Model 3
is getting a few improvements, but American customers will have to wait a little longer, as the company has decided to start the rollout outside of the U.S.
Model 3s delivered starting in the fourth quarter of this year will finally be capable of exporting energy from their high-voltage batteries through a feature called
vehicle-to-load (V2L)
. It’s something that EVs from other automakers have been equipped with for years, and now Tesla has added it to the
The feature will only be available on cars sold in China, Australia, New Zealand, and South Korea, but other countries are expected to get in on the action in the following months. By using an adapter that plugs into the vehicle’s charging port, owners can power tools, appliances, or camping equipment with a combined power draw of up to 2.2 kilowatts.
What’s more, all
versions sold in these countries are also getting V2L functionality. In the United States, the only Tesla vehicles that come with V2L out of the box are the
Cybertruck
Model Y Premium, Model Y L, and Model Y Performance
. The entry-level Model Y is left out, but that’s probably going to change after Tesla ramps up the distribution of the updated hardware that enables bidirectional charging.
The Tesla Outlet Adapter for cars with a Type 2 charging port.
Photo by: Tesla
In the U.S., all Model Y EVs that can export power need an adapter that plugs into the mobile charger. With it, the car can deliver up to 2.4 kW through a pair of outlets.
Getting back to the Model 3, its central infotainment screen is also getting a minor update, with a 16-inch touchscreen with an improved pixel density replacing the 15.4-inch display of the outgoing model. Tesla didn’t say it out loud, but it’s probably the same 16-inch screen that made its way into the Model Y earlier this year.
Other changes include a black headliner, a new Zen Grey seat color, and 19-inch Dark Nova wheels.
It’s worth noting that retrofitting V2L to an older Model Y or Model 3 is not possible, as the hardware that enables the function differs. That may change in the future, but for now, it’s a no-go. What’s more, owners won’t be able to power an entire house off the V2L adapter, as its power output is quite limited, but it should be enough to power a fridge and some essential gear during an outage.

title: You Won't Be Able To Buy A Rivian R2 With Lidar This Year After All
content:
Rivian still plans to launch its new autonomy computer and lidar this year. But you won't be able to buy it.
Photo by:
2:24pm ET
Rivian's latest autonomy hardware is still planned to launch this year—you just won't be able to buy it.
The company revealed that it plans to release lidar and its new in-house computer for employees.
Regular buyers will see the hardware in consumer cars starting in 2027.
If you've been waiting to pull the trigger on a new Rivian R2 over its soon-to-be-upgraded autonomy computer and sensor suite, you might be waiting a bit longer than expected.
Rivian still plans to put its new in-house silicon (
called RAP1
) and lidar sensor in the newly launched R2 before the end of the year. However, it turns out that there's a little asterisk attached to that sentence. Those first cars will be going to employees, not public reservation holders.
Photo by: Rivian
The automaker's VP of Investor Relations, Chip Newcom,
revealed
the company's plans for its autonomy hardware while speaking at Evercore's ADAS, AV, and AI Forum on Tuesday.
He clarified how Rivian plans to roll out its latest and greatest autonomy tech:
For employees, the plan is to start rolling out [RAP1]—so our third-generation computer plus the LIDAR—to go into the vehicle later this year for employees, and then start rolling that out to customers next year.
That's a little bit different than how CEO
RJ Scaringe
sold the timeline. Scaringe held that the its new
Gen 3 autonomy platform
(which includes the new compute, long-range lidar, five radar sensors, and 11 cameras) would arrive "starting in late 2026," which is a bit of a murky outlook. Officially, this is the first time that Rivian has provided clarification on that timeline. And while it's still
technically
true that the platform is getting an upgrade this year, Newcom's comments reveal that the 2026 launch only includes cars purchased by Rivian employees.
In July, Rivian told
InsideEVs
that RAP1 and lidar would not be offered with the R2's Launch Package, and that the Launch Package would only be available for 2027 vehicles. We asked Rivian if that meant the new hardware meant waiting for the 2028 model to launch, however, the automaker did not respond to any of our follow-up emails at that time.
Rivian also did not respond to a request from
InsideEVs
to clarify Newcom's new public timeline.
Autonomy-savvy consumer have viewed this as a substantial upgrade to the car's future autonomy capability, despite Rivian saying that the
effects wouldn't be felt for several years
. And for many
Musk expats coming to Rivian R2 from a car equipped with Tesla's doomed Hardware 3
, the small time between when deliveries started in June and the end of the year was was enough to justify the wait.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
It's clear that Rivian wants to play its launches safe. The R2 is arguably its most important product launch to-date, directly taking on the
Tesla Model Y
. And with autonomy being on the forefront of many buyers' minds, it needs to make sure that the expansion of R2 equipped with its latest tech will go smoothly.
So, sure, if you want to wait for lidar before buying R2, you might be in line for a bit longer than expected. But if today's version of Rivian's hands-free driving is good enough for you, why wait?

title: 任天堂《宝可梦传说 Z-A》Switch 2 卡带 + 超次元爆涌 DLC 版 10 月 29 日发售
content:
IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，任天堂宣布将于 10 月 29 日推出新的《宝可梦传说 Z-A》Nintendo Switch 2 版实体扩充包，将“超次元爆涌”（Mega Dimension）DLC 一并收录其中。
不含 DLC 的《宝可梦传说 Z-A》Nintendo Switch 2 版已于 2025 年 10 月 16 日发售，数字版和实体版港区定价均为 359~409 港币（IT之家注：现汇率约合 307.3 ~ 350.1 元人民币）。
据介绍，Nintendo Switch 2 版针对性能、分辨率和帧率进行了优化；因此，玩家也可以先购买实体卡带，之后再升级至 Nintendo Switch 2。另外，实体版还将附赠 100 个高级球（Ultra Ball）的兑换码（每个存档只能兑换一次）。
“超次元爆涌”扩展内容中还加入了新的宝可梦和 Mega 超级进化内容。据任天堂介绍，异次元密阿雷市中的部分宝可梦等级可能超过 100 级，从而突破原本的等级上限。
“超次元爆涌”此前作为独立 DLC 推出，支持 Nintendo Switch 及 Nintendo Switch 2 版游戏。任天堂目前仍提供单独购买该 DLC 的方式，而此次实体合集则将本体与扩展内容整合在同一套产品中。

title: 宝马计划 2027 年在欧洲推行代理直销模式，避免经销商加价销售
content:
IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，宝马集团宣布将从 2027 年年中开始，在欧洲导入新的“代理直售”模式。
IT之家注意到，该模式此前已通过 MINI 品牌在 24 个欧洲市场落地，宝马集团希望借此建立覆盖试驾、购车直至售后服务整个客户旅程的统一数据体系。宝马集团表示，MINI 采用新模式后积累的经验将为宝马品牌后续大规模推广提供基础。
这里所说的“直售”并不意味着宝马将取消经销商网络。经销商仍然负责与消费者接触，并提供试驾、咨询、交付等服务，但不再以传统方式从宝马买断新车后自行加价销售。
在新模式下，经销商将按照每辆车辆获得固定佣金，而不是主要依靠批发价与零售价之间的差价获取收入。宝马集团此前表示，这种方式能够提高经销商收入的可预测性。
对于消费者而言，较明显的变化是价格体系。宝马品牌旗下车型将在全国范围内采用统一定价，消费者无法在不同经销商之间比价并通过议价获得折扣。
宝马集团还计划进一步打通线上与线下购车流程。消费者可以在线购车、在经销商处试驾，随后继续在线操作，并根据自身需求选择最终的购买渠道。
宝马集团表示，人工智能将成为这一销售体系的基础，而不仅是工具。公司计划利用 AI 结合经销商和数字渠道的数据，为消费者提供更加个性化的销售服务。

游戏保留原版无飞行坐骑、无等级缩放的经典体验，强调野外探索与组队协作，并对艾泽拉斯地图光照和画面纹理进行视觉升级。官方称引入实时全局光照和体积光雾系统，同时保留 2004 年原版手绘风格。
全新可玩种族“天裔”为御风而生的精灵种族，源自泽风岛的高等精灵流亡者，联盟和部落均可选择，拥有专属技能、德鲁伊变形形态及自定义选项。购买天裔英雄礼包或更高版本方可解锁该种族及泽风岛起始剧情。
IT之家注意到，暴雪提供了天裔史诗 / 英雄两大礼包，天裔英雄礼包售价 218 元，天裔史诗礼包售价 388 元。
史诗礼包包含国服 Beta 测试资格、天裔种族与泽风岛起始剧情、全新坐骑及装饰物品、30 天游戏时间，以及 11 月 3 日至 4 日的名称预留资格。
内容方面，游戏新增泽风岛、海加尔山、河林边疆等区域，以及 1000 多个全新任务。故事线大体承接《魔兽争霸 3》，但关键事件产生分支：海加尔山的世界之树并未爆炸，达拉然仍停留在希尔斯布莱德丘陵。
副本包含 9 座全新地下城，如洛丹伦废墟、达拉然下水道、奥卡兹监狱等。12 月 10 日将解锁墓穴深窟 10 人模式和海加尔峰 20 人模式，后续上线重制经典 40 人团本奥妮克希亚的巢穴。
种族与职业新增组合，被遗忘者可选圣骑士，矮人可选萨满，并引入亡灵圣骑士剧情线。系统新增账号传承系统，角色养成进度账号互通，一个角色的成果可共享给同账号下其他角色。
游戏新增露营系统，玩家可搭建营地互相提供增益效果。PVP 方面新增 15v15 战场暗矛群岛，并对原有战场机制进行平衡性重做。Beta 测试等级上限为 30 级，测试数据不予保留。
预下载可通过战网桌面应用或官网绿色客户端进行。官方建议将游戏安装至固态硬盘，并更新显卡驱动。预约玩家可获 4 种背包。游戏包含在魔兽订阅内，后续将持续更新专家模式、更多地下城、PVP 内容和世界扩展任务线。

title: 用户反馈升级微软 Win11 26H2 后内存用量减少约 1.5~2GB
content:
IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，科技媒体 Wccftech 今天（10 月 1 日）发布博文，报道称基于社区用户反馈，在相同配置情况下，从 Windows 11 25H2 系统升级到 26H2，内存占用减少约 1.5GB~2GB。
该媒体查询 Reddit 社区、X 社交平台，发现部分用户反馈升级到 Windows 11 26H2 系统之后，内存占用基本可以下降 1.5~2GB。由于在 8GB、32GB、48GB 配置上内存占用下降幅度基本相同，下文不从降幅比例方式计算。
用户 @SoyITPro 在 X 平台发布推文，在配备 32GB 内存的设备上，升级 Windows 11 26H2 后内存占用从 9.1GB 降至 7.5GB，降幅为 1.6GB。IT之家附上相关截图如下：
网友 u/shutter_singh 在 Reddit 社区反馈，在配备 48GB 内存的设备上，25H2 开机后内存占用约为 6.9GB，更新 26H2 系统后内存占用降低到 4.8~5GB，降幅约为 2GB。
网友 @rakamajaka 在 X 平台发布推文，指出在 56GB 内存配置上，25H2 开机内存占用约为 13.1GB，升级到 26H2 系统之后，内存占用下降到 7.3GB，下降约 6GB。
网友 @Honchan_P 昨日（9 月 30 日）在 X 平台发布推文，8GB 内存配置情况下，在 25H2 系统情况下内存占用约为 5.7GB，不过在升级到 26H2 系统之后，内存占用约为 4.1GB，降幅约 1.6GB。
网友 @gabHernandez285 反馈在同样 8GB 内存配置情况下，不使用 Chrome 浏览器，也没有玩游戏情况下，卸载了 WebView2 和 SearchHost.exe 之后，内存占用约为 4.6GB。

title: 致敬《终结者 2》：Figure 让 F.02 人形机器人亲自跳入熔炉，采纳施瓦辛格本人提议
content:
IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，美国初创企业 Figure 今日发布视频，为寿终正寝的 F.02 机器人举行一场“火化仪式”。
随着 Figure F.03 机队不断壮大，F.02 已经日显颓势。该公司认为继续维护老一代机器人已经没有意义，但直接报废并不是最优选择，因为这些机器人内含大量专用硬件和知识产权结晶。Figure 甚至表示，直接进行拆解工作需要大量时间，甚至可能拖慢 F.04 的研发进度。
Figure 表示，让机器人自己跳入熔炉这个想法正是源自 T-800 扮演者阿诺德 · 施瓦辛格本人。此前 Figure 曾在网上征集如何进行 F.02 送别仪式，后来施瓦辛格的想法被采纳。
IT之家注意到，后来施瓦辛格亲自来到了熔解现场，他身穿全套防护装备，带领一台 F.02 走向熔炉，致敬了《终结者 2》电影。在视频结尾，他摘下面具说道：“Figure 2 已经退役。”
不过，想找到合适的熔炉并不容易。许多美国和墨西哥企业都拒绝了 Figure 的请求，因为他们无法确认机器人内部锂电池的安全性。最终公司在芬兰伊马特拉找到了符合要求的设施。
此外，Figure 并没有简单地把 F.02 扔进熔炉，而是专门训练了一个 AI 模型，让机器人能够以尽可能壮观之方式跳入熔炉。

content:
IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，英伟达于当地时间 30 日推出 GeForce 安全更新驱动程序 582.78，适用于 Maxwell、Pascal 和 Volta 架构显卡，涵盖 GTX 700 系、GTX 900 系、GTX 10 系显卡及 Tesla V100、Titan V 等专业卡。

title: 魁匠团宣布取消《绝地求生：黑色任务》搜打撤项目，游戏尚未发售便已落幕
content:
IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，魁匠团（KRAFTON）今日宣布已终止《绝地求生：黑色任务》项目的开发，这款搜打撤游戏尚未正式发售便宣告落幕。
KRAFTON 表示，在评估项目当前开发状态及未来方向后，团队认为现有方向无法打造一款能够让玩家长期满意的游戏，因此作出了终止开发的决定。KRAFTON 官方同时感谢参加封闭测试并提供反馈的玩家，并表示 PUBG Studios 将把开发和测试过程中积累的经验应用于未来项目。
IT之家查询获悉，《绝地求生：黑色任务》是一款第一人称战术撤离射击游戏，玩家进入名为“Coli”的时间循环岛屿，搜集资源并与其他玩家及 AI 敌人交战，随后尝试成功撤离。游戏采用 PvPvE 模式，每场最多 45 名玩家组成 3 人小队参与。
该项目此前已经进行多轮封闭测试。首次封闭 Alpha 测试于 2025 年 12 月举行，官方当时表示参与度超过预期，同时玩家反馈也指出战斗反馈、战场态势判断以及重复游玩疲劳等问题。
2026 年 6 月 26 日至 29 日，游戏又进行了第二次封闭 Alpha 测试，并开放玩家直播、录制和分享测试内容。
今年早些时候，该公司已经停止了《PUBG：Blindspot》的开发；8 月公布的《PUBG：DED.NET》则采用 Roguelike 射击玩法，目前仍是另一款独立项目。

Kaiserslautern. Zum 01. September startete an der Hochschule Kaiserslautern ein neues Projekt: BMWi - die Entwicklung eines Berufsbegleitenden Masterstudiengangs Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, das vom Europäischen Sozialfonds Plus und dem Ministerium für Wissenschaft, Weiterbildung und Gesundheit Rheinland-Pfalz (MWWG) gefördert wird. Mit einer Laufzeit von zwei Jahren sollen neue Wege zwischen beruflicher und akademischer Bildung eröffnet und zugleich ein Beitrag zur Fachkräftesicherung in der Region geleistet werden.
Der berufsbegleitende Masterstudiengang Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen richtet sich insbesondere an beruflich Qualifizierte und kann ab dem Wintersemester 2028/2029 am Campus Kaiserslautern studiert werden. Im Mittelpunkt der zweijährigen Entwicklungsphase stehen die Konzeption des Studiengangs, die Ausarbeitung eines arbeitsmarktorientierten Curriculums, die Entwicklung geeigneter digitaler Lehr- und Lernformate sowie die Vorbereitung der organisatorischen Strukturen und die Durchführung des Akkreditierungsverfahrens. Inhaltlich wird der künftige Masterstudiengang technische und ingenieurwissenschaftliche Kompetenzen mit wirtschaftswissenschaftlichen Themen mittels anwendungsorientierter Lern- und Transferformate verbinden.
Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt des Projekts liegt auch auf der Entwicklung von Unterstützungsangeboten für beruflich qualifizierte Studierende. Angesprochen werden beispielsweise Meisterinnen und Meister, Technikerinnen und Techniker, Fachwirtinnen und Fachwirte sowie berufserfahrene Fachkräfte. Die geplanten Angebote sollen den Übergang aus der beruflichen Praxis in ein akademisches Masterstudium erleichtern und unterschiedliche fachliche und methodische Eingangsvoraussetzungen berücksichtigen.
Geleitet wird das Projekt von Marie Kindopp, Mitarbeiterin im Fachbereich Angewandte Ingenieurwissenschaften an der Hochschule Kaiserslautern. Die wissenschaftliche Projektbegleitung liegt bei Prof. Dr. Christian M. Thurnes. Ab dem 1. Oktober stößt Mareike Beier als neue Projektmitarbeiterin zum Team und wird insbesondere die Entwicklung und Umsetzung der Studiengangs- und Unterstützungsangebote vorantreiben.

Spatenstich für den Forschungscampus im Lausitz Science Park:
Das IHP – Leibniz-Institut für innovative Mikroelektronik plant auf dem neuen Forschungscampus ein neues Gebäude mit Platz für rund 140 Arbeitsplätze
Cottbus / Frankfurt (Oder), 1. Oktober 2026. Mit einem gemeinsamen Spatenstich haben das Deutsche Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR), die Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft und das IHP – Leibniz-Institut für innovative Mikroelektronik heute die Erschließung des neuen Forschungscampus im Lausitz Science Park begonnen. Auf dem 51.000 Quadratmeter großen Areal errichten die drei Partner in den kommenden Jahren jeweils eigene Gebäude. Das IHP plant dort ein Büro- und Laborgebäude, das als Leibniz-Standort angelegt ist und rund 140 Arbeitsplätze bieten soll. Die Fertigstellung ist für Ende 2029 angesetzt.
Am Standort Cottbus will das IHP Forschungsthemen bearbeiten, bei denen Mikroelektronik, innovative Materialsysteme und künstliche Intelligenz zusammenwirken, etwa intelligente Edge-Systeme, die Mikroelektronik und KI verbinden, verteilte Sensorik und neue Materialsysteme für sensorische Anwendungen. Die Labore sind für Materialanalytik, für Sensorik und eingebettete Systeme sowie für Biomaterialien im Gesundheitsbereich vorgesehen, ein weiteres dient dem Aufbau von Systemen und Demonstratoren. Die Hälfte des Gebäudes nutzt das IHP für den eigenen Bedarf; die andere Hälfte steht weiteren Instituten der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft als dauerhafte oder projektbezogene Anlaufstelle offen. So können mehrere Institute unter einem Dach interdisziplinär forschen.
Das IHP ist seit 1998 in Cottbus aktiv, mit gemeinsamen Professuren, einem Joint Lab und einem Joint Research Center an der Brandenburgischen Technischen Universität Cottbus-Senftenberg (BTU). Seit 2023 unterhält es zudem einen eigenen Standort in der Cottbuser Nordstraße, wo es bis zum Einzug in den Neubau sein Team aufbaut. Den Strukturwandel unterstützt es durch die Beteiligung an den Strukturstärkungsprojekten iCampus, OASYS und AI-DISCO; AI-DISCO hat das IHP selbst initiiert und führt es als Konsortialleiter. Am künftigen Campus wird das Institut direkter Nachbar von BTU, DLR und Fraunhofer und will dort gemeinsame Forschung entlang der Profillinien der BTU und des Lausitz Science Parks betreiben. Für die Region kann die Ansiedlung Anknüpfungspunkte für weitere Forschungseinrichtungen und für Unternehmen aus der Wirtschaft schaffen, auch überregional.
„Viele Fragen, an denen wir heute arbeiten, lassen sich innerhalb einer einzelnen Disziplin nicht mehr beantworten. Sensorsysteme für die Medizin etwa brauchen Mikroelektronik, Materialforschung und KI zugleich“, sagt Prof. Dr.-Ing. Gerhard Kahmen, Wissenschaftlich-Technischer Geschäftsführer des IHP. „Mit dem Neubau bringen wir diese Fächer unter ein Dach, direkt neben der BTU und unseren Partnern auf dem Campus. Was wir hier erforschen, soll in der Lausitz angewendet werden und wird wichtige Impulse für den Strukturwandel geben.“
Die Erschließung des Forschungscampus wird gefördert durch den Bund aus Mitteln des Investitionsgesetzes Kohleregionen und kofinanziert aus Mitteln des Landes Brandenburg.

Der Maschinenbau verändert sich rasant. Digitalisierung, intelligente Systeme und Künstliche Intelligenz schaffen neue Anforderungen – und eröffnen spannende Karriereperspektiven. Mit zwei neuen Studienrichtungen im Bachelorstudiengang Maschinenbau können Sie Ihr Studium ab Oktober noch gezielter auf diese Entwicklungen ausrichten.
Ob Sie sich für den klassischen Maschinenbau begeistern oder die Verbindung von Ingenieurwissenschaften und Informatik vertiefen möchten – wählen Sie den Schwerpunkt, der am besten zu Ihren Interessen und beruflichen Zielen passt.
Studienrichtung Maschinenbau: Ingenieurwissen für die Industrie von morgen
Maschinenbau gehört zu den vielseitigsten Ingenieurdisziplinen überhaupt. Mit der neuen Studienrichtung vertiefen Sie Ihr Wissen in Konstruktion, Entwicklung und Fertigung und erweitern Ihr Kompetenzprofil gleichzeitig um Zukunftsthemen wie Digitalisierung, Systems Engineering, Nachhaltigkeit und Künstliche Intelligenz.
So bereiten Sie sich auf anspruchsvolle Aufgaben in Entwicklung, Produktion und technischen Projekten vor.
Studienrichtung Maschinenbau-Informatik: Wenn Maschinen intelligent werden

Sie verbinden fundiertes Maschinenbauwissen mit Informatik, Automatisierung und digitalen Technologien. Dadurch qualifizieren Sie sich für Aufgaben rund um Industrie 4.0, intelligente Maschinen und die digitale Transformation im Maschinen- und Anlagenbau.
Mit den beiden neuen Studienrichtungen erweitert die Wilhelm Büchner Hochschule ihr Maschinenbau-Angebot gezielt um Kompetenzen, die in einer zunehmend digitalen Industrie gefragt sind.

Navigieren trotz Signalstörung: Neue Lösungen für Umgebungen mit eingeschränktem Satellitenempfang
Navigationssysteme sind aus unserem Alltag kaum noch wegzudenken. Doch die Technik hat eine Schwachstelle: In dicht bebauten Gebieten, in Bereichen mit starker Vegetation sowie an Orten mit physischen Hindernissen können die Signale des Globalen Navigationssatellitensystems (GNSS) blockiert oder reflektiert werden. Dies beeinträchtigt in der Regel die Ortungsgenauigkeit. Das europäische Forschungsprojekt "egeniouss", an dem die Technische Universität Braunschweig beteiligt ist, hat in dreieinhalb Jahren Forschung Lösungen entwickelt, um die Genauigkeit der satellitengestützten Ortung trotz solcher Störungen zu verbessern.
Medienvertreter*innen sind herzlich zur Präsentation der Ergebnisse mit Vorführungen zu Fahrradnavigation, Vermessungsarbeiten und Flugnavigation eingeladen:
Donnerstag, 15. Oktober 2026, 9:00 Uhr
Haus der Wissenschaft
Pockelsstraße 11, 38106 Braunschweig
Bei der Präsentation gibt es für Medienvertreter*innen die Möglichkeit, die Vorführungen zu filmen und zu fotografieren sowie Interviews mit Wissenschaftler*innen und den für das Projekt verantwortlichen technischen Teams zu führen.
Wir freuen uns über Ihre Anmeldung unter: https://1znjap5vdsd.typeform.com/to/bBa2KVL3
Im Projekt egeniouss werden das Globale Navigationssatellitensystem, Computer Vision und Geodaten aus mehreren Sensoren kombiniert. Das System nutzt von Geräten aufgenommene Bilder sowie Informationen über die Umgebung, um die satellitengestützte Ortung zu ergänzen, wenn die Signale gestört oder unzureichend sind. Die Veranstaltung im Haus der Wissenschaft bietet die Gelegenheit, die Technologie unter realen Bedingungen in Aktion zu erleben und mehr über die Erkenntnisse und Schlussfolgerungen des Projekts zu erfahren.
Die Entwicklungen wurden in drei Bereichen angewendet: Fahrradnavigation im städtischen Umfeld, Erfassung von Geodaten für Vermessungszwecke und luftgestützte Navigation. Diese Anwendungsfälle umfassen sowohl alltägliche als auch professionelle Anwendungen, bei denen die Kontinuität und Zuverlässigkeit der Positionsbestimmung für die Leistungsfähigkeit von Anwendungen, Geräten und Betriebsabläufen entscheidend sind.
Die Veranstaltung befasst sich auch mit der Frage, wie die Technologie über das Projekt hinaus genutzt werden kann. Dabei werden auch die praktischen Anforderungen für ihren Einsatz sowie ihre Anpassung an andere Branchen und Dienste, die auf eine genaue und zuverlässige Positionsbestimmung angewiesen sind, beleuchtet.

Die Technologie des Projekts kombiniert das Globale Navigationssatellitensystem (GNSS), Computer Vision und Multisensor-Datenfusion, um satellitengestützte Informationen in komplexen städtischen und operativen Umgebungen zu ergänzen. Mechanik, Elektronik und Software wachsen immer mehr zusammen. Mit zwei neuen Studienrichtungen im Bachelorstudiengang Mechatronik können Sie Ihr Studium ab Oktober noch gezielter an diesem Megatrend und Ihren Interessen und beruflichen Zielen ausrichten.

Prof. Dr.-Ing. Guido Spars, Inhaber des Lehrstuhls Ökonomie des Planens und Bauens an der Bergischen Universität Wuppertal, ist Mitglied im neu gegründeten Beirat des Netzwerkes Stadtentwicklung NRW. Am 9. Oktober 2026 kommt das Gremium zu seiner ersten Sitzung zusammen. Spars bringt zukünftig seine wissenschaftliche und praktische Expertise in die Arbeit des Beirats ein, insbesondere in den Bereichen Stadt- und Immobilienökonomie, im Wohnungsbau sowie in der nachhaltigen Stadt- und Quartiersentwicklung.
„Viele Kommunen stehen derzeit vor sehr konkreten Herausforderungen. Um funktionierende und tragfähige Lösungen zu entwickeln, kann der intensivere Austausch zwischen kommunaler Praxis und Wissenschaft eine Lösung sein. Ich freue mich darauf, meine Erfahrungen in die Arbeit des Beirats einzubringen und zugleich von den Erfahrungen der Städte und Gemeinden zu lernen“, sagt Prof. Guido Spars.
In seiner Forschung verbindet Guido Spars ökonomische Fragestellungen des Planens und Bauens mit aktuellen Herausforderungen der Stadt- und Quartiersentwicklung. Dabei beschäftigt er sich insbesondere mit den wirtschaftlichen und institutionellen Rahmenbedingungen der Stadtentwicklung und des Wohnungsbaus und berät Kommunen in stadt- und immobilienökonomischen Fragen.
Diese Fragestellungen gewinnen gerade auf kommunaler Ebene zunehmend an Bedeutung. Städte und Gemeinden stehen vor der drängenden Aufgabe, zusätzlichen und bezahlbaren Wohnraum zu ermöglichen, und müssen dabei unter anderem mit steigenden Baukosten und weniger Personal umgehen. Zugleich müssen auf lokaler Ebene Antworten auf Fragen des Klimaschutzes und der Klimafolgenanpassung gefunden und die Transformation von einer linearen, ressourcenintensiven Wirtschaft hin zu einer zirkulären gestaltet werden.
Wissenstransfer zwischen kommunaler Praxis und Wissenschaft
Im Netzwerk Stadtentwicklung NRW haben sich rund 170 Kommunen unterschiedlicher Größe aus ganz Nordrhein-Westfalen zusammengeschlossen. Ziel des Netzwerks ist es, den Erfahrungsaustausch zwischen den Städten zu fördern, Wissen zu aktuellen Fragen der Stadtentwicklung zu vermitteln und Kommunen bei der Entwicklung von Lösungsansätzen für gemeinsame Herausforderungen zu unterstützen. Unter dem Dach des Netzwerks arbeiten fünf Arbeitsgemeinschaften mit unterschiedlichen fachlichen Schwerpunkten.
Zur Person
Prof. Dr. Guido Spars ist Stadt- und Immobilienökonom und Inhaber des Lehrstuhls Ökonomie des Planens und Bauens an der Bergischen Universität Wuppertal. Der Diplom-Volkswirt promovierte zum Doktor der Ingenieurwissenschaften und habilitierte sich an der Technischen Universität Berlin mit der Lehrbefugnis für Stadt- und Regionalökonomie, insbesondere Immobilienwirtschaft.
Seine Forschungsschwerpunkte liegen in der Stadt- und Immobilienökonomie, der nachhaltigen Stadt- und Quartiersentwicklung, im Wohnungsbau sowie in der Transformation der Immobilien- und Bauwirtschaft.
Spars leitet zudem den wissenschaftlichen Beirat des Deutschen Instituts für Urbanistik in Berlin, einem Institut, das nah an den Themen des Deutschen Städtetages forscht.

Prof. Dr.-Ing. Steffen Leppla und Tobias Siekemeyer haben am 29. September 2026 den Sustain Award an der Frankfurt University of Applied (Frankfurt UAS) erhalten. Sie wurden für ihr Forschungsprojekt zur Wiederverwertung von Bauabfällen ausgezeichnet. Der Preis ist mit 4.000 Euro dotiert und wird von der Frankfurter Stiftung für Forschung und Bildung gemeinsam mit Procter & Gamble vergeben. Das Ziel der Preisstifter ist es, Nachhaltigkeit in Forschung und Lehre an der Frankfurt UAS zu fördern.
Mit rund 222 Mio. Tonnen verursachen Bauabfälle 54 Prozent des jährlichen Gesamtabfallaufkommens in Deutschland. Die zunehmend schwierige Entsorgung führt zu längeren Transportwegen, steigenden Kosten und einem drohenden Entsorgungsnotstand. Wie sich Bauabfälle wiederverwerten und gleichzeitig Primärrohstoffe einsparen lassen, untersucht das Forschungsprojekt „Kreislauforientierte Material- und Verfahrenskonzepte zur Wiederverwertung von mineralischen Bauabfällen“ der Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences (Frankfurt UAS). Dafür wurde es nun mit dem Sustain Award der Frankfurter Stiftung für Forschung und Bildung ausgezeichnet. Die Preisurkunde nahmen die Forschenden Prof. Dr.-Ing. Steffen Leppla und Tobias Siekemeyer am 29. September 2026 bei einer Preis-Gala im Beisein von Katrin Hechler, Staatssekretärin im Hessischen Ministerium für Arbeit, Integration, Jugend und Soziales, entgegen. Die Auszeichnung ist mit 4.000 Euro dotiert. Mit dem 2024 erstmals ausgelobten Sustain Award möchte die Frankfurter Stiftung für Forschung und Bildung gemeinsam mit dem Förderer Procter & Gamble die Frankfurt UAS in ihren Bestrebungen unterstützen, Nachhaltigkeit in Forschung und Lehre zu verankern.
„Die Frankfurt UAS macht Nachhaltigkeit in ihren Forschungsvorhaben sichtbar und entwickelt Lösungen für die Herausforderungen von morgen. Ein herausragendes Beispiel hierfür ist das nun ausgezeichnete Forschungsprojekt zur Wiederverwertung von mineralischen Bauabfällen“, betont Astrid Schulte, Vorsitzende der Frankfurter Stiftung für Forschung und Bildung.
„Nachhaltigkeit braucht neue Ideen, wissenschaftliche Exzellenz und vor allem den Mut, bestehende Lösungen zu hinterfragen. Genau hier setzt der Sustain Award an: Er macht Projekte sichtbar, die in vorbildlicher Weise einen konkreten Beitrag für die Zukunft leisten und zeigt auf, wie Forschung gesellschaftliche Herausforderungen in Lösungen übersetzen kann, die funktionieren. Wir freuen uns, gemeinsam mit der Frankfurter Stiftung für Forschung und Bildung dieses Engagement an der Frankfurt UAS zu fördern und junge Talente auf ihrem Weg zu nachhaltigen Innovationen zu unterstützen“, so Gabriele Hässig, Geschäftsführerin Kommunikation & Nachhaltigkeit bei Procter & Gamble DACH.
„Als Hochschule wollen wir mit unserer Forschung Lösungen für eine nachhaltige Entwicklung bereitstellen und den verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit Ressourcen fördern. Wir danken der Frankfurter Stiftung für Forschung und Bildung sowie Procter & Gamble für die Unterstützung solcher Forschungsprojekte“, so Prof. Dr. Susanne Rägle, Vizepräsidentin für Forschung, Transfer und Internationalisierung der Frankfurt UAS.
Bauabfälle als Ressource nutzen
Die Verknappung von Deponiekapazitäten für Bauabfälle stellt das Entsorgungsmanagement in Deutschland vor große Herausforderungen. Modellrechnungen der Forschenden zeigen, dass in mehreren Bundesländern bereits vor 2030 die verfügbaren Deponiekapazitäten für bestimmte Bauabfälle ausgeschöpft sein könnten. Das Forschungsprojekt untersucht daher den Einsatz sogenannter zeitweise fließfähiger Bodenbaustoffe (ZFSB). Hierfür werden Aushub- und Bodenmaterialien mit Wasser, Tonmineralien und geringen Mengen Zement aufbereitet und für Baugrundverbesserungsmaßnahmen nutzbar gemacht. Dadurch lassen sich mineralische Bauabfälle wiederverwerten und zugleich Primärrohstoffe wie Kies oder Sand ersetzen. Im Fokus der Forschung stehen die technische Umsetzbarkeit, das mechanische Verhalten sowie die umwelttechnische Eignung der Baustoffe. Erste Laboruntersuchungen zeigen, dass insbesondere Schwermetalle durch Tonminerale zuverlässig gebunden werden können. Langfristig soll nachgewiesen werden, dass die Materialien sicher und praxistauglich in realen Bauvorhaben eingesetzt werden können. Das Verfahren könnte einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Ressourcenschonung, zur Einsparung von Deponievolumen und zur Reduktion von CO₂-Emissionen leisten.
Mit dem Preisgeld möchten Leppla und Siekemeyer weitere umweltanalytische Untersuchungen zur Immobilisierung von Schadstoffen finanzieren. Die Laborversuche werden extern durchgeführt. Zudem sollen studentische Hilfskräfte die Probenherstellung, Dokumentation und Auswertung unterstützen.
Das Projekt überzeugte die Jury durch seinen Beitrag zur nachhaltigen Transformation der Bauwirtschaft: Es zeigt einen praxisnahen Weg auf, Bauabfälle als Ressource im Sinne der Kreislaufwirtschaft zu nutzen, Deponievolumen einzusparen und CO₂-Emissionen zu reduzieren. Zur Jury gehören neben Astrid Schulte, Gabriele Hässig und Prof. Dr. Susanne Rägle zudem Gabriele Holzner, Organisationsentwicklerin und Change-Beraterin sowie ehemalige Programmdirektorin und stellvertretende Intendantin des Hessischen Rundfunks, Sönke Reimers, Senior Media Professional, B2B-Experte und vormalig CEO der dfv Mediengruppe, Dr. Christine Lemaitre, CEO Deutsche Gesellschaft für Nachhaltiges Bauen, sowie Michael Müller, Vorstandsvorsitzender der Wirtschaftsinitiative Frankfurt Rhein-Main.
Der Sustain Award würdigt darüber hinaus weitere herausragende Nachhaltigkeitsprojekte der Frankfurt UAS: Platz zwei ging an fabricGREEN, ein Forschungsprojekt zu textilbasierten Grünfassaden für klimaresiliente Städte. Den dritten Platz belegte das Projekt „Innovative Pflegequalifizierung“, das die Integration internationaler Pflegefachkräfte fördert und einen Beitrag zur Fachkräftesicherung im Gesundheitswesen leistet. Insgesamt haben sich in diesem Jahr 13 herausragende Projekte um den Sustain Award 2026 beworben, darunter Forschungs- und Lehr- und Studierendenprojekte, Mentoring- und Weiterbildungsprogramme. Alle liefern einen wertvollen Beitrag, sowohl für die nachhaltige Entwicklung der Gesellschaft als auch für das nachhaltige Profil der Hochschule.
Über den Sustain Award
Die Frankfurt UAS orientiert sich an den 17 Zielen für nachhaltige Entwicklung (Sustainable Development Goals), wie sie in der Agenda 2030 der Vereinten Nationen dokumentiert sind, und hat eine eigene Nachhaltigkeitsstrategie entwickelt. Diese Bestrebungen fördert die Frankfurter Stiftung für Forschung und Bildung mit Unterstützung des Konsumgüterunternehmens Procter & Gamble mit der jährlichen Auslobung des Sustain Awards. Neben fachwissenschaftlicher Exzellenz und einer spezifisch praxisrelevanten Bedeutung zählt die sozial, wirtschaftlich und ökologisch nachhaltige Bedeutung der eingereichten Projekte.

Wann kommt das Molekül aus der Säule?

Die Bioinformatiker und Autoren der aktuellen Publikation in „Nature Methods“: Prof. Dr. Sebastian Böcker (l.) und Fleming Kretschmer von der Universität Jena.
| Quelle:
Foto: Nicole Nerger/Uni Jena
Download
Forschende der Universität Jena entwickeln mit Partnern aus München ein KI-Verfahren, das Retentionszeiten kleiner Moleküle zuverlässiger vorhersagen kann
Ob in der Wirkstoffsuche, der Umweltanalytik oder der Metabolomik: Wer komplexe biologische Proben untersucht, muss häufig herausfinden, welche kleinen Moleküle darin enthalten sind. Forschende der Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena haben gemeinsam mit Partnern vom Helmholtz Zentrum München und der Technischen Universität München ein Verfahren entwickelt, das ein seit Jahrzehnten bestehendes Problem der analytischen Chemie adressiert. In der aktuellen Ausgabe des Fachmagazins „Nature Methods“ stellt das Team um Bioinformatiker Prof. Dr. Sebastian Böcker sein neues Tool vor.
Ein alltägliches Problem der chemischen Analytik
In biologischen Proben wie Blut, Zellmaterial oder Bakterienkulturen können sehr viele unterschiedliche Moleküle vorkommen. Während DNA und Proteine heute mit etablierten Verfahren vergleichsweise gut analysiert werden können, ist die Vielfalt kleiner Moleküle — sogenannter Metabolite — besonders groß. Zu ihnen gehören Stoffwechselprodukte, Naturstoffe, Gifte, Abbauprodukte und viele Arzneistoffe.
Um solche Moleküle voneinander zu trennen, wird häufig Flüssigchromatographie eingesetzt. Dabei wandert ein Stoffgemisch durch eine Trennsäule; einzelne Moleküle werden unterschiedlich stark zurückgehalten und treten deshalb zu verschiedenen Zeiten aus der Säule aus. Diese sogenannte „Retentionszeit“ liefert einen wichtigen Hinweis darauf, welche Substanz in einer Probe vorliegt. Doch wann genau kommt ein bestimmtes Molekül aus der Säule heraus? Genau diese Frage beschäftigt die analytische Chemie seit Jahrzehnten.
Warum bisherige Vorhersagen an Grenzen stoßen
„Die Schwierigkeit besteht darin, dass Retentionszeiten stark von den experimentellen Bedingungen abhängen: von der verwendeten Säule, dem Lösungsmittel, dem Gradienten, dem pH-Wert, der Temperatur und sogar von scheinbar kleinen technischen Änderungen“, sagt Prof. Böcker. „Wird etwa ein Schlauch im Gerät ausgetauscht oder ist ein neuer Schlauch etwas länger als der alte, können sich die gemessenen Zeiten deutlich verschieben.“
Bisherige Modelle mussten daher häufig mit Daten aus genau dem Messsystem trainiert oder nachjustiert werden, auf dem sie später Vorhersagen machen sollten. In der Praxis bedeutet das: Forschende müssten zunächst zahlreiche Standardsubstanzen messen, bevor sie das Modell sinnvoll einsetzen können. Das ist aufwendig, teuer und für viele Anwendungen schlicht nicht möglich.
Erst die Ordnung, dann die Zeit
Der neue Ansatz aus Böckers Team ist nicht auf ein System beschränkt, sondern kann Vorhersagen selbst für neue Systeme und unbekannte Moleküle machen. Die Methode fokussiert sich dabei auf die am häufigsten verwendete Art von Flüssigchromatographie, den sogenannte „Reversed-phase“-Modus, und arbeitet in zwei Schritten: Im ersten Schritt berechnet ein maschinelles Lernmodell für ein Molekül einen sogenannten Retention Order Index. Dieser Index beschreibt nicht unmittelbar eine Zeit, sondern die Position eines Moleküls in der erwarteten Abfolge der Retentionsordnung. Im zweiten Schritt wird dieser Index mithilfe weniger bekannter Referenzpunkte auf konkrete Retentionszeiten übertragen.
An der Entwicklung war maßgeblich Fleming Kretschmer beteiligt, der im Rahmen seiner Promotion an dem Verfahren gearbeitet hat und Co-Erstautor des Papers ist. „Ein zentrales Ergebnis unserer Arbeit ist, dass unsere Methode andere Ansätze übertrifft, die im Gegensatz zu unserer erst aufwendig auf dem Zielsystem trainiert werden müssen“, betont Fleming Kretschmer. „Unser Ansatz ermöglicht also präzise Vorhersagen out-of-the-box auch für neue Systeme.“
Relevanz für Wirkstoffsuche, Naturstoffforschung und Umweltanalytik
Der Ansatz kann überall dort helfen, wo unbekannte kleine Moleküle identifiziert werden sollen. In der Naturstoffforschung etwa suchen Forschende nach Substanzen aus Bakterien, Pilzen oder Pflanzen, die als neue Antibiotika, Krebsmedikamente oder Wirkstoffe gegen andere Krankheiten infrage kommen. Auch in der Umweltanalytik, Lebensmittelchemie oder pharmazeutischen Forschung stellt sich immer wieder dieselbe Frage: Was ist in einer komplexen Probe enthalten — und passt die gemessene Retentionszeit zu der vermuteten chemischen Struktur?
Software soll in Analysewerkzeuge einfließen
Das neue Tool mit dem Namen „2-step“ ist als Softwarepaket und als Webanwendung verfügbar (
https://github.com/boecker-lab/2-step
). Nach Einschätzung der Forschenden kann die Methode künftig in viele Analyseprogramme integriert werden und so automatisch von Laboren genutzt werden, die mit Flüssigchromatographie und Massenspektrometrie arbeiten.
