title: Ride1Up just launched a 28 MPH German mid-drive e-bike for an insanely low $1,295
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 2 2026 - 4:16 am PT
There are cheap e-bikes, and there are good mid-drive e-bikes. Those two circles on the Venn diagram don’t overlap nearly as often as we’d like. But Ride1Up’s newly launched Prodigy V2 Eco is doing its best to smash them together with a surprisingly low
$1,295 price tag
And this isn’t a $1,300 bike with some no-name mid-drive motor you’ve never heard of. At the heart of the Prodigy V2 Eco is a German-made Brose TF Sprinter mid-drive motor pumping out 90 Nm of torque, paired with a 504 Wh battery using Samsung cells.
In other words, the expensive bits are still there.
The Prodigy line has been around
for several years now
, and Ride1Up has historically used it as the company’s more premium mid-drive offering. The new Eco version appears to take that same basic formula and ask a fairly simple question: How much can we shave off the price without cutting into the parts that actually make the bike so good?
The answer, apparently, is quite a lot.
Ride1Up has made some component concessions compared to its higher-end Prodigy builds. The fancier Maxxis rubber is gone in favor of more affordable tires, while the higher-spec four-piston hydraulic brakes have been replaced with 180mm two-piston hydraulic brakes. The drivetrain is also a fairly pedestrian 9-speed setup with a microSHIFT Advent derailleur and Shimano Alivio 11-34T cassette.
These are all fine parts, but not top shelf components like you’d find on a $4,000 Specialized or Trek. However the battery and motor – basically the heart and soul of the bike – could stand toe to toe with those top tier bike shop e-bikes any day of the week.
And those are exactly the kinds of compromises I like to see on a value-focused e-bike. Save money on the components that are relatively easy and inexpensive to replace someday, not on the expensive electrical drivetrain buried in the middle of the bike. If my tires wear out a bit faster, I can decide to put on nicer rubber later. But giving me a $3,000 e-bike for less than half the price – now that’s a deal.
And that’s what it looks like the company is doing, because Ride1Up didn’t cheap out there. You still get the Brose mid-drive with its integrated torque sensor, a 36V 14Ah battery, and Class 3 performance up to 28 mph (45 km/h).
There’s also a 100mm suspension fork with lockout (though here too, it’s not clear which fork they went with), integrated front and rear lights, full-coverage fenders, a 40 lb-rated rear rack, an adjustable stem, and 27.5-inch wheels. The bike comes in both step-through and step-over frame styles, which in lieu of multiple frame sizes, gives riders a ‘shorter’ and ‘taller’ mounting option.
Perhaps the most eyebrow-raising part is simply
what $1,295 buys you here
compared to the rest of the market.
Ride1Up itself points toward bikes like Trek’s FX+ 7S and Allant+ 8S, as well as the Specialized Turbo Vado SL 2 5.0, all of which sit north of $4,000. That’s not to say these are apples-to-apples comparisons; premium dealer brands bring their own advantages in component selection, dealer support, frame engineering, refinement, and service networks.
But when we’re talking about more than a three-fold difference in sticker price, it’s hard not to notice.
A $1,295 hub-motor e-bike
isn’t particularly surprising anymore. We’ve seen plenty of those. A $1,295 e-bike with a 90 Nm Brose mid-drive, torque sensor, Samsung-celled 504 Wh battery, hydraulic brakes, suspension, fenders, lights, and a rear rack? That’s a very different proposition.
And frankly, it’s the kind of aggressive pricing that makes you wonder just how much room is left beneath the premium e-bike market.
The Prodigy V2 Eco is currently listed for pre-order
at $1,295
, with Ride1Up indicating shipments are expected to begin in the next couple of weeks.
Hopefully we’ll get to test one of these out for you soon, but until then, check out my review of the Prodigy V2 below, which is largely the same e-bike but with a bit nicer brakes, tires, and other components.

title: Rivian continues to ramp with R2 even as EV market growth slows
content:
Rivian posted its third-quarter production and delivery numbers this morning and, with the R2, remains on track to meet its annual targets despite some headwinds across the US electric vehicle sector.
Rivian’s 2026 production and delivery output has accelerated steadily through the year as it now ramps up R2 production:
- Q1 2026: Produced 10,236 vehicles and delivered 10,365.
- Q2 2026: Produced 12,613 vehicles and delivered 12,194, outperforming initial quarterly expectations. R2 is part of this acceleration
- Q3 2026: Produced 19,751 vehicles and delivered 19,248.
Taken in a vacuum, the numbers are impressive:
- 58%: Quarter-over-quarter surge in vehicle deliveries from Q2 to Q3, likely helped by R2 ramp.
- 41,807: Total vehicles delivered through the first three quarters of 2026.
- 65,000 – 70,000: Reaffirmed full-year delivery guidance range, requiring roughly 23,000 to 28,000 deliveries in Q4 to hit targets. That seems likely given Rivian’s ramp and the introduction of the Premium version in “late 2026”
Obviously, the lower-cost R2 is likely responsible for much, if not all, of this growth, even though Rivian is selling only the higher-cost Performance version through the end of the year. Rivian this week announced that its Lidar suite wouldn’t reach customers until 2027, a pushback from its original late 2026 target.
Zooming out: The broader U.S. EV transition is experiencing a reality check in 2026.
- EV share of U.S. light-duty vehicle sales has hovered around 6%–7% this year, down from a peak above 10% in 2025.
- The loss of federal purchase credits in late 2025, paired with elevated interest rates, has driven down overall EV growth rates and led several legacy automakers to push back ambitious electrification timelines.
- Electricity prices have risen because of AI infrastructure and other factors, but the Iran War has driven up gas prices even more.
Top comment by lostnspace
Glad to see early signals that the R2 is going to be a real success for Rivian. A 58% jump in deliveries quarter over quarter, with only the Performance trim on sale, is a strong start.
That said, it's hard to look at the broader EV slowdown without noting that this administration did the market no favors. Demonizing EVs, pulling the federal credits, and actively working against adoption has made a tough transition tougher.
The economy is the other piece. People like me are sitting on the wait-and-see fence. I'm not going to commit to a car loan and then find myself looking for a job a few months later.
I also agree with the commenters saying price point is everything. With everything costing more, it's increasingly hard to justify a $60k to $80k vehicle. The R2 only becomes the car Rivian needs it to be once the trims that avoid sticker shock actually reach buyers.
Rivian will release its full Q3 2026 financial results after market close on October 29, 2026, followed by an investor webcast and Q&A session at 5:00 p.m. ET. We’ll be covering it live.
Electrek’s take:
Rivian’s ability to nearly double its quarterly delivery volume since Q1 shows improving manufacturing efficiency at its Normal, Illinois facility, alongside growing demand for its core R1 vehicles, commercial delivery vans, and, more to the point, newly introduced R2 Performance.
While the overall average sale price will be lower on the R2 compared to the flagship R1 vehicles, the Performance version, which is now exclusively being sold, should still have an ASP close to the R1.
Anecdotally, I’m getting an itchy trigger finger on the Performance version, especially after reviewing it this summer, even though I promised myself I would wait for the Lidar suite and V2X updates.

title: Tesla (TSLA) Q3 2026 deliveries slip 2% to 486,532, but beat estimates
content:
TSLA - Tesla Stock Price
Fred Lambert
| Oct 2 2026 - 6:11 am PT
Tesla (TSLA) delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter of 2026, down 2.1% from the record 497,099 it delivered in the same quarter last year.
That’s still about 25,000 more than Wall Street expected, with the consensus at 461,974 deliveries. Tesla also delivered about 22,000 more vehicles than it built.
Breaking down the numbers
According to Tesla’s
production and delivery report
, the company produced 464,391 vehicles and delivered 486,532 in Q3 2026.
Model 3 and Model Y accounted for 478,237 of those deliveries. “Other Models,” which now means the Cybertruck, the Semi, and whatever Model S and Model X inventory is left, added 8,295. That’s down 48% from 15,933 a year ago.
Here’s the full breakdown:
Production
Deliveries
Model 3/Y
Other Models
Tesla delivered 22,141 more vehicles than it built. That’s the second quarter in a row that it has worked down inventory, and between Q2 and Q3, it has now cleared the
roughly 50,000 excess vehicles it built in Q1
Down from last year’s tax credit record
The year-over-year comparison was always going to be tough. Tesla
delivered 497,099 vehicles in Q3 2025
, still its all-time record, when US buyers rushed to claim the $7,500 federal tax credit before it expired on September 30, 2025.
Against that, 486,532 is a 2.1% drop. It’s also up 1.3% from the
480,126 vehicles Tesla delivered in Q2
Tesla is still ahead for the year. It has delivered 1,324,681 vehicles through three quarters, up 8.8% from 1,217,902 at the same point in 2025.
On expectations,
Tesla’s own company-compiled consensus
had 24 analysts averaging 461,974 deliveries. Individual
estimates ranged from 421,758 at Cantor Fitzgerald to 482,000 at JPMorgan
, with prediction markets in the low-to-mid 470,000s.
Tesla beat the consensus by 24,558 units, and it beat every estimate on that list.
Energy storage misses expectations
Tesla also deployed 13.7 GWh of energy storage products in Q3, up 9.6% from the 12.5 GWh it deployed a year ago and up from 13.5 GWh in Q2.
That’s short of the 14.2 GWh record Tesla set in Q4 2025, and well below the 15.9 GWh analysts expected.
Electrek’s Take
I said earlier this week that I expected Tesla’s deliveries to be roughly flat to slightly down versus Q3 last year, and that’s what we got. Wall Street was too low again.
High gas prices are doing a lot of the work here. They’re replacing most of the demand Tesla lost in the US when the tax credit expired, and exports out of Shanghai are covering for
weak retail sales in China
The good news is that Tesla didn’t build inventory to get here. But volume isn’t profit. Tesla
badly missed on profit in Q2
, and it
just lined up $30 billion in credit
Meanwhile, BYD outsold Tesla by about 276,000 EVs in a single quarter. Imagine where Tesla would be with a $25,000 to $30,000 model in production during a gas price crisis. That was the plan before Elon bet the house on autonomy.

title: Tesla might charge you up $25,000 if you use its latest feature
content:
Tesla Supercharger
Fred Lambert
| Oct 2 2026 - 7:59 am PT
Tesla says its new “Emergency Drive Away” feature can do up to $25,000 in damage to a Supercharger every time someone uses it, and the car needs a mandatory service visit too.
Tesla has since released more details about the feature in response to owner questions. But Tesla hasn’t said who gets that bill.
Yesterday,
Tesla launched Emergency Drive Away
, which lets drivers shift into Drive and pull away while still plugged into a Supercharger. It arrived two months after a gunman shot three people in Teslas at a Supercharger station in Twin Falls, Idaho.
Tesla was upfront that the feature “will damage your vehicle and the Supercharger.” It didn’t put a number on that damage until an owner asked what to expect, physically and financially.
Tesla’s charging team answered:
Depends on the Supercharger, but electrical & civil cost can be up to $25k. Service visit mandatory for the chargeport. Only use in case of an emergency.
That’s “up to,” and Tesla says it depends on the Supercharger. Still, “electrical and civil” is construction language.
The car doesn’t get away clean either. Tesla says a service visit for the charge port is mandatory, and it didn’t give a price for that.
There’s a cleanup too. Another owner asked about the liquid gushing out of the charger in Tesla’s demo video. Tesla said it’s glycol, the coolant in the cable, and that it will clean it up as part of a “mandatory service visit to the Supercharger.”
$25,000 is 40% of a new Supercharger post
For scale, look at Tesla’s own price list. Its
Supercharger for Business configurator
puts an eight-post V4 site at $500,000 in hardware, or $62,500 per post, before installation. Tesla’s worst-case repair is 40% of that.
It’s also more than 80 times the price of EVject, the $299 breakaway adapter that owners started recommending again after Twin Falls.
Tesla sued EVject in 2024
over overheating claims.
Tesla skipped the question about who pays
Several owners asked Tesla directly who pays, including whether a driver who uses the feature in a real emergency is responsible for the Supercharger repair.
Tesla didn’t answer them. Its account kept replying to other questions in the same thread, confirming that the feature works on V2, V3, and V4 stalls and that it doesn’t work on home chargers.
It did answer one about penalties. Asked if there are any for misuse, Tesla replied “Yes,” and its launch post says deliberate misuse “will invoke additional penalties.” It hasn’t said what those are, or how it will decide what counts as misuse.
Tesla has an easy way to collect. Every Supercharger session runs through a Tesla account with a payment method on file, which is how it bills idle and congestion fees.
And $25,000 is more than the minimum insurance coverage in a lot of states. In Idaho, where the Twin Falls shooting happened, drivers only have to carry $15,000 in property damage liability. New York requires $10,000. Pennsylvania, $5,000.

title: 2027 Hyundai Tucson Bets On Hybrids And A Modern Infotainment System
content:
2027 Hyundai Tucson Bets On Hybrids And A Modern Infotainment System
Hyundai’s best-seller is bigger, more efficient, and fancier than ever.
- The all-new Hyundai Tucson debuted last night in New York.
- Hyundai’s best-seller is bigger, more powerful, and leans more on hybridization than its predecessor.
- Both the hybrid and plug-in hybrid come with two electric motors, and the PHEV gets a bigger battery.
There’s a new Hyundai Tucson, and it looks nothing like its predecessor. The compact crossover has been Hyundai’s breadwinner for the longest time, and now the 2027 Tucson brings an exterior design that seems to have been made with little more than a ruler, a properly modern infotainment system, and an emphasis on hybridization.
I’ll start with what’s under the hood. All 2027 Tucsons come with a 1.6-liter turbocharged gas engine, which can be had in three configurations: a traditional combustion setup with 184 horsepower, a traditional hybrid, and a plug-in hybrid. That’s the same as the outgoing model, but it’s the details that matter here, because the latest-gen Tucson is more powerful, more efficient, and the hybrid models get more electric motors.
The traditional hybrid has a 17-horsepower (13-kilowatt) electric motor bolted at the rear of the gas engine, directly to the crankshaft. This little pancake-like motor replaces the traditional belt-driven starter-generator, but it can also send power to the wheels during hard acceleration and send energy back to the high-voltage battery during deceleration.
The hybrid’s main motor, however, is a more powerful unit sandwiched between the little electric motor and six-speed automatic transmission. It makes 64 hp (47.7 kW) on its own and is energized by a 1.49-kilowatt-hour battery rated at 270 volts. The main e-motor and its accompanying battery are the same as on the outgoing Tucson hybrid, but the addition of the crank-integrated motor is new. The crank-mounted motor, however, is new.
2027 Hyundai Tucson Limited
Hyundai says the 2027 Tucson Hybrid can get up to 42 miles per gallon when specced with front-wheel drive and 17-inch wheels, while the all-wheel drive models get between 40 and 42 mpg. That’s better than the 38 and 36 mpg achieved by the previous model. The combined power output is also slightly higher, with the new Tucson hybrid putting down 233 horsepower and 279.9 pound-feet of torque, up from the previous generation’s 231 hp and 271 lb-ft.
The 2027 Tucson Plug-In Hybrid gets the same engine and electric motor layout as the hybrid, but with a higher output and a larger-capacity high-voltage battery that enables a more-than-decent electric driving range. The PHEV’s main e-motor makes 106 hp (79 kW), up from the previous model’s 97 hp, leading to an overall output of 288 hp, a 20 hp increase over the previous generation.
2027 Hyundai Tucson XRT
The traction battery also got a capacity boost to 17.1 kWh, up from 13.8 kWh, leading to an estimated all-electric range of roughly 50 miles on a full charge. That’s quite an impressive figure, but I’d take it with a grain of salt because Hyundai didn’t say whether it’s on the NEDC, WLTP, or EPA cycle. By comparison, the 2026 Tucson PHEV has a 32-mile EPA-estimated electric range on a full battery. There’s no DC fast charging, and the on-board AC charger is capped at 7.2 kW.
All powertrain options come with an integrated electric water pump, and the hybrid model gets a Stay Mode, which keeps the A/C, heating, and audio running even when the engine is turned off.
Here’s the catch, though. Hyundai only released official specifications for the gas and hybrid versions, leaving the plug-in hybrid’s U.S. status unknown. I reached out to the company to find out whether the PHEV is coming stateside, and I’ll update this story when I hear back. Logic dictates that the 2027 Hyundai Tucson will be sold as a plug-in hybrid here, though, as the outgoing model is also available with a PHEV powertrain.
Size-wise, the automaker’s best-selling model is bigger in every metric than its predecessor. The 2027 crossover is 2.3 inches longer, 1.57 in wider, and 0.8 in taller than the previous generation, totalling 185 in in length, 75 in in width, and 66.3 in in height. The wheelbase is 109.6 in, and the rear doors now open 10 degrees wider than before, up to 83 degrees. The standard models’ ground clearance is 7.1 in (180 mm), while the off-road-flavored XRT PRO trim gets an extra 1.1 in for a total of 8.2 in (210 mm). Cargo volume stands at 41.7 cubic feet.
Inside, the new Tucson gets Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system that pairs a 12.9- or 17-inch central touchscreen with a 9.9-inch slim digital gauge cluster. Based on Android Automotive OS, Pleos Connect comes with Gleo AI, a natural-sounding voice assistant that can take complex commands without the driver having to fiddle with the screen. And because it’s based on AAOS, drivers can install third-party apps like Spotify, Waze, and others. Over-the-air software updates are also part of the deal.
Thankfully, Hyundai hasn’t forgotten about proper buttons, with a row of physical controls under the main touchscreen for essential functions.
The 2027 Hyundai Tucson with gas and hybrid powertrains will launch in the U.S. in early 2027, with the plug-in hybrid expected to follow.

title: Dead: Mercedes-Benz EQE Sedan
content:
The electric E-Class alternative is out of the picture for 2027. The same goes for the top-spec EQS SUV and AMG S-Class.

Mercedes-Benz is discontinuing two EVs and a plug-in hybrid from its 2027 U.S. lineup.
The EQE Sedan is out of the picture completely.
The casualties also include the most expensive version of the EQS SUV and the performance S-Class plug-in hybrid.
Mercedes-Benz EQE electric sedan
is joining
America’s growing EV graveyard
after the German automaker has decided to axe all trims from its 2027 U.S. lineup. The battery-powered E-Class alternative survived just three years stateside, where its sales figures have been lukewarm at best.
Now, all EQE Sedan trims are out of the picture, including the hot AMG flavor, as confirmed by a company spokesperson quoted by
Car and Driver
. But the EQE Sedan isn’t the only casualty.

Mercedes-Maybach EQS 680 electric SUV
, which starts at an eye-watering $180,000, has also been discontinued in the U.S. for the 2027 model year. The rest of the EQS lineup, Sedan and SUV included, is still on sale.

Car and Driver
. The PHEV retails for $191,050, pairing a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 engine with a single electric motor for a combined output of 791 horsepower.
The ultra-expensive sedan’s high-voltage battery can hold 10.4 kilowatt-hours of energy, resulting in an all-electric range of just 16 miles. But the S63 E was never about efficiency—it was about outrageous performance and street presence. Now, though, it’s gone.

title: General Motors' EV Sales Are Way Down. But It's Not As Bleak As It Seems
content:
Silverado EV sales fell 92% year over year. But it's more to do with tax credits than anything else.
Photo by:
Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
2:09pm ET
Last year's Q3 was a big one for GM. It
sold 66,501 EVs in Q3 2025
, making last year its strongest ever for electric vehicles. This year, things look different.
Q3 EV sales fell by more than a third
, only 25,473 electric cars delivered. While that drop is massive, it likely has more to do with the loss of federal tax credits and an industry reset than a lack of demand for GM's electric portfolio.
The Trump administration eliminated the federal tax break for $7,500 EV buyers one year ago. Many buyers pulled ahead their purchases, racing to get EVs before the tax credit ended on September 30, 2025. That led to GM's record third quarter last year, which may have over-inflated its sales perceptions.
So this drop off more likely just a recalibration toward normal than it is customers losing interest in electric Chevys and Cadillacs. EV and hybrid sales are down across the board in the U.S., not just at GM,
despite growing consumer interest
. These vehicles are more expensive than they were last year, and the regulations that
incentivized automakers to sell more EVs have been largely dismantled
Some electric GM models are still selling pretty well, though, even though Cadillac seems to be doing most of the heavy lifting. America's luxury brand had two of GM's three best-selling EVs in Q3. The
Cadillac Optiq
recorded 4,550 deliveries. The return of the Chevy Bolt took the number two spot, with 3,866 deliveries, and the Cadillac Lyriq was close behind with 3,617. The Cadillac Vistiq did well, too, with 2,587 sales.
Photo by: Jeff Perez / Motor1
Perhaps unsurprisingly, the cheaper models suffered the most. The previous tax incentives benefited affordable car buyers most, as rich folk don't need the extra discount. So the Chevy Equinox EV saw the biggest sales fall from last year, at a massive 92.4%. The
Blazer EV
dropped 84.4%, too. Interestingly, both EV pickups dropped a similar amount, with the Silverado EV falling 58% and the Sierra EV losing 50.8% of sales. Cadillac Escalade IQ and IQL sales fell only 29.2%. The outlier is the Hummer EV, which saw a massive 72.9% decline. (The Chevy Bolt might technically have improved in sales but that's only because it wasn't on sale during Q3 2025.)
It might seem like doom and gloom, over at GM's electrified lineup, but only if you just look at the sales sheet without context. This year, GM is only down from a record year. If anything, this proves how effective federal tax incentives are for customers to switch over to electric. As demand recovers and gas prices rise, we'll see how long it takes for GM to reach its previous high water mark.

title: Germany Wants Parked EVs To Earn Money
content:
Germany is clearing the way for EV owners to sell power back to the grid, provided their cars and chargers are up to the job.
8:22am ET
Germany’s new rules make it easier for EV owners to earn money by selling electricity back to the grid.
Drivers need a V2G-capable car, compatible charging equipment, and the right electricity contract.
Nationwide implementation could take until September 2027, and earnings will depend on costs and contract terms.
Your parked car does little other than depreciate and lose you money over time. But that may change if you have an electric car in Germany because the country wants to streamline EVs earning money by supplying electricity back into the grid when it’s needed most.
Yesterday,
Germany’s Federal Network Agency
adopted rules called MiSpeL, covering electricity storage and bidirectional charging points. The idea is pretty simple: store cheap electricity in EV battery packs, then sell it when prices rise.
But while that sounds simple enough, the paperwork to make it happen has been considerably less straightforward. This is because previously, mixing grid electricity with locally generated renewable power complicated eligibility for Germany’s renewable energy support program.
The new framework lets owners store solar power and grid electricity in the same battery without losing eligible solar subsidies. Previously, batteries generally had to store only locally generated renewable electricity to qualify for subsidies. Charging the same battery from the grid went against that condition.
More On This
The new rule gives ways to account for the two sources separately. They also reduce certain fees on electricity sent back to the grid, although those fees still apply to electricity used for driving.
However, an essential hardware requirement remains. To take part, EVs must support
bidirectional charging
capable of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operations, paired with compatible charging equipment, metering, and a specific electricity contract. The type of bidirectional charging is important, because simply having a vehicle-to-load (V2L) outlet for plugging in a coffee maker doesn’t qualify the car to trade electricity.
The VDA (the main trade group for Germany’s car industry) liked the updated rules, noting that regulators listened to their feedback about how power is measured. Now, their main goal is to implement these rules quickly and evenly across the country.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
This won't happen right away. Grid and meter companies have until September 30, 2027, to get ready, unless they choose to opt in sooner. Additionally, a simplified setup for home solar panels still needs official approval from European Union regulators.
Germany isn’t guaranteeing your electric car will pay for itself. Instead, it’s giving you a simpler way to use the battery in the EV you already own to earn back some money. Whether it’s worth it depends on the cost of the required equipment, the contract terms, and how much the car stays plugged in.
Germany’s effort to make V2G easier is part of a broader global trend. In the United States, there isn't one set of rules for the whole country. Instead, it’s a mix of state laws and local power companies trying their own setups.
California
is pushing to mandate that
all new electric cars can send power back to the grid
, while other states are testing the idea using parked
electric school buses
giant backup batteries
during hot summer days when power use spikes.
In Europe, other countries are trying different approaches to involve EV owners. The Netherlands, for instance, is putting power-sharing chargers right on public streets so people can automatically buy cheap power and sell it back when prices jump. In the UK, energy companies offer special plans that pay drivers with credits on their electric bills for giving energy back to the grid. Meanwhile, in France, carmakers are starting to bundle bidirectional charging-capable home-sharing chargers with new car purchases.

title: Over 60% Of Toyotas Sold In Q3 Were Electrified
content:
Over 60% Of Toyotas Sold In Q3 Were Electrified
A growing proportion of Toyota and Lexus sales are EVs, hybrids, and plug-in hybrids. And the company isn't slowing down any time soon.
- High gas prices due to the war in Iran gave Toyota and Lexus hybrids a boost in Q3.
- The sales of electrified models grew 28.5% even though overall sales were flat.
- The Camry is Toyota's best-selling model so far this year, followed by the RAV4, and Sienna in a distant third.
Toyota’s electrified vehicle sales reached new heights in the third quarter, even as its overall sales were flat over the same period last year. The automaker said Thursday that hybrids, plug-in hybrids, and fully electric models accounted for a record 61% of its sales mix between July and September.
Including both Toyota and Lexus brands, the automaker sold 633,223 vehicles in the U.S. in the third quarter, a 0.6% year-over-year increase. But a whopping 363,367 of those models were electrified, up 28.5% from the same period last year. The vast majority of those were regular hybrids, followed by plug-in hybrids, and fully electric models.
The U.S. war in Iran which began towards the end of February has strained global oil supplies and kept gas prices elevated in the U.S. for a prolonged time period. Analysts said this has nudged buyers towards more fuel-efficient hybrids, boosting the sales for automakers with hybrid-heavy lineups, like Toyota, Honda, Hyundai, and Kia.
2026 Toyota bZ Woodland charging at an Ionna station in New Jersey.
For model-specific sales, Toyota only releases monthly and year-to-date numbers, not quarterly figures.
The automaker sold 931,434 hybrids between January and September this year, and that’s despite the production ramp up of the sixth-generation RAV4, which is now hybrid-only. The RAV4’s overall sales were actually down 6.6% in September as the factory scaled up production, while declining by 29.2% year to date.
However, robust sales growth in the rest of the hybrid lineup, including the Camry, Sienna Hybrid, and Grand Highlander Hybrid made up for that.
The Japanese automaker’s EV sales were nowhere as impressive, but there are some standouts. The sales of the refreshed bZ have doubled from last year, growing 103% to 24,994 units in the first three quarters of this year. That means year-to-date, the bZ is ahead of key rivals like the Chevy Equinox EV (18,154 units), but still lagging behind the Hyundai Ioniq 5 (31,112 units).
Lexus RZ 550e F Sport
The new C-HR and bZ Woodland didn’t quite add meaningful sales volume, with their January-September sales standing at 7,215 units and 2,600 units, respectively. We’ve compared all the new Toyota EVs here at InsideEVs—you can read that review here.
For Lexus, the RX crossover continued to be the brand’s top-seller. Of the 89,824 RXs sold year-to-date, 37,448 were hybrids and 5,738 plug-in hybrids. Sales of the fully electric RZ also doubled through September to 10,214 units. As expected, the new generation ES Hybrid is outselling its all-electric counterpart by more than double, with 5,133 units versus the EV’s 2,083 units.

title: Tesla Will Now Let You Drive Away From A Supercharger In An Emergency
content:
Tesla says misuse of the feature could result in "additional penalties," since each use can cause up to $25,000 in damages.
Photo by:
11:54am ET
Tesla will begin rolling out a new Emergency Drive Away feature to its vehicles.
This will let cars drive away from a Tesla Supercharger while still connected to the stall.
It warns that the safety feature is only to be used in emergencies and can cause up to $25,000 in damages to the charger.
Tesla is releasing a
new safety feature
for its cars. It's not automatic collision evasion—
that was last month
—instead, it's something that will allow owners to escape dangerous scenarios when their cars are stationary.
The feature is called "Emergency Drive Away," and it allows owners to quickly drive away when charging at a
Tesla Supercharging station
while the charger is still connected to their car. In an
, Max de Zegher, Tesla's senior director of charging for North America, called it "a feature we hope you never need."
"We select Supercharger locations with safety in mind and relocate sites deemed unsafe. Our goal is that you always feel safe getting out to unplug," he said. "We went back and forth on this for years, but believe offering it is the right call. Don't abuse it, so we don't have to restrict it."
It comes just two months after a
high-profile shooting at an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho
that spilled over into a nearby Supercharging station. The gunman opened fire on vehicles at the Supercharging station, including one that was unable to drive away while it was connected to the charger.
To activate the new feature, owners put the car in Drive, accept a pop-up on the screen acknowledging that using the feature will damage both their vehicle and the Supercharging station, and then mash the gas.
Tesla says that using Emergency Drive Away will require a "mandatory" service visit for the vehicle charge port. Slowing down a video Tesla shared shows the motorized charging door going limp, though it's not clear what other damage may have occurred to the port. Driving away with the charger attached also causes the Supercharger's plug to break away from the cable. We can also see the Supercharger's coolant spill from the charging cable.
Tesla says that the cost for electrical and civil envineering work to repair the Supercharging stall can be as high as $25,000, so it's taking all activations of the feature seriously. It will even send recorded clips of each use directly to Tesla, according to the notification shown in Tesla's demo video.
Tesla calls it a "peace of mind feature" and notes that it is only to be used in an emergency. If all of the other warnings aren't enough to dissuade you, Tesla also cautions that deliberate misuse will "invoke additional penalties."

The automaker will begin rolling out Emergency Drive Away to cars via an
over-the-air update
. It warns that it only works on Tesla Superchargers—not third-party charging stations or Level 2 Tesla Wall Connectors—and only in the U.S.

title: The Fathom Is Ford's Shot At EV Redemption. The CEO Knows He Has To Get It Right
content:
Ford's $30,000 electric pickup is its opportunity to reset its EV business, but it won't be easy.
Photo by:
4:53pm ET
Ford's upcoming Fathom is an incredibly important vehicle to the brand.
CEO Jim Farley acknowledged that it's going to be "a heck of an effort" to launch the truck effectively.
There's still a lot that goes into the launch, but Ford is intent on delivering the affordable pickup at scale, at cost, and on time.
Ford has already taken a swing at the whole electric pickup thing. The all-electric
F-150 Lightning
proved—technically and mechanically—that the Blue Oval has the chutzpah to make it happen. But it also demonstrated the most important part of building a car: making something that folks will actually show up to buy.
There's a lot that goes into that recipe. It's not just transplanting an electric powertrain into an existing platform, either. There's a practical reality here, as big batteries cost big bucks. And that's what makes the
upcoming Ford Fathom
considerably more important than its larger, ill-fated brother.
Photo by: Ford
Ford's CEO, Jim Farley, knows this. In fact, he's sweating it. At the
Automotive News Congress
in Detroit earlier this week, Farley made it clear that the automaker pulling out all the stops to get the Fathom release right. Even then, it's a big lift to launch the company's new Universal EV platform in a way that ensures a smooth takeoff.
"It’s going to be a heck of an effort to launch this at scale, at cost, on time," acknowledged Farley.
The Fathom is Ford's attempt to deliver a quality electric vehicle at prices that can compete with Chinese automakers. It studied the biggest names in the country's EV space to
understand what consumers liked about them
. Ford also learned what made them tick—under their hoods and in their silicon brains. Engineers took a look at BYD's vehicles and found a 20% battery cost advantage, and rather than shrug it off, engineers were pushed to rethink motors, gearboxes, and inverters so they could make up the difference without ultimately sacrificing range.
Ford chased weight, battery size, wiring, software, parts count, supplier costs, and more. It needed to figure out how to operate on razor thin margins to deliver what consumers were actually going to use. After all, a sub-$30,000 starting price doesn't leave a lot of room for inefficiencies in an market that is only becoming more globally competitive by the day.
Production of the Fathom is penciled in for 2027 at the
Louisville Assembly Plant,
where the brand is spending north of $2 billion to retool for the production UEV platform vehicles. Add on its
BlueOval Battery Park
and that investment rockets up to $5 billion. The question is whether all of the pieces will come together at the right time. Or, as Farley eloquently puts it, Ford hasn't "landed the plane on mass production of UEV" just yet.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
All of those factors makes Ford's caution fairly understandable. The Fathom can't just be yet another electric science project for the brand. It can't be late. It can't cost more than promised. It has to be a clean launch for consumers to see that Ol' Blue still has it on the electric front.
Now that Ford has dumped billions of dollars into its production line and set the stage for success, it has to do the most complicated part of this whole process. It needs to actually build the trucks. Farley knows that's no easy pitch, but he's taking the company down the hard path anyway.

title: The Tesla Model 3 Gets A Range Bump And A New Screen In The U.S.
content:
American Model 3s still don’t have vehicle-to-load (V2L) functionality, despite the feature being introduced in China.
9:03am ET
The U.S.-spec Tesla Model 3 now comes with a better central touchscreen.
The top Performance trim gains a few miles of range and more power.
Vehicle-to-load, which enables energy export from the high-voltage battery, is still not available stateside.
Tesla Model 3
sold in the United States, Puerto Rico, and Mexico is getting a few improvements, but the four-door electric sedan still doesn’t offer bidirectional charging, despite Tesla adding the functionality overseas.
All U.S.-spec Model 3s, including the base Rear-Wheel Drive trim, come with a larger 16-inch central infotainment touchscreen, which also packs a higher pixel density than the outgoing model’s 15.4-inch display. The company didn’t offer details, but the Model 3’s new screen is probably the same one that made its way into the Model Y crossover a few months ago.
Next up is a slight spec boost for the top-spec
Model 3 Performance
, which can now deliver 316 miles of range on a full charge, up from 309 miles, and 528 horsepower. When the sporty sedan debuted in 2024, its power output was advertised as 510 hp. Despite the power bump, the zero-to-60 miles per hour sprint is the same as before, at 2.9 seconds. The Model 3 Performance also comes with a black headliner now.
Last but not least, the Model 3 Premium All-Wheel Drive can accelerate quicker than before, with a 3.8-second time for the sprint to 60 mph, down from 4.2 seconds before. The 346-mile estimated range is unchanged.
Tesla didn’t say what changes it made under the car’s skin to achieve the range and performance gains. However, it’s clear that the improvements come without a cost increase. All Model 3 trims cost the same, with prices starting at $38,630 for the base Rear-Wheel Drive, $44,130 for the Premium trim, and $56,630 for the Performance trim.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The lack of
vehicle-to-load (V2L)
, however, is a little perplexing.
The feature was announced yesterday
for Model 3s sold in China, Australia, New Zealand, and South Korea, alongside the same 16-inch screen and black headliner as on the U.S.-spec version. V2L may eventually make it on the American Model 3, but as it stands today, the only Tesla EVs offering it stateside are the Cybertruck, Model Y Premium, Model Y Performance, and Model Y L.
An adapter that plugs into the mobile charger enables owners to export up to 2.4 kilowatts from the car’s charging port to power tools, appliances, or camping equipment directly from the high-voltage battery. It can’t power an entire house during an outage, but it will happily keep a fridge and other essentials powered when the grid goes down.

title: Volvo Sales Tumble, Forcing The Company To Abandon Its Full-Year Guidance
content:
Europe is the only market where Volvo is still doing alright. Everywhere else, it’s all red.
Photo by:
7:08am ET
Volvo pulled its sales guidance for the entire year after sales took a dive in China and the U.S.
In the third quarter, the Swedish automaker saw global sales decrease by 10.7% compared to last year.
In the U.S., Volvo sold fewer than 24,000 cars this past quarter, with EVs taking a huge dive.
is facing significant headwinds in China and the United States, where sales have gone down once again this past quarter. As a result, the company decided to pull its full-year sales volume and cash flow guidance, sending shares down as much as 4% in early trades. Since the beginning of the year, Volvo Cars’ shares have lost roughly 50% of their value.
“An increasingly challenging market situation and deteriorating near-term market outlook has resulted in lower-than-expected sales and a weaker full year outlook for Volvo Cars,” the company said in a statement. “Therefore, Volvo Cars will not fulfill the previous full-year 2026 outlook statements on volume and cash flow.”
Volvo's U.S. EV sales nosedived. The arrival of the new EX60 should improve things.
Photo by: Volvo
During the third quarter, the Swedish automaker sold 141,609 cars globally, a 10.7% decrease over the same period last year. Mild hybrids led the drop with 23.6% fewer units sold, followed by plug-in hybrids with an 18% decrease over Q3 2025. Meanwhile, all-electric models kept the company from dropping even more, with a striking 28.6% increase year over year, totaling 45,060 units finding new owners across the world from July through September.
China was the region where Volvo lost the most ground, with 20,284 cars sold, resulting in a 40.6% drop compared to last year. In the United States, the company moved 23,766 cars, 8.7% fewer than last year, with fully electric models tumbling 41.1%. According to the automaker, “weaker consumer sentiment, increased SUV competition, and softer electrified-vehicle demand” impacted its results stateside.
Europe is the only region where the car manufacturer has seen good numbers this past quarter. Sales totaled 90,548 units, up 2% year-over-year, with EVs reaching 40,466 new customers, 51% more than last year.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Volvo’s previous guidance, released in July, predicted much stronger sales in the second half of the year and strong positive cash flow toward the end of 2026.
Things should start to change for the better once the new
EX60 electric SUV
starts hitting U.S. dealerships, which have had an aging lineup to contend with for the past few years. The
entry-level electric crossover was on sale for
a very short period of time
and had a much higher price tag than originally anticipated, the EX40 was a little too expensive for its own good and was ultimately
discontinued
, and the flagship
failed to make inroads after a rocky launch and a high price tag.
Now, though, Volvo is bringing the highly competitive EX60, as well as the
refreshed XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids
with a lot more electric range than before.
More models are also slated by the end of the decade
, when Volvo still hopes to see margins improve to 8%, up from 3.5% in 2025.
A new CEO
, poached from the Volkswagen Group’s Skoda brand, is also coming on board to try and sort things out for the Swedish brand that (still) has a reputation for dependability and safety.

"Zen 3" 微架构时代是 AMD 探索 3D V-Cache 技术初期。AMD 尽管最终并未在锐龙 5000 系列中正式推出拥有 2 颗 CCD 的 X3D 处理器，但那时在内部进行过各种 2CCD 的 3D V-Cache 产品的探索。

title: Meta 旗下 AI 智能体 Muse 将登陆智能眼镜平台，可代用户完成各种任务
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 2 日消息，Meta 宣布旗下 AI 智能体 Muse 将于近期登陆智能眼镜，用户无需拿出手机，只需通过语音下达指令，Muse 就能在后台代用户完成一系列任务。
Meta 表示，Muse 基于 Muse Spark AI 模型运行，其核心运行环境是一台部署在云端的私有持久化 Linux 虚拟机，配备独立的网页浏览器、文件系统和终端。即使用户关闭应用，这些组件仍会持续运行。为了完成用户交代的任务，Muse 可以自行决定编写并运行代码，也可以将工作分配给多个子智能体，还能创建定时任务。此外，Muse 还能够生成文档、PDF、网站以及消费记录追踪器、数据仪表盘等交互式工具。
与主要面向开发者和专业用户的其他 AI 智能体相比，Muse 的定位更加偏向普通消费者。其界面采用类似即时通讯的简化设计，并配有拟人化头像，同时重点宣传日常生活中的实际使用场景。
Meta 称，Muse 可以帮助用户预订旅行、发送电子邮件、填写表格以及通过网站购买商品，还能完成更加复杂的任务，例如与服务商协商账单、协助出售汽车，甚至可以代用户拨打电话。在支付环节，Muse 接入 Stripe 旗下 Link 服务，通过虚拟的一次性支付卡完成交易，因此 AI 本身不会接触用户的银行卡或信用卡信息。
针对智能眼镜场景，Meta 列举了更多使用场景，
包括代用户预约服务、查询机票价格、寻找替换零部件、记录饮食、提供健身指导、帮助购买用户眼前看到的商品
。用户只需说出“Hey Muse”或预先设置的 Muse 名称，然后提出具体要求，Muse 便会在后台执行任务，并在完成后向用户反馈结果。
在隐私方面，Meta 声称公司不会将 Muse 数据用于广告业务，但除非用户主动选择退出，否则相关数据将用于训练未来的 AI 模型。目前 Muse 使用的云端 Linux 虚拟机与其他环境相互隔离，但 Meta 自身仍然具备访问权限。Meta 计划在今年晚些时候推出 Confidential VM（机密虚拟机）选项，在这一模式下，甚至 Meta 自身也无法访问对应运行环境，以确保相应智能体拥有更加强大的隐私性。

在通知功能方面，用户现在能够自由控制眼镜显示的通知，并选择需要关闭的通知类型，从而进一步减少无关信息对使用体验的干扰。

用户需要通过 Meta AI 应用扫描自己的面部，并录制约 1 分钟的语音样本来创建 Hologram。完成设置后，当用户佩戴 Meta Ray-Ban Display 拨打或接听 WhatsApp 视频电话时，对方将看到一个完全由 AI 生成的用户虚拟化身，其面部表情主要根据眼镜麦克风采集到的语音信息实时生成。
此外，Meta 计划在今年晚些时候为 Ray-Ban Display 加入“Explore”应用，可以看作是一个“App 推荐位”，能够直接在眼镜上展示和推荐 Meta 认为值得体验的第三方 Web 应用，让用户更容易发现新的功能和服务，至于未来是否会进一步发展成完整的应用商店，Meta 目前尚未公布具体计划。

title: 上海市委网信办：督促平台重点防范化解七类涉未成年人心理健康风险，哔哩哔哩、小红书、拼多多等参会
content:
IT之家 10 月 2 日消息，9 月 30 日，上海市委网信办组织召开未成年人网络保护专题指导会，聚焦压实网站平台主体责任，深入推进未成年人网络保护专项行动，重点加强心理健康工作，全方位守护未成年人上网环境。属地哔哩哔哩、小红书、拼多多、喜马拉雅、SOUL、阅文集团、米哈游等 17 家重点平台参会。
IT之家注意到，会议通报了专项行动期间涉未成年人违法违规和不良信息典型案例，重点部署进一步加强未成年人心理健康工作，督促平台严格落实主体责任，重点防范化解七类涉未成年人心理健康风险。
- 一是网络沉迷成瘾风险，避免造成未成年人作息失调、注意力下降、厌学逃避等问题；
- 二是网络欺凌风险，防范其造成未成年人长期心理创伤；
- 三是容貌身材焦虑扩散风险，警惕由此滋生未成年人自卑心理等；
- 四是自残自杀类消极有害信息传播风险，严防未成年人模仿；
- 五是线上社交过度挤占现实交往风险，防止未成年人社交能力弱化，被极端对立信息误导；
- 六是 AI 技术衍生新型侵害风险，警惕 AI 换脸、虚拟人设带来的情感操控问题；
- 七是不良价值观传播风险，避免影响未成年人价值判断、诱发行为偏差。
会议要求，各平台在持续清理各类危害未成年人身心健康有害信息的基础上，针对未成年人心理健康风险，深挖风险产生的内在成因，立足算法调控、迭代升级未成年人模式、优化防护举报渠道、提升高危内容识别处置能力、规范 AI 功能应用管理、从严管控不良营销行为、扩大优质正向内容供给等关键环节，推动治理工作从事后处置向源头预防转变，切实降低互联网对未成年人心理健康的不良影响。
下一步，上海市委网信办将加大对网站平台常态化巡查、抽检和执法力度，会同有关部门对问题突出的平台依法从严处置。同时统筹协调多方资源，努力提高未成年人网络素养，培育文明上网行为习惯，推动未成年人健康安全使用网络。

title: 央视曝光二手平台低价机票陷阱，一男子被骗近 30 万元
content:
IT之家 10 月 2 日消息，据央视财经今日报道，近期，北京市公安局海淀分局接到了市民王先生的报警，称自己因购买低价机票遭遇诈骗，但是令他疑惑不解的是，订票过程中，他明明拨打了官方平台的客服电话进行查询，也确实查到了自己的“机票信息”，但还是被骗了。
警方调查发现，该订单虽然真实存在，却一直处于“未付款”状态。诈骗分子只是预先用王先生的信息占座下单，制造出“票已订好”的假象。见王先生已经上钩，诈骗分子继续以“交易仍未成功”为由，要求他下载指定的通联软件，并引导王先生开启屏幕共享。向对方提供的账户进行转款。经查，王先生共计损失二十九万余元。目前，案件仍在进一步办理中。
警方表示，此类节假日票务诈骗套路基本如下：骗子依托二手平台发布所谓超低价“特价票、内部票、员工票、捡漏票”等，利用大家想省钱、怕抢不到票的心理引流，先收取小额定金，再以操作失败、订单冻结、需要解锁退款为由，诱导持续转账。
IT之家注意到，为了进一步控制被害人的手机，诈骗分子往往会要求被害人下载小众通联软件或者屏幕共享软件。
所谓“屏幕共享”，是当前诈骗中常见的一种手段：骗子让事主下载一款陌生 App，打开后与其共享手机屏幕。此后事主如何操作手机、手机收到的银行验证码，骗子都能实时看到，相当于把手机支付软件的控制权直接交给了对方。警方因此提醒，任何陌生人要求下载屏幕共享类软件或开启屏幕共享功能的，都应当直接视为诈骗。
遇到疑似诈骗，可拨打全国公安反诈专线 96110 咨询或报警。此外，由公安部刑事侦查局组织开发的国家反诈中心 App，具备报案助手、举报线索、风险查询、诈骗预警、最新骗局曝光等功能，在接到可疑来电、短信、网址或安装可疑 App 时可智能识别并提前预警，还能检测手机内可疑应用、核验交易对方身份、进行支付风险核验。2026 年 9 月，由公安部刑事侦查局指导、上海市公安局研发的“国家反诈 AI”App 也已上线，支持以文字、语音、视频等方式拆解诈骗手法并提供防范对策。
值得注意的是，航空公司本身也不会通过电话、短信索要旅客的银行卡号和验证码，或要求转账汇款、下载陌生 App、开启屏幕共享。中国国际航空曾发布提示称，不法分子会冒充航司或代理商，以航班变动（如航班取消、延误、机械故障）、客票退改、里程变动等为由实施诈骗，旅客可通过官方客服电话、官网、官方 App 及小程序等正规渠道核实信息。

title: 桌面 AI 超算新选择：英伟达 NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB 内存版正式发布，4999 美元
content:
IT之家 10 月 2 日消息，英伟达今天正式对外披露 DGX Spark 产品更新，推出 64GB 内存版本 DGX Spark 桌面 AI 计算机，起售价 4,999 美元（现汇率约合 33,566 元人民币），将于 10 月 23 日正式发售，宏碁、戴尔、华硕、技嘉、微星、H3C 等众多 OEM 厂商均会推出基于该平台的整机产品。
官方此前推出的 128GB 版本同步更新定价，128GB FE 版本售价 6,950 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 46,666 元人民币）。
硬件层面，DGX Spark 基于 GB10 Grace‑Blackwell 超算芯片，依靠统一内存架构打通 CPU 与 GPU 内存空间，本次新增 64GB 内存版本，整机总内存 64GB，系统预留约 8GB 内存，可供模型权重与 KV 缓存使用的内存空间约 56GB，支持 NVFP4 量化格式，能够流畅部署 Gemma4 26B、Qwen3.8‑27B、Meta Muse Glimmer、Nemotron3.5 Lightning 等主流开源大模型，模型加载完成后还留有充足内存余量用于 KV 缓存，支撑长上下文推理任务。
该设备最大的亮点之一是原生具备多机集群扩展能力，内置 ConnectX‑7 高速网卡，搭配全新 NVIDIA Sync 工具套件，普通开发者无需深厚网络运维知识，就可以搭建多节点集群。套件内置 Cluster Assistant 集群助手，自动完成网络配置、设备校验、SSH 环境部署，最多支持 4 台 DGX Spark 组网。
官方实测两台 64GB DGX Spark 组成集群运行 Qwen3.8‑27B 模型，相比单台设备性能最高提升 1.7 倍，显著提高推理吞吐量。开发者还可以从普通 PC 远程接入 DGX Spark 集群，对接 VS Code、Cursor 等主流 IDE，远程监控整机状态，一键启动 vLLM 推理容器，大幅降低分布式 AI 开发门槛。
软件生态是 DGX Spark 的核心竞争力，整机完整搭载 NVIDIA CUDA 加速 AI 软件栈，深度适配 vLLM、llama.cpp 推理框架，针对本地智能体工作流做专项优化，运行本地智能体推理最高可实现 1.9 倍速度提升。Perplexity 已经完成适配，推出针对 DGX Spark 优化的便携式计算机智能体，Laguna S2.1 118B 大模型能够在硬件上完成本地部署运行。同时，Nemotron 系列模型、Gemma、Qwen、DeepSeek、Mistral、Stability.ai 等主流开源社区模型、框架都完成适配，开箱即可运行前沿模型，硬件厂商与开源社区形成完整开发者生态矩阵。
性能测试显示，部署在 DGX Spark 上的 Qwen3.8 27B 模型，评测得分距离前沿闭源模型仅有 10 分差距，证明桌面硬件已经具备运行高质量模型的能力。统一内存架构也得到行业开发者认可，Perplexity 创始人 Aravind Srinivas 评价，DGX Spark 可以近乎打满 GPU 与内存负载，散热表现稳定，统一内存设计能够最大化每瓦功耗下的 Token 产出效率，适合 7×24 小时不间断运行本地智能体任务。
当然这套平台依旧面向专业开发者，4,999 美元（现汇率约合 33,566 元人民币）起的定价，决定其目标群体为 AI 研究人员、独立开发者、小型 AI 创业团队，并非面向普通消费用户。随着 64GB 版本的推出，相比 128GB 版本降低采购门槛，让更多团队可以体验本地集群能力。

Prof. Dr.-Ing. Petra Schäfer (Mitte) wurde von Petra Rossbrey, Vorsitzende des Fördervereins der Frankfurt UAS (rechts daneben), mit dem Innovationspreis ausgezeichnet. Mit dabei: Prof. Dr. Kai-Oliver Schocke, Präsident der Frankfurt UAS (vorne links)

Förderverein der Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences verleiht Innovationspreis an das Research Lab for Urban Transport
Für ihr herausragendes Forschungskonzept zur Verkehrswende erhalten die Wissenschaftler*innen des Research Lab for Urban Transport (ReLUT) den Innovationspreis des Fördervereins der Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences (Frankfurt UAS) e.V. Der Förderverein würdigt den ambitionierten Antrag der Forschungsgruppe bei der Deutschen Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG). Die mit 2.000 Euro dotierte Auszeichnung überreichte Petra Rossbrey, die Vorsitzende des Fördervereins, am 29. September 2026 bei der offiziellen Festveranstaltung.
Anwendungsnahe Forschung und Erfahrungsgewinn
„Innovation entsteht dort, wo Forschung neue Perspektiven eröffnet und zugleich Antworten auf konkrete gesellschaftliche Herausforderungen sucht“, so Rossbrey. „Das Projekt des ReLUT verbindet genau beides: wissenschaftliche Exzellenz mit dem Anspruch, Erkenntnisse für Politik und Verkehrsplanung nutzbar zu machen. Das ist Forschung mit unmittelbarer praktischer Relevanz – und damit gelebte Innovationskraft an der Frankfurt UAS.“
„Mit ihrem Antrag bei der DFG haben unsere Forschenden Wissen und Strukturen aufgebaut, von denen wir bei künftigen Projekten profitieren“, betont Prof. Dr. Kai-Oliver Schocke, Präsident der Frankfurt UAS. „Eingespielte Abläufe, agile Teams aus Forschung und Verwaltung und die Einbindung externer Stakeholder sind das Ergebnis einer professionellen Zusammenarbeit. Von dem erfolgreichen Wissenstransfer zeugt ein weiterer Antrag unserer Hochschule, der aktuell von der DFG bewertet wird. Ich danke allen Beteiligten für ihr außerordentliches Engagement.“
Zum Konzept: Forschung für eine erfolgreiche Verkehrswende
Trotz großen Handlungsbedarfs wird das bundesweite Verkehrsnetz derzeit nur schleppend umgestaltet. Die Gründe dafür sind vielfältig: Häufig mangelt es an Wissen über konkrete Interessenskonflikte, betroffene Gruppen und die Auswirkungen unterschiedlicher Nutzungen. Erst wenn Forschung, Politik und Verkehrsplanung die Zusammenhänge präzise verstehen, können sie wirksame Strategien entwickeln.
Diese Lücken wollte das ReLUT wissenschaftlich bearbeiten und schließen. Im Zentrum seines DFG-Antrags stand die Frage, wie unsere Gesellschaft die Verkehrswende erfolgreich gestalten kann. Um diese zu beantworten hatte das Forschungsteam geplant, internationale Erkenntnisse einzubinden und mit Akteur*innen des Verkehrssystems zu kooperieren, u.a. mit der Stadt Frankfurt, dem House of Logistics & Mobility, dem Hessischen Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Energie, Verkehr, Wohnen und ländlichen Raum und dem Fachinformationsdienst Mobilitäts- und Verkehrsforschung (FID move). Erklärtes Ziel der Wissenschaftler*innen war es, eine fundierte Basis für politische und planerische Entscheidungen zu schaffen.
Zum Preis:
Der Innovationspreis des Fördervereins der Frankfurt UAS e.V. wird an Professor*innen und Mitarbeitende der Hochschule verliehen, die sich durch herausragende Leistungen hervortun: in Lehre und Weiterbildung, Forschung und Transfer oder Hochschulentwicklung. Über die Preisvergabe entscheidet eine Jury, bestehend aus Vertreterinnen und Vertretern des Fördervereins, der Hochschulleitung, des AStA, Personalrats und der Professorenschaft. Weitere Informationen:
https://www.frankfurt-university.de/de/hochschule/hochschulforderung/forderverein/
Zum ReLUT:
Das ReLUT wurde 2018 gegründet und hat sich regional und national als feste Größe in der Forschungslandschaft etabliert. Die Forschungsgruppe besteht aus 11 Professor*innen und 8 Mitarbeitenden. Gemeinsam arbeiten sie interdisziplinär und gemeinsam mit Praxispartnern zu den Themen Verkehr, Logistik und Mobilität. Seit Januar 2026 setzt das ReLUT das EU-Horizon-Projekt „NEXTLOGIC: Next-Gen Urban Freight Logistics For Net Zero Emissions Through Innovative Solutions“ um.

https://www.frankfurt-university.de/de/hochschule/hochschulforderung/forderverein/

Die 34. Internationale Conference on Plastic Optical Fibers (POF 2026) brachte rund 80 Expertinnen und Experten aus Wissenschaft und Industrie in Nürnberg zusammen. Vom 29. September bis 1. Oktober war die Technische Hochschule Nürnberg Georg Simon Ohm (Ohm) Gastgeberin der Konferenz.
Die POF-Konferenzserie gilt seit 1992 als die führende internationale wissenschaftliche Plattform für Forschung und Anwendung polymerer optischer Fasern (POF). Rund 60 Programmpunkte mit Fachvorträgen, Diskussionsrunden und Präsentationen gaben in diesem Jahr Einblicke in aktuelle Forschung und industrielle Anwendungen.
Ein Schwerpunkt der POF 2026 war der Einsatz der robusten und flexiblen Kunststoff-Lichtwellenleiter. POF können dort eingesetzt werden, wo herkömmliche elektronische Sensoren und Messfühler aufgrund der Umgebungsbedingungen nicht geeignet sind. Ein Beispiel dafür ist die Überwachung von Rotorblattlagern in Windkraftanlagen. Das Polymer Optical Fiber Application Center (POF-AC) der Ohm hat gemeinsam mit dem Nürnberger Unternehmen eolotec GmbH ein Messsystem auf Basis einer polymeren optischen Faser entwickelt. Es ermöglicht, Schäden an den Lagern frühzeitig zu erkennen. Die Technologie wird inzwischen europaweit an mehreren hundert Windkraftanlagen eingesetzt.
Ein zweiter Schwerpunkt der Konferenz ist die Nutzung polymerer optischer Fasern für die Datenübertragung in industriellen Maschinen und Anlagen. Ein wesentlicher Vorteil der optischen Datenübertragung liegt hier darin, dass sie unempfindlich gegenüber elektromagnetischen Störungen ist, und dass Lichtwellenleiter als Isolatoren keine Kurzschlüsse verursachen können. Damit eignet sich die Technologie unter anderem für Anwendungen in der Hochspannungselektronik. Ein Beispiel ist die Steuerung und Regelung leistungsstarker Elektromotoren, wie sie etwa bei Antrieben in Schienenfahrzeugen zum Einsatz kommen.
„Die Forschung zu polymeren optischen Fasern entwickelt sich in viele Richtungen. Die POF 2026 machte diese Bandbreite sichtbar und brachte Wissenschaft und Industrie miteinander ins Gespräch“, sagt Prof. Dr.-Ing. Rainer Engelbrecht, einer der Leiter des POF-AC. „Das Institut POF-AC trägt seit seiner Gründung im Jahr 2001 im Rahmen der High-Tech Offensive zur anwendungsorientierten Erforschung dieser Lichtwellenleitertechnologie bei“, ergänzt Prof. Dr.-Ing. Olaf Ziemann als weiter Institutsleiter. Gegründet von Prof. Dr. Hans Poisel, der inzwischen im Ruhestand die Konferenz verfolgte, feiert das POF-AC in diesem Jahr sein 25-jähriges Jubiläum.
Neben den regulären Fachvorträgen gehörten eingeladene Plenary Talks renommierter internationaler Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler zu den Höhepunkten der POF 2026. Sie gaben Einblicke in aktuelle Spitzenforschung und diskutieren Entwicklungen, die für die Zukunft der Polymeroptik relevant sind.
Die POF 2026 findet bereits zum dritten Mal an der Ohm statt, dabei erstmals im neuen Ohm Innovation Center (OIC). Bereits 2004 und 2015 war die internationale Fachgemeinschaft in Nürnberg zu Gast. Koordiniert werden die weltweite POF-Fachgemeinschaft und die Konferenzserie von der International Cooperative on Plastic Optical Fibers (ICPOF). Die Organisation der diesjährigen Konferenz übernahmen das Polymer Optical Fiber Application Center (POF-AC) der Ohm in Zusammenarbeit mit der ICPOF.

title: VR Summit 2026 findet in Bochum statt
content:
VR Summit 2026 findet in Bochum statt
Wie kann Extended Reality zu einem besseren Verständnis menschlicher Kognition und Gesundheit beitragen? Diese Frage steht im Zentrum des VR Summit 2026 vom 10. bis 13. Oktober 2026 in Bochum. Der Hackathon findet am 10. und 11. Oktober im Technologie- und Gründerzentrum Wattenscheid (TGW) statt, die Konferenz am 12. und 13. Oktober in der Rotunde Bochum. Es kommen internationale Forschende, Fachleute aus Entwicklung und Praxis sowie Menschen, die von Extended Reality (XR) begeistert sind. Vier Tage lang erwartet sie ein Programm des wissenschaftlichen Austauschs, der Live-Demonstrationen und des schnellen Prototypings.
Die vierte Ausgabe des Summit wird vom KlaesLab der Ruhr-Universität Bochum organisiert. Das Programm vereint Perspektiven aus Neurowissenschaften, Psychologie, klinischer Praxis, Bildung, Mensch-Computer-Interaktion und immersiver Technologie in einem eingleisigen Format, das Diskussion und Zusammenarbeit fördert.

Wie sollten automatisierte Fahrzeuge mit Fußgängerinnen und Fußgängern interagieren?

Im Juli und August 2026 fanden an der TU Chemnitz mehrere Studien statt, bei denen Interaktionen mit einem automatisierten Shuttle im Fokus standen.
| Quelle:
Foto: Dr. Josephine Halama
Download
Gemeinsame Studien der TU Chemnitz und der TU Berlin untersuchen, wie Fahrzeugmodus, Geschwindigkeit und Bremsverhalten die Interaktion mit einem automatisierten Shuttle beeinflussen
Wie reagieren Fußgängerinnen und Fußgänger auf ein automatisiertes Fahrzeug, wenn es ihnen auf der Straße begegnet? Fühlt sich die Interaktion sicher und entspannt an und macht es einen Unterschied, ob das Fahrzeug automatisiert, von einer Person gesteuert oder aus der Ferne teleoperiert wird? Wie sollte das Fahrzeug bremsen, wenn es der Fußgängerin bzw. dem Fußgänger Vorrang gewährt? Diesen Fragen sind Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler der Technischen Universität Chemnitz und der TU Berlin mit einem automatisierten Shuttle im Juli und August 2026 auf dem Universitätsteil Erfenschlager Straße 73 nachgegangen.
Die Untersuchungen führte ein Team der Professuren Allgemeine Psychologie und Human Factors (Leitung: Prof. Dr. Stefan Brandenburg) sowie Arbeitswissenschaft und Innovationsmanagement (Leitung: Prof. Dr. Angelika Bullinger-Hoffmann) der TU Chemnitz als Teil des Chemnitz Center for Mobility (CCM) durch. Kooperationspartner war das Fachgebiet Kraftfahrzeuge der TU Berlin (Leitung: Prof. Dr. Steffen Müller), welches das Fahrzeug für die Untersuchungen zur Verfügung stellte und programmierte.
Wie erleben Fußgängerinnen unterschiedliche Fahrzeugmodi?
Es wurde untersucht, welchen Einfluss der Fahrzeugmodus und die Geschwindigkeit eines Fahrzeugs auf die Wahrnehmung und das intendierte Querungsverhalten von Fußgängerinnen und Fußgängern während einer Interaktion haben. Dabei wurden drei unterschiedlichen Betriebsarten simuliert: automatisiert, manuell und teleoperiert. Das Shuttle näherte sich den Probandeninnen und Probanden mit verschiedenen Geschwindigkeiten, die im Anschluss die Situation bewerteten.
Erste Ergebnisse zeigen, dass die Interaktion mit dem Shuttle insgesamt als sicher, entspannt, selbstbestimmt und effizient wahrgenommen wurde. Mit steigender Geschwindigkeit sank jedoch die wahrgenommene Sicherheit und Entspanntheit leicht, während die Effizienz zunahm. Der Fahrzeugmodus hatte keinen Einfluss auf die Wahrnehmung der Interaktion. Die Ergebnisse legen nahe, dass sowohl automatisierte als auch teleoperierte Fahrzeuge aus Sicht der Fußgängerinnen und Fußgängereine positiv bewertete Interaktionen ermöglichen.
Wie soll ein automatisiertes Fahrzeug bremsen?
Eine weitere Studie untersuchte das Bremsverhalten des automatisierten Shuttles in der Interaktion mit Fußgängerinnen und Fußgängern. Den Probandinnen und Probanden wurden unterschiedliche Bremsmanöver des Shuttles präsentiert. Dabei wurden sowohl der Abstand, in dem das Fahrzeug zum Stillstand kam, als auch die Art der Bremsung variiert. Untersucht wurden unterschiedliche Bremsstrategien.
Die ersten Auswertungen zeigen, dass sowohl die Art des Bremsmanövers als auch der Abstand zum endgültigen Haltepunkt einen wesentlichen Einfluss darauf haben, wie die Interaktion mit dem automatisierten Fahrzeug wahrgenommen wird. Damit deutet sich an, dass nicht allein die Tatsache, dass ein automatisiertes Fahrzeug anhält, für die Wahrnehmung der Situation entscheidend ist. Auch die konkrete Ausgestaltung des Bremsvorgangs und die Position, an der das Fahrzeug zum Stillstand kommt, spielen eine wichtige Rolle.
Nutzerperspektive als Grundlage für die Gestaltung automatisierter Fahrzeuge
Die beiden Studien liefern Erkenntnisse, wie das Verhalten automatisierter Fahrzeuge in Interaktionen mit anderen Verkehrsteilnehmerinnen und -teilnehmern gestaltet werden kann. Ziel ist es, Fahrzeugverhalten nicht ausschließlich aus technischer Perspektive zu definieren, sondern auch menschzentriert zu gestalten. Die Ergebnisse der Studien werden derzeit ausgewertet und anschließend in wissenschaftlichen Fachpublikationen veröffentlicht. Die gewonnenen Erkenntnisse tragen zur menschzentrierten Gestaltung automatisierter Mobilität bei.
Die Studien wurden aus Haushaltsmitteln der TU Chemnitz und der TU Berlin finanziert. Darüber hinaus wurde die Forschung durch ein Doktorandenstipendium der Sächsischen Aufbaubank (SAB) in Kooperation mit der Europäischen Union unterstützt.
Weitere Informationen werden auf der Projekt-Homepage (www.mytuc.org/jywc) bereitgestellt.

https://www.cvag.de/fachtagung-autonomes-fahren
) dem Fachpublikum und am Abend im Rahmen einer öffentlichen und kostenfreien Veranstaltung auch interessierten Bürgerinnen und Bürgern vorgestellt.

Erstmals erfasst das Jahrbuch auch die Verkaufszahlen Humanoider Roboter und präsentiert zudem ein detailliertes Kapitel rund um die Technologie.
| Quelle:
Rainer Bez
| Copyright:
Fraunhofer IPA
Download
Humanoide Roboter sorgen weltweit für Aufmerksamkeit, während Bauroboter zunehmend den Weg von Pilotprojekten in die Praxis finden. Die neue Ausgabe von »World Robotics Service Robots«, die das Fraunhofer IPA gemeinsam mit der International Federation of Robotics veröffentlicht, enthält erstmals ein Kapitel über Humanoide Robotik sowie eine Komplettüberarbeitung des Themas Baurobotik.
Fachkräftemangel, demografischer Wandel und steigende Anforderungen an Produktivität und Flexibilität stellen Unternehmen weltweit vor große Herausforderungen. Servicerobotik gilt neben der seit Jahren etablierten Industrierobotik zunehmend als Schlüsseltechnologie, um diesen Entwicklungen zu begegnen.
Welche Trends die Branche derzeit prägen und welche Anwendungen bereits wirtschaftlich relevant sind, zeigt die neue Ausgabe von »World Robotics Service Robots«, die die International Federation of Robotics (IFR) kürzlich veröffentlicht hat. Das Fraunhofer-Institut für Produktionstechnik und Automatisierung IPA erarbeitet seit Jahren gemeinsam mit der IFR die branchenspezifischen Kapitel, die neben den statistischen Informationen technische Grundlagen und marktspezifische Analysen bieten. Im Mittelpunkt der Ausgabe 2026 stehen zwei aufstrebende Technologiefelder: Humanoide Roboter und Baurobotik.
Humanoide Robotik: Zwischen großer Erwartung und realem Praxiseinsatz
»Unternehmen benötigen heute mehr denn je eine fundierte Einordnung neuer Robotertechnologien“, sagt Dr. Werner Kraus, Leiter des Forschungsbereichs Automatisierung und Robotik am Fraunhofer IPA. „Gerade dort, wo die öffentliche Aufmerksamkeit besonders groß und die Erwartungen mitunter sehr hoch sind, ist es wichtig, Potenziale, Reifegrad und Einsatzmöglichkeiten realistisch bewerten zu können.«
Das gilt insbesondere für die Humanoide Robotik, denn kaum ein Robotikthema erfährt derzeit weltweit so viel Resonanz. Hohe Investitionen, rasante Fortschritte bei Künstlicher Intelligenz und erste Pilotanwendungen haben die Technologie in den Mittelpunkt zahlreicher Zukunftsdebatten gerückt. Vor diesem Hintergrund hat die IFR erstmals Verkaufszahlen für Humanoide 2025 erfasst. So wurden letztes Jahr knapp 7000 dieser Systeme verkauft (berücksichtigt wurden Humanoide ab einer Größe von 1,4 m). Zudem widmet das Jahrbuch Humanoiden ein eigenes Kapitel.
Dieses Kapitel bewertet den aktuellen Stand Humanoider Roboter und nennt Beispielapplikationen sowohl für Haushalt, Hotel und Gastgewerbe als auch für Produktion und Logistik. Es untersucht technologische Grundlagen wie KI-gestützte Steuerung, Trainingsmethoden, verfügbare Robotersysteme, Anwendungsszenarien sowie wirtschaftliche und sicherheitsrelevante Fragestellungen.
Die Analyse zeigt, dass Humanoide Roboter insbesondere für Materialtransport, Maschinenbeladung und einfache Serviceaufgaben großes Potenzial besitzen, da sie in menschenzentrierten Umgebungen ohne größere Anpassungen eingesetzt werden können. Gleichzeitig befinden sich die meisten Anwendungen noch im Pilotstadium, häufig mit menschlicher Unterstützung oder für sehr spezifische Aufgaben. Als größte Hürden gelten fehlende Sicherheitsstandards, hoher Trainings- und Wartungsaufwand, begrenzte Autonomie sowie eine bislang oft noch nicht überzeugende Wirtschaftlichkeit. Das Fazit lautet: Humanoide Robotik hat durch Fortschritte in KI und Sensorik erheblich an Reife gewonnen, der breite industrielle Einsatz wird jedoch erst mit weiterer technologischer Entwicklung, Standardisierung und Skalierung realistisch.
Baurobotik entwickelt sich vom Pilotprojekt zur Praxisanwendung
Neben der Humanoiden Robotik ist die Baurobotik ein weiteres Fokuskapitel im Jahrbuch. Es zeichnet das Bild eines noch kleinen Marktes, der aber insbesondere getrieben durch eine Produktivitätslücke zunehmend an Reife gewinnt und in dem robotische Systeme bereits heute konkrete Mehrwerte schaffen.
Die Anwendungsfelder reichen von Vermessung und Baustellendokumentation über Materialtransport bis hin zu Bohr-, Installations-, Maler- oder Putzarbeiten. Dabei zeigt sich ein klarer Trend: Besonders erfolgreich sind spezialisierte Robotersysteme, die einzelne Arbeitsschritte effizient und zuverlässig automatisieren. Statt vollständiger Autonomie steht zunächst die gezielte Unterstützung von Fachkräften bei körperlich belastenden, repetitiven oder sicherheitskritischen Tätigkeiten im Vordergrund. Universelle Mehrzweckplattformen spielen bislang eine untergeordnete Rolle.
Ein weiterer Schwerpunkt des Kapitels liegt auf neuen Geschäftsmodellen. Robot-as-a-Service-Angebote senken die Einstiegshürden für Unternehmen, um Anwender zu gewinnen, und erleichtern somit den Einsatz neuer Technologien auf Baustellen. Gleichzeitig gewinnt die Verknüpfung mit digitalen Planungswerkzeugen wie Building Information Modeling (BIM) an Bedeutung. Dadurch lassen sich Arbeitsabläufe zunehmend automatisieren und besser in bestehende Prozesse integrieren.
Orientierung in einem dynamischen Technologiemarkt
Mit der Ausgabe 2026 unterstreicht World Robotics Service Robots seine Rolle als internationale Referenzpublikation für Marktanalysen, Technologietrends und wirtschaftliche Entwicklungen in der Servicerobotik. Gemeinsam erfassen IFR und Fraunhofer IPA weltweit 1001 Unternehmen, die Servicerobotiklösungen für professionelle und private Anwendungen entwickeln und anbieten.
Der Band enthält außerdem auch die Fokuskapitel der letzten Jahre:
- 2025: Laborrobotik // Transportroboter in Innenräumen ohne öffentlichen Personenverkehr
- 2024: Autonomes Be- und Entladen von LKW // Transportroboter in Außenumgebungen ohne öffentlichen Personenverkehr
- 2023: Agrarrobotik für Pflanzenanbau // Professionelle Bodenreinigung // Transportroboter in Innenräumen mit Personenverkehr
World Robotics Service Robots 2026 richtet sich an Unternehmen, Investoren, Politik, Medien sowie alle Akteurinnen und Akteure, die die Zukunft der Servicerobotik aktiv mitgestalten möchten. Das Jahrbuch ist einzeln oder im Paket mit dem Band zur Industrierobotik bei der IFR erhältlich.

title: A new contest pits competitors against each other in a race to biological youth
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This week, I officially signed up for an unusual competition. One that rewards competitors for getting
I recently turned 40, and I don’t need reminding that both time and my chronological age only tick forward. But this game is focused on competitors’
biological
ages—figures that are meant to provide a better way to measure the age-related health of our organs and bodies.
Over a six-month period, around 500 of us will try to reverse our biological age as measured in a bunch of different ways. There’s even a leaderboard! The winners will include the person who shows the greatest difference between their chronological and biological age, as well as the person who manages to reverse their biological age the most.
The competition is the brainchild of the neuroscientist and physician Christin Glorioso,
who is also founder and CEO of NeuroAge Therapeutics. The company offers tools to track brain health and aging and is
running a trial
to find out if biological brain age can predict the onset of Alzheimer’s disease.
Glorioso says she has several goals for
the Younger contest
. The first, she tells me, is to “explain to the world what
aging clocks
are.” Regular Checkup readers will be familiar with these tools, but for the uninitiated, they are basically designed to measure biological age.
Many measure chemical signatures that form a layer on top of our DNA and seem to change with age. But others might involve looking at proteins or lipids in blood. Some are designed to measure functional health, while others predict when a person will die. There are more than a hundred clocks out there, and they probably each capture a specific aspect of the biological process of aging.
These clocks are proving
very useful for scientists
, who use them to study aging and development in humans and many other species. But using them to estimate the biological age of an individual person is more controversial. They’re just not good enough for that yet.
Part of the problem is that we don’t really understand what each clock is capturing.
Glorioso hopes that data collected through the Younger contest might help answer that question. She’s hoping to generate “the world’s most comprehensive clock dataset.”
longevity clinics
try to get around the limits of biological age testing by using multiple clocks. That’s this competition’s approach too. As a standard competitor, I’ll be sending a blood spot sample to TruDiagnostic, a company that measures epigenetic chemical groups on DNA and offers to reveal an overall biological age as well as a person’s pace of aging and the biological ages of each of 11 organ systems, including the heart and brain.
I’ll get a brain age score from NeuroAge once I complete the cognitive tasks on offer. I’ll also submit some physical measures like grip strength. And I’ll upload a series of selfies to an app developed by a team at Harvard that promises to tell me my face age. That’s exactly what it sounds like—an estimate of how old my face looks.
I’m intrigued to see my scores, even though I know I shouldn’t put too much stock in them. The first time I took a test, four years ago, the company I used
gave me a biological age
that matched my chronological age, which was a little disappointing and, if I’m honest, a bit underwhelming. A year later, the same company
told me I had a young heart
but a relatively old brain, liver, and hormonal system. My lifestyle hasn’t changed much since then. Will the years have made much difference?
(Ultra competitors—who pay $4,499 rather than the $999 cost of regular entry—are also offered a range of other blood tests and clocks, as well as MRI and DEXA scans. I’ve got complimentary press access to the standard package.)
Glorioso is also hoping to gather information about the effects of some purported longevity approaches.
During the competition, some participants will be offered red-light masks, access to a sauna, or other low-risk offerings that partner companies who are sponsoring the event to varying degrees might want to collect data on. “A lot of these companies just can’t afford to run [clinical] trials,” says Glorioso.
She also sees the event as a public health initiative. A couple of years ago, David Sinclair, who studies aging at Harvard Medical School, and his colleagues estimated that if we could slow down aging in the general population and increase life expectancy by one year, it
would save the US economy $38 trillion
The event officially kicks off in January, but around 120 people have already signed up, says Glorioso. Ultimately, she expects 500 participants. Each person’s six-month run starts as soon as they take their baseline measurements, whenever that may be. A handful of people have already started. “I think the majority of people are going to want to sign up after the holidays,” says Glorioso. “They’re not going to want to be trying to win an aging contest over Christmas and Hanukkah.”
Glorioso took her own baseline measurements back in August. Those initial tests suggested that her biological age was around 10 years below her chronological age. That sounded pretty impressive to me until I looked at the leaderboard and saw that competitor @Fred had a biological age 28.8 years below his chronological age.
The leaderboard is pretty sparse at the moment,
as only seven people have logged their baseline measurements so far. Six of them have biological ages tracking low, but one 47-year-old has been given a biological age of 68.1. She’s competing publicly, so I can see the breakdown of her scores. The worst is for the speed at which she can stand from sitting in a chair—by that measure, she’s been given a biological age of 100.
Hillary Lin, a longevity-focused physician in New York, has just started logging her baseline measurements for the competition. She tells me she’s taken biological age tests in the past and that they’ve tended to give scores below her chronological age, which is currently 37. Last year, the TruDiagnostic test put her pace of aging at 0.75—suggesting she’s only doing nine months’ worth of aging in a typical year. “That’s supposed to be quite good,” she says.
If it had been up to her, Lin says, she would have incorporated more blood tests into the competition, to build a fuller picture of a person’s health. And she’s worried that a six-month period might not be long enough to see changes in biological measures of aging. Still, she’s excited, and is already making plans to improve her sleep, diet, and exercise.
But she already follows a high-protein, low-carb diet and works out at the gym every day. She also visits a sauna every few days (sauna use
has been linked to improved heart health
). Glorioso’s efforts are impressive too. She tells me she’s started drinking a smoothie made from
a pond plant that has been linked to health improvements
, and that she’s cut added sugar and deep-fried foods from her diet. She’s also bought “a bunch of fancy Korean sunscreens” in an attempt to lower her face age.
I haven’t received my kit or logged my baseline measurements yet, and I’ll wait until then to start setting health goals. I don’t fancy my chances against these two competitors. But at the very least, I hope I can stand up faster than a 100-year-old.
