title: Toyota Opens $50M Michigan Battery Lab Amid EV Market Uncertainty
content:
Battery News
Automotive & Mobility
Design & Manufacturing
$50 million R&D center will evaluate battery technologies across multiple powertrains as adoption rates lag projections and competition intensifies.
October 2, 2026
10 Slides
Start slideshow
Aerial view of Toyota Battery Center of North America in York Twp., Michigan.
At a Glance
30,000-sq-ft facility evaluates batteries across hybrid, plug-in, hydrogen, and full EV powertrains in York Twp., Michigan.
Investment strengthens domestic R&D capabilities as Chinese manufacturers dominate global EV and battery technology markets.
University of Michigan partnership to train next generation of battery engineers, support North American manufacturing.
Toyota Motor North America officially opened its Toyota Battery Center of North America (TBC) on October 1, marking an expansion of the automaker's battery development capabilities and its commitment to electrification in the region. The 30,000-square-foot, $50 million facility is located at Toyota's existing R&D headquarters in York Township near Saline, less than an hour’s drive from Detroit (and a 20-minute drive from this writer’s office in Ann Arbor). The center will serve as a central hub for battery evaluation and development across the full lifecycle—from raw material sourcing to customer applications and recycling.
Strategic investment amid market transition
The facility opening comes as the US EV market navigates a complicated transition period. As we’ve reported, though EV sales continue to grow in absolute numbers, adoption rates have fallen short of earlier industry projections, with consumers citing concerns about vehicle cost, charging infrastructure availability, and range anxiety.
Related:
Battery Breaking-News Headlines
At the same time, Chinese manufacturers have emerged as formidable competitors in EV and battery technology, leveraging significant government support, integrated supply chains, and aggressive pricing strategies. This competitive pressure has intensified calls for domestic investment in battery R&D and manufacturing capabilities.
In response to these market dynamics, automakers have recalibrated their electrification strategies. Some have delayed all-electric model launches or scaled back production targets, while others have renewed focus on hybrid technologies as a bridge solution. Toyota's approach—maintaining what it calls a "multi-pathway strategy"—positions the company to serve diverse customer needs across the electrification spectrum.
The new Michigan facility directly supports this strategy by enabling development and testing across multiple powertrain technologies simultaneously. This flexibility may prove advantageous as market preferences continue to evolve and as different regions adopt electrification at varying paces.
The investment also aligns with broader industry efforts to localize battery development and manufacturing in North America, reducing dependence on overseas supply chains and positioning domestic facilities to respond more quickly to regional market demands and regulatory requirements.
While the Michigan facility represents a significant commitment to R&D, Toyota's largest battery investment remains in North Carolina, where the company has invested nearly $14 billion in a battery production facility with plans for more than 5,000 jobs.
Related:
Editors' Roundtable: Significant Battery News in September 2026
Toyota's battery plant in Liberty, NC. Credit: Toyota
Comprehensive testing capabilities
Engineers and technicians at the facility will assess battery performance and develop technologies for hybrid, plug-in hybrid, hydrogen, and fully electric vehicles. The center will support Toyota's North American manufacturing network, including battery manufacturing operations in North Carolina and vehicle assembly plants across the continent.
"Toyota has long been at the forefront of battery development," stated Keita Moritsu, Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer at Toyota Motor North America R&D. "This center is where that leadership expands to North America — and where we're building its next chapter."
Jordan Choby, Group Vice President of Powertrain, emphasized the customer benefits of having advanced testing capabilities closer to North American operations. "For Toyota customers, this facility means Toyota engineers can detect and resolve field concerns faster and closer to the source," Choby stated. "It also means we can develop longer-lasting batteries designed to perform in the conditions American drivers face every day."
an interview with WXYZ
, Choby added: "We're now the bridge between some of the most advanced battery development teams and our North American manufacturing."
Related:
Sodium-Ion Battery Production Scales Up as CBAK and HiTHIUM Target 2027 Commercial Deployment
Strategic location and political support
Toyota first announced plans for the battery center in 2023. The company's decision to locate the facility in Michigan reflects the state's automotive ecosystem advantages, including supplier networks and university partnerships.
The center represents the latest milestone in Toyota's more than 50-year history in Michigan, where the company now employs 2,000 people on its York Township campus,
according to WEMU
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer attended the grand opening ceremony and praised the investment as strengthening the state's leadership in advanced automotive manufacturing. "We are proud to welcome this investment by Toyota that positions Michigan as the best place to build the future," Whitmer stated.
Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (D-MI 6) emphasized the facility's role in maintaining American competitiveness against foreign rivals. Investments like this one from Toyota will help keep out Chinese influence in electric vehicle technology, Dingell said, according to WEMU.
The battery center "is a tangible representation of what it means to keep Michigan at the cutting edge of innovation," Dingell said. "This facility is creating good-paying high-tech jobs, supporting American manufacturing, and ensuring that the next generation of automotive innovation happens right here in Michigan."
Academic partnership and workforce development
Toyota will provide research access to the University of Michigan Electric Vehicle Center, allowing students and research partners to benefit from the facility's testing and evaluation capabilities. As a founding member of the Electric Vehicle Center, this collaboration is part of Toyota's commitment to developing the next generation of battery engineers and technicians in Michigan.
"Researchers and students will work alongside industry experts to research cutting-edge technology, and this partnership will prepare students to tackle the biggest challenges of the future, right here at home," Whitmer said, according to WEMU.
The Michigan battery center will support evaluation of batteries produced at the North Carolina facility as well as Toyota's vehicle manufacturing plants across North America.

In a record-setting commercial truck deal, international shipping giant FedEx has placed an order for 2,000 all-electric box trucks from American startup Harbinger in a deal that’s reportedly worth more than $300 million – but the ROI could be

Let’s do the math

2,000 trucks x $20,000 in fuel savings per year x 20 years. That works out to $800 million in total savings, for a
whopping

“Electrifying a fleet at this scale requires vehicles that can perform the work our robust operations demand while also delivering meaningful economic benefits,” said Paul Melander, Senior Vice President Safety & Transportation, FedEx and member of Harbinger’s Board of Directors. “Expanding our deployment of Harbinger vehicles gives us an opportunity to continue making progress toward our fleet electrification goals while reducing fuel and operating costs.”
Saving money is great, but the much more important issue for you and me is that the move to Harbinger electric trucks will help FedEx avoid more than 1.7 million tons of CO2 emissions over their projected operating lives – and that is a real win.

title: I tried taking the budget-priced Ride1Up Roadster V3 e-bike off-roading. Here's what happened next
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 3 2026 - 6:26 am PT
Ride1Up Roadster V3
is, for all intents and purposes, is a budget-focused daily driver urban bike. It’s not really a gravel bike. Maybe if you stand back a bit and squint, you could give it a bit more of a gravel bike interpretation. But ultimately, it’s a lightweight, affordable urban e-bike with decent multi-role tires that I mostly use for cruising around bike lanes and city streets.
So naturally, yesterday I took it on a 38 km (24 mile) ride where I spent most of the time off-road.
And you know what? The little
$1,295 e-bike
surprised me.
My route included just about every type of surface I probably wouldn’t have chosen when pulling a metro bike out of my quiver of e-bikes: gravel roads, hard-packed dirt, loose sandy trails, muddy puddles, and even a few rocky climbs thrown in for good measure.
The ride started with a train trip north of the city, which immediately highlighted one of the
Roadster V3’s
biggest advantages: it’s light. Compared to the
70- or 80-pound fat-tire e-bikes
that have become increasingly common, getting the Roadster through the train station, onto the train, and even holding it securely on escalators in the stations was refreshingly easy. It tips the scales at 40 lb (18 kg) stock, though the extra rack and bags I installed, not to mention the dropper seat post, probably add a couple of extra pounds to that total.
That train maneuverability might not sound like much of an “off-road” feature, but for real-world adventure riding, being able to easily combine a bike with public transportation or lift it into a truck to get to the trails can open up a lot more interesting routes.
Once I left the train station and got rolling, I kept the bike in Eco mode basically the entire time, taking advantage of the MiVice torque sensor that provides super natural power application – like the bikes is just an extension of your legs.
The Roadster V3 isn’t an overly powerful e-bike, and that’s actually part of what I like about it. It feels much more like riding a bicycle that happens to have an electric tailwind than riding a small motorcycle with pedals attached.
That was especially true off-road. I was still putting in plenty of effort, but the motor was there to take the edge off when things got tougher.
There were a couple of climbs where I realized a little too late that I was in too high of a gear. Instead of grinding nearly to a halt while trying to downshift under load, I gave the Roadster’s hidden throttle a quick blip to keep my momentum while I sorted myself out. It gave me the chance to let my own power off the pedals for a few seconds and downshift without losing too much speed.
That’s basically how I prefer to use a throttle on this kind of e-bike: not as the primary means of propulsion, but as an occasional little electric get-out-of-jail-free card. It happens a lot when I need to squirt out away from cars in the city, but the same benefits apply when I need a little extra help on a rocky ascent or to power through a section of deep sand.
And speaking of sand, the biggest challenge was definitely all of that sand.
The harder-packed sand sections of trails were fine, but some sections were fairly loose, and the Roadster’s relatively narrow Continental 700x45c tires obviously aren’t going to float over sand like a four-inch fat tire.
I could feel the bike starting to wander sideways underneath me a few times, which definitely got my attention. But with a little finesse, some momentum, and perhaps a healthy amount of optimism, I managed to keep the rubber side down and my feet on the pedals. Though again, installing
that dropper seat post
was quite helpful when I got to a more technical section and wanted to be sure I could easily and safely tap toes on the ground if it came to that, then pop the seat back up to proper pedal position as soon as I passed the obstacles – all without stopping or dismounting the bike.
Whenever back on the gravel and harder-packed dirt, though, the bike felt right at home. Even the occasional rocky sections were manageable as long as I remembered what I was riding and picked my lines accordingly.
It had also drizzled a few hours before I started, leaving several puddles scattered along the route. Here, the Roadster V3 had another surprisingly useful advantage over many purpose-built gravel bikes: fenders.
There’s something wonderfully practical about blasting through a puddle and not immediately painting a stripe of muddy water up your back.
After 38 km (24 miles) and around 1 hour and 50 minutes of riding, I rolled back home with roughly a third of the battery remaining. That was particularly impressive considering how much of the ride involved sand, dirt, climbing, and other conditions that tend to make an electric motor work harder.
Granted, when I stick to the city, I generally get around 70 km (44 miles) per charge, but riding through sand has a way of eating battery like nothing else. I’d call an extrapolated range of 57 km or 35 miles in off-road conditions pretty good, at least for a relatively small 360Wh battery.
Of course, part of that range came from the fact that I was working pretty hard, too.
My Garmin watch estimated that I burned 696 calories during the ride. I always take smartwatch calorie estimates with a grain of salt, but my legs certainly agreed with the general assessment. This wasn’t a ride where I sat back and let the motor haul me around. I was pedaling hard, choosing gears, maintaining momentum, and using the electric assist to supplement my effort rather than replace it.
And that might be my biggest takeaway from the whole experiment.
If your idea of an e-bike is something you expect to throttle around on without contributing much yourself, the Roadster V3 probably isn’t the machine I’d choose for a 38 km mixed-terrain adventure. It does have that stealth throttle, but it’s not a powerhouse and it’s not a motorcycle.
But if you’re a cycling-friendly e-biker who likes doing much of the work yourself and simply wants some assistance to flatten hills, fight headwinds, or get through tougher sections, it works remarkably well.
Would I recommend the Roadster V3 as a dedicated gravel e-bike? Probably not, at least not in this variant.
There’s a suspended version with a suspension fork
that would help a bit, but there are bikes with wider tires, more aggressive geometry, and components specifically designed for dedicated gravel riding jobs.
But that’s also what made this ride so much fun, seeing how versatile my daily driver urban bike can be when I push it.
This is the same relatively inexpensive e-bike I can ride through the city, carry onto a train without throwing out my back, commute on without looking like I’m preparing for the Dakar Rally, and then apparently spend nearly two hours bouncing through dirt, gravel, sand, rocks, and puddles.
And it got me home with battery to spare.
For $1,295
, I’d call that a pretty successful adventure.

title: Musk explains why Tesla Robotaxi is not running at night, and lidar is the answer
content:
Elon Musk
Tesla Robotaxi
Fred Lambert
| Oct 3 2026 - 7:36 am PT
Elon Musk says the main thing holding back Tesla Robotaxi’s night hours is that the cars have a hard time seeing pets in the dark. His example was “grey kittens on grey tarmac.”
That’s a low-light, low-contrast detection problem, which is the textbook weakness of cameras and the exact thing lidar and radar handle. Musk has spent years calling those sensors a “crutch” and a “fool’s errand.”
Robotaxi gets one more hour, and Musk explains why it’s only one
Late Friday night, Tesla’s Robotaxi account announced that the Austin service is “now available until 11pm.” Until now, it shut down at 10 PM.
Musk reposted the announcement and explained what’s keeping the cars off the road later than that:
“The main thing we’re trying to solve is making sure that we don’t run over pets when they’re hard to see at night. Literally trying to avoid grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark.”
Robotaxi operating hours moved from 10pm to 11pm.
The main thing we’re trying to solve is making sure that we don’t run over pets when they’re hard to see at night. Literally trying to avoid grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark.
https://t.co/y4HSVILLqd
Some context on that extra hour. When Tesla
launched Robotaxi in Austin in June 2025
, the app took ride requests from 6 AM to midnight. Fifteen months later, the service closes an hour earlier than it did on day one.
And it’s a small service. Tesla has barely scaled since launch, even with the addition of the Cybercabs last month.
Cameras need light and contrast. Lidar and radar don’t
A camera is a passive sensor. It works with whatever light bounces off an object, and it picks that object out by how much it stands apart from the background. A grey animal on grey pavement at night gives it very little of either.
Lidar is an active sensor. It fires its own laser pulses and times how long they take to come back, which gives the car a distance and a 3D shape for whatever is sitting on the road. It works the same at midnight as it does at noon, and it doesn’t need the kitten to be a different color than the asphalt. It needs the kitten to stick up from the road, and kittens, being 3D objects, tend to do that.
Radar does a similar job with radio waves and adds speed. It’s weaker on something that small, but it keeps working in the fog, dust and glare that blind cameras.
Every company running driverless cars at scale uses all three. Waymo’s sixth-generation system has 13 cameras, 4 lidars and 6 radars. In August,
Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov showed kids chasing dogs across a pitch-black street
, where the camera feed was close to useless and the lidar view was clean. Waymo’s roughly 4,000 driverless vehicles run 24 hours a day.
Tesla went the other way. It
removed radar from its cars in May 2021
, dropped ultrasonic sensors in 2022, and has never shipped a car with lidar.
Musk’s record on lidar and night vision
Musk in April 2019: “Lidar is a fool’s errand. Anyone relying on lidar is doomed.”
In February 2022, he called lidar “a seductive local maximum” and said a general solution to self-driving “necessarily will require silicon neural nets & cameras.”
In August 2025, he went further and claimed that “lidar and radar reduce safety due to sensor contention.”
And in May of this year, he posted a “photon count reconstruction” image from Tesla’s cameras and wrote: “This is why Tesla FSD can see so well at night or through extreme glare.”
That was five months ago, and now seeing at night is “the main thing” Tesla is trying to solve.
He knew the trade-off all along. When Tesla was pulling radar in 2021,
Musk told Electrek in direct messages that “vision with high-res radar would be better than pure vision.”
And NHTSA is currently
investigating 3.2 million Teslas over FSD crashes in low-visibility conditions
, a probe in which it demanded an internal Tesla document titled “Radar Saves Us.”
Electrek’s Take
Musk wrote that post like Tesla just found a new problem. It didn’t. Cameras losing dark, low-contrast objects at night is the oldest limitation in the book, and it’s why everyone else put lidar and radar on their cars. Ten years ago this month, Tesla said every car it built had the hardware for full self-driving. Its CEO is figuring out in October 2026 that grey things are hard to see in the dark.
And Musk picked the cutest example available. The same physics applies to a tire tread on the highway or a kid in a black hoodie. Those are bigger and easier to spot, but nobody should want the safety margin to be “bigger than a kitten.”
To be fair, no sensor suite gets this to zero. A Waymo ran over a bodega cat in San Francisco last October, and Waymo said it darted under the car as it pulled away. But Tesla is the only one whose CEO says the cars have trouble seeing the animal in the first place.
The cost excuse is gone too. Rivian
said this week that lidar now costs it “a few hundred dollars”
per vehicle.
What bothers us most is the part Musk skipped. The sun sets a little after 7 PM in Austin right now, so Tesla’s Robotaxis are already driving in the dark every night with a problem he says isn’t solved. And customer Teslas run “Full Self-Driving” on the same cameras at any hour, with no curfew.
Tesla is now one update away from getting back to its launch-day midnight closing time. Waymo, with lidar and radar on every car, never closes. How many more one-hour updates before Tesla admits there’s a sensor for that?

title: Watt's up, doc? Huddig hybrid loader gets a big battery boost [video]
content:
Commercial EVs
Electric Heavy Machinery
Jo Borrás
| Oct 3 2026 - 4:58 am PT
Swedish heavy equipment brand HUDDIG has given its 1370 hybrid wheel loader platform a major battery upgrade for the new model year, boosting its battery capacity from 44 kWh to fully 61 kWh – an impressive, 40% upgrade!
HUDDIG’s 1370 TIGON hybrid is an incredibly flexible machine that can be equipped for a wide range of work.
In addition to being able to do everything a conventional wheel loader can do
, it can be fitted with a loader-mounted crane (LCC), a bucket lift with an insulated basket, and even be operated via remote control. The killer app for this machine, though, is a high-capacity traction battery that enables the loader to operate as a fully electric machine.
And this isn’t a gimmick or a concept for HUDDIG
, either – the company has a deployed fleet of 41 first-generation machines that had collectively operated for 96,306 hours and saved an estimated 140,439 gallons of diesel before the launch of the second-gen machine.
With 100,000 hours of actual operation
, we’ve had a very solid foundation for our development work,” says Daniel Åkerström, design engineer at Huddig. “The larger battery makes it possible to run on electric power even more, and we therefore expect to be able to improve these figures even further with the TIGON G2 HUDDIG.”
1370 TIGON G2
1370 TIGON G2; by HUDDIG.
For its second act, HUDDIG is giving the 1370 hybrid wheel loader platform a 40% bigger battery
regenerative braking, enabling operators to recover electrical energy while braking, driving downhill, or even lowering the boom.
That doesn’t mean the G2 will just spend 40% more time spent running on electric power – it’s a substantially bigger cut in fuel use when the G1 was
running on pure electric power nearly 60% of the time.
“The combination of extended electric runtime and more attachment options makes the Tigon G2 even more versatile and provides greater freedom to adapt the machine to the job at hand,” says Daniel Myrgren, marketing and sales manager at HUDDIG. “
The electric powertrain can also provide a clear competitive advantage in jobs where low emissions and low noise levels are becoming increasingly important

title: China Wants Mass-Produced Solid-State Batteries By 2030. CATL Knows That's Hard
content:
Beijing wants large-scale production, but the world’s biggest EV battery maker warns that making the technology affordable is another matter.
Photo by:
11:00am ET
China wants large-scale solid-state battery deployment by 2030 to extend its lead in EV technology.
CATL warns that cost and manufacturing hurdles still stand between solid-state batteries and mass adoption.
Getting solid-state batteries into affordable EVs could take longer than getting them into production.
It’s easy to get excited about
solid-state batteries
in electric vehicles. Predicting when you’ll actually be able to buy an EV equipped with one is a lot harder. China has set
mass-producing solid-state batteries
as a national goal to help move things along, but its largest battery manufacturer, CATL, is careful not to overpromise.
China wants to achieve large-scale deployment of solid-state batteries by 2030, under a new battery industry roadmap released on September 28. According to the
South China Morning Post
, the aim is to extend the country’s already significant advantage in conventional batteries into the next generation of technology.
But doing that will require lower costs, better performance and stability, and advances (preferably breakthroughs) in materials and manufacturing. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology acknowledged that China’s existing battery industry has problems, including shortcomings in innovation and imbalances in supply and demand.
What’s clear is that having an enormous manufacturing and research base gives China a strong starting point. But it also needs to find the engineering solutions needed to actually make it happen.
More On This
Earlier this summer, and months before this roadmap appeared, CATL chairman Robin Zeng rated solid-state technology at level four out of nine on the readiness scale, with nine representing mass-production readiness.
Zeng had also said adoption in millions of vehicles was unlikely before the end of the decade because performance and cost remained obstacles. That makes 2030 a possible starting point for these batteries to reach more cars, rather than the year they suddenly become an industry-wide standard.
CATL has confirmed plans to start limited production of solid-state batteries in 2027, but it suggested that moving to much larger volumes would be difficult.
We’ve heard similar caution elsewhere. LG Energy Solution’s North America president Robert Lee highlighted
the difficulty of manufacturing large solid-state cells
. He also expects the first mass-market applications to not arrive in electric vehicles.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Semi-solid-state batteries are already reaching vehicles in China in limited numbers. Those introductions shouldn’t be mistaken for proof that all-solid-state batteries are ready for widespread adoption. One BloombergNEF’s forecast that solid-state technology will account for just 10% of combined global EV and battery-storage demand by 2035.
China’s battery roadmap is broader than solid-state technology. It includes sodium and flow batteries, better safety and temperature performance, and improved manufacturing quality. A separate target calls for long-life lithium batteries capable of 15,000 cycles, although that doesn’t mean solid-state batteries will come close.
The coordinated national push should not be taken lightly. China sets its economic and industrial priorities through five-year plans, giving government agencies and businesses a shared direction. The previous cycle, which ran between 2021–2025, saw China cement its EV dominance: by its end, the country accounted for 70% of global electric car production.
The new 2026–2030 battery roadmap aims to carry that advantage into the next generation of technology.
Getting solid-state batteries in cars
will be a milestone. Getting them into millions of reasonably priced cars will be the real achievement.

title: Tesla Sales Are Down. But They're Doing A Lot Better Than Some Competitors
content:
Tesla Sales Are Down. But They're Doing A Lot Better Than Some Competitors
Tesla sales fell slightly in the third quarter. But it could be a lot, lot worse.
- Tesla deliveries were down about 2% in the third quarter.
- That's not a bad showing, given how tumultuous a year it has been for automakers.
- The company doesn't break out invidual model sales, but the Model 3 and Model Y account for the vast majority of its sales.
Tesla global deliveries fell slightly in the third quarter, the company reported Friday. Deliveries dipped from 497,099 in the third quarter of 2025 to 486,532 this year, a 2.1% drop. But based on the year we've had in the EV market, this is hardly a bad showing.
Many competitors posted double-digit drops in EV sales in the U.S. this quarter as the industry reels from the loss of the federal tax credit and regulations that encouraged more EV sales. The Chinese market, too, is in a tough spot, as domestic competitors remain locked in a perpetual price war, putting pressure on Tesla. Meanwhile in Europe, Chinese imports are starting to push out demand for other foreign brands. All of this explains why European, Japanese, and American automakers are struggling.
Against that backdrop, a 2.1% slide is remarkably mild. Tesla is still fighting a multi-front battle against the all of the world's best automakers with only two real volume products, both of which are based on a platform first introduced in 2017. The new three-row Model Y L is likely helping, as are the recent refreshes in the Model Y and Model 3, but it's incredible how much staying power those products have had, as dozens of competitors have come to market since. (Tesla does not break out specific model sales, but the Model S/X are dead, and the Cybertruck is a low-volume product primarily for the U.S.)
The Cybertruck was Tesla's first all-new product since 2017. It's been a commercial flop, which means future growth has to come from increased Model 3/Y sales or new models like the Robotaxi.
None can match Tesla's dominance, at least in the U.S. market. The Model 3 and Model Y together account for about half of all U.S. EV sales. The Model Y remains the best-selling EV in the world, and was, for a time, its best-selling vehicle overall. It's the only EV to ever come close to taking that title.
Still, Tesla's worldwide third-quarter delivery numbers were essentially the same this year as they were in 2023. The company has avoided the sales drops of its competitors, but despite strong EV market growth over the last three years, Tesla's car business looks flat.
It's not hard to guess why. CEO Elon Musk has been absolutely clear that he sees Tesla as primarily an AI company, with its main bets being making Full Self-Driving (Supervised) into a truly autonomous system for public consumption, and with making humanoid Optimus robots. Those are the kinds of gambles that Wall Street likes; incremental improvements to the cars seem far less sexy to both Musk and investors.
Critics have argued that such a focus on AI and autonomy will leave Tesla's car business vulnerable to competitors. That may well be true. But so far, Tesla's lead has proven remarkably enduring. And with Semi mass production starting, the Cybercab on the road, a true self-driving pilot in Texas, and a Roadster event scheduled for later this month, the company may not be out of ideas yet.

title: The 2027 Cadillac Escalade IQ Gets A NACS Port And Faster Home Charging
content:
All 2027 GM EVs will come out of the factory with a Tesla-style charging port, but the Escalade EV gets a little extra.
Photo by:
Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
8:00am ET
General Motors is making a few improvements to its flagship electric SUV.
The 2027 Cadillac Escalade IQ comes with a native NACS port.
A more powerful on-board charger comes standard across all trim levels.
The all-electric
Cadillac Escalade SUV
will be a little easier to charge at Tesla Superchargers, and owners who plan to charge at home are also in for a little treat.
That’s because
General Motors
is ditching the old CCS1 charging port for a native Tesla-style NACS connector on the 2027 Cadillac Escalade IQ and
long-wheelbase Cadillac Escalade IQL
. What’s more, GM’s flagship electric SUV will come with a more powerful on-board charger across all trim levels, as discovered by
GM Authority
Gallery: 2026 Cadillac Escalade IQ
For 2027, the electric
Escalade
will be equipped with a 19.2-kilowatt on-board charger, which enables owners to use a 240-volt, 80-ampere connection to top up the car’s batteries a little faster than on the outgoing model. By comparison, the 2026 Escalade came with an 11.5 kW module on the Luxury and Sport trims, whereas the Premium Luxury and Premium Sport were offered with the 19.2 kW OBC.
The upgraded on-board charger doesn’t affect the Escalade’s DC charging capabilities, but it’s a welcome addition for those who want to take full advantage of their house’s grid connection. The 2027 Escalade IQ also comes standard with the Dual Level Charge Cord, which can be plugged into either a 120V or a 240V outlet, though it goes without saying that charging the Escalade’s massive 205-kilowatt-hour battery on a Level 1 connection will take days, not hours.
On a 120V outlet, the Dual Level Charge Cord provides just 1.4 kW of power, which means a full 0-to-100% charge will take almost a week.
On the DC charging side, however, the native NACS port removes the need for a CCS-to-NACS adapter at Tesla Superchargers and other NACS-equipped stalls. At the same time, though, topping up at a CCS will only be possible with a NACS-to-CCS adapter. Thankfully, though, most non-Tesla public charging networks offer both connectors now, so it shouldn’t be an issue on the road.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The same NACS port will accept a NACS home charger—unlike Mercedes-Benz’s newest EVs—but if there’s already a J1772 charger installed, the owner will need an adapter to make it work.
As a reminder, all General Motors EVs are scheduled to switch from a CCS1 charging port to
NACS for the 2027 model year

title: 余承东：华为星河通信团队驾驶享界 G9 实测独库公路，98.7% 路段信号都很好
content:
IT之家 10 月 3 日消息，华为常务董事、产品投资评审委员会主任、终端 BG 董事长余承东今日发文称，前阵子，星河通信团队开着享界 G9 去了趟独库公路，实测车载星河通信在独库公路的表现，反复测试下来 98.7% 以上的路段信号都非常不错。
他表示：“星河通信是鸿蒙智行六大独有核心技术之一。华为在通信领域积累了几十年，我们也把这些技术带到了车上，希望大家开车走到更远的地方，都能保持稳定通信，出行更有底。国庆准备自驾的朋友，路上如果遇到弱网，可以打开车上热点，给同行的家人朋友共享网络”。
IT之家注意到，去年 2 月发布的尊界 S800 车型首发搭载华为星河通信，该技术支持主动智能选网、双网双待，可实现三网连接和弱网加速，并支持将网络共享至手机、平板等设备。在无地面网络时，支持通过车载卫星完成通话及紧急联络功能。
据悉，独库公路北起北疆石油之城克拉玛依市独山子区，南至终点为天山南麓、塔里木盆地北缘的南疆阿克苏地区库车市。据官方最新公告，G217 线独库公路 2026 年国庆节假日期间正常通行，自 2026 年 10 月 8 日 20 时起实施冬季封闭，禁止社会车辆通行（伊阿铁路、G3033 奎独库高速公路、G217 天山神秘大峡谷等重点项目物资运输及相关施工车辆除外）。

title: 充电桩扫码充电暗藏“弹窗投保”陷阱，消费者莫名被扣款
content:
感谢IT之家网友 不一样的体验 的线索投递！
IT之家 10 月 3 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，有消费者在充电桩扫码充电时遭遇“弹窗投保”陷阱，扫码操作后，页面会弹出伪装成广告的窗口，诱导用户填写信息并办理保险业务。
IT之家从报道获悉，西藏林芝的索朗先生在一个充电站给电动汽车充电的时候，手机扫充电桩的二维码，首先跳出来的并不是充电桩的小程序，而是一个看着并不像广告的页面，要求输入银行卡、手机号等信息。索朗以为这是充电必须填写的信息，因此也没多想就填了，过了一段时间后居然收到了银行发来的某保险公司的扣款信息。
该消费者称：“我以为充电桩需要验证身份信息，当时输入了身份证号、银行卡号。我没太在意，因为当时比较着急就直接输进去了。当时也没有扣款，然后突然扣款，我发现是那种保险类的。”
索朗告诉记者，当时弹窗页面并不像是广告，因为广告一般都有关闭按钮并且会有倒计时，而这个弹窗所展示的内容，也没有明确说是办理保险，更没有详细展示保险的产品说明以及保单等关键信息。
据悉，“弹窗投保”陷阱多发生于：充电桩扫码、快递柜扫码、共享充电宝扫码、停车缴费等各类生活消费场景。扫码操作后，页面会弹出伪装成广告的窗口，诱导用户填写信息并办理保险业务。

title: 公安机关发布国庆假期安全提示：警惕机票退改签、冒充电商物流客服等电信网络诈骗
content:
IT之家 10 月 3 日消息，据公安部刑侦局，国庆假期期间，旅游出行、休闲娱乐、购物消费活动增多，为提高广大群众的防范意识，针对假期高发的诈骗类型，公安机关今日发布防范安全提示。IT之家附整理主要内容如下：
一、警惕机票退改签类诈骗
假期期间，民航客流增多，票务紧张，航班延误、退票改签等情况多发，容易给不法分子以可乘之机。诈骗分子往往冒充航空公司客服，通过电话或者短信与被害人进行联系，准确说出其姓名、身份证号、航班号、登机时间等信息，以此骗取信任，再谎称航班因故障、天气等原因延误或取消，需被害人办理机票退改签手续，并主动提出给予赔偿，诱导被害人点击不明链接、登录虚假网站或下载具有屏幕共享、远程控制功能的诈骗 App，套取被害人银行卡账号、密码、验证码实施诈骗，或者以缴纳保证金等理由，直接诱骗被害人向诈骗分子转账。
公安机关提醒：当被告知航班延误或取消，应通过航空公司客服电话、官方网站等正规渠道核实，避免脱离官方平台操作，切勿向不明账户转账，切勿点击不明链接、登录虚假网站、下载涉诈 App 或开启屏幕共享功能。
二、警惕冒充电商物流客服类诈骗
假期期间，购物消费活动增多，诈骗分子通常会通过群发短信、拨打电话等方式，冒充电商物流平台客服，以快递丢失、快递滞留、包裹破损、网购商品存在质量问题等为由，向被害人主动提出理赔补偿，诱导点击所谓退货链接、登录虚假购物网站，套取被害人身份证号、银行卡账号、密码、验证码等实施诈骗，或者以缴纳保证金等理由，直接诱骗被害人向诈骗分子转账。
公安机关提醒：正规网络商家退款无需买家提前支付费用，退款均通过原有支付渠道退回，无需买家提供银行卡号、密码、验证码。接到自称电商、物流客服电话的，务必主动与官方平台核实，切勿脱离官方平台。
三、警惕网络游戏虚假交易和追星票务类诈骗
假期期间，人们使用短视频、社交、游戏平台的时间明显增多，诈骗分子会借机在平台发布“高价收购游戏账号”“免费送皮肤”“解除防沉迷”等网络游戏虚假交易类信息，或兜售所谓“明星见面会”“明星演唱会”门票等，主要吸引青少年群体关注并添加好友，随后再诱骗其点击陌生链接、扫描二维码、登录仿冒平台、下载涉诈 App 等实施诈骗。
公安机关提醒：一切脱离官方平台监管的私下交易均存在被骗风险。家长要加强对未成年人使用电子设备的监督和管理，设置支付限额和使用权限，教育引导孩子从小树立不添加陌生网友、不点击陌生链接、不下载不明来源 App、不透露个人信息的反诈防范意识。

title: 成达万高铁铺轨施工启动，我国“八纵八横”高铁网建设迎来新进展
content:
IT之家 10 月 3 日消息，据中国铁路官方公众号，10 月 1 日 8 时 18 分，在四川省南充市南充北站的施工现场，随着第一组 500 米长钢轨稳稳落下，成都至达州至万州高速铁路（以下简称：成达万高铁）铺轨施工正式启动。
成达万高铁是我国“八纵八横”高铁网沿江通道的重要组成部分，线路西起四川省成都市天府站，途经四川省资阳市、遂宁市、南充市、达州市及重庆市开州区、万州区，接入既有郑渝高铁万州北站，正线全长 477 公里，设计时速 350 公里。
成达万高铁全线铺轨总里程约 890 公里，含 178 组道岔，其中无砟道岔 133 组、有砟道岔 45 组。目前，成达万高铁建设桥梁桩基、承台、墩身已全部完成，隧道、站房及“四电”工程正按节点有序推进。铺轨节点的如期实现，标志着项目从线下工程转入线上施工阶段，为全线按期通车奠定坚实基础。
据介绍，成达万高铁建成后，将形成成都直达中原和京津冀地区的便捷客运通道，对推动成渝地区双城经济圈建设、长江经济带发展具有重要意义。
IT之家注：“八纵”通道包括沿海通道、京沪通道、京港（台）通道、京哈-京港澳通道、呼南通道、京昆通道、包（银）海通道、兰（西）广通道。“八横”通道包括绥满通道、京兰通道、青银通道、陆桥通道、沿江通道、沪昆通道、厦渝通道、广昆通道。

title: 点球大战制胜！国足击败乌兹别克斯坦队，时隔 28 年再夺亚运会男足比赛铜牌
content:
IT之家 10 月 3 日消息，2026 爱知-名古屋亚运会男足三四名决赛，中国队在常规时间内 2 比 2 战平乌兹别克斯坦队。点球大战中，中国队 4 比 3 取胜，获得本次亚运会男足比赛铜牌。
上半场，中国队胡荷韬破门。半场结束，中国男足与对手 1-1 战平。
下半场，中国队王钰栋破门。90 分钟双方战成 2-2。
这也是中国队时隔 28 年再次获得亚运会男足比赛铜牌！也是亚运会男足项目实行 U23 年龄限制后，中国队首次获得奖牌。
IT之家查询获悉，中国男足曾在 1994 年广岛亚运会上获得银牌，并于 1978 年、1998 年两次获得铜牌。本届比赛，中国队时隔 28 年再次闯入亚运会男足四强，并最终登上领奖台。
另外，今年 1 月，在 2026 年 U23 亚洲杯半决赛中，中国 U23 男足以 3:0 战胜越南队，历史首次晋级决赛，彭啸、向余望、王钰栋先后建功。在最终决赛中，中国队负于日本队，与冠军失之交臂（获得亚军）。这也是中国队在 U23 亚洲杯参赛历史上最好成绩。

title: 超八成 16 岁以下青少年绕过监管，澳大利亚拟强化社媒禁令
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 3 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，去年 12 月，澳大利亚正式实施全球首个针对 16 岁以下未成年人的社交媒体禁令。然而，有研究显示，这一禁令在澳大利亚实际执行效果并不明显。近期，澳大利亚政府推出新法案，继续强化社交媒体管控和青少年社交媒体禁令。
今年 9 月，澳大利亚议会通过了《网络安全法案》修订案，继续强化社交媒体最低年龄限制的执法。修订案扩大了澳大利亚电子安全局和电子安全专员的执法权限，并提高了违反社交媒体最低年龄限制的罚款额度。新规加大惩戒力度，倒逼受管控社交媒体平台履行法定义务，
阻止 16 岁以下澳大利亚人持有平台账号
澳大利亚政府还在 9 月公布《数字注意责任法》草案，并向公众征询意见。这份草案要求互联网公司允许用户关闭算法选项。如果社交媒体平台未能保护青少年用户免受有害内容侵害，
将面临最高 1.09 亿澳元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 5.09 亿元人民币）
澳大利亚今年 7 月发布的官方监管与评估报告显示，社交媒体禁令去年 12 月正式实施，3 个月后，
80% 以上的 16 岁以下青少年
通过虚报年龄、借用家人或朋友账号等各种方式绕过监管，继续使用社交媒体。禁令效果有限。
IT之家注意到，去年 12 月，澳大利亚开始实施全球首个 16 岁以下未成年人社交媒体禁令，禁止未成年人使用 Facebook、Snapchat、YouTube 等社交媒体平台。
澳大利亚电子安全专员办公室表示，限制措施旨在保护澳大利亚未成年人，防止其在社交媒体使用过程中遭受心理压力与潜在风险。澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯在一段给未成年人的视频中表示，他们比任何人都更清楚在算法、无尽的信息流以及随之而来的压力中成长的感受。他强调：“好好利用即将到来的学校假期，而不是不停地刷手机。去学习一项新的运动、一门新乐器，或读一读那本在你书架上放了很久的书。重要的是，多和你的朋友、家人面对面地度过高质量的时光。”
今年 4 月，有报道称澳大利亚监管机构拟对 Facebook、Instagram、Snapchat、YouTube 等平台采取法律行动，指控它们未能有效阻止 16 岁以下未成年人使用其服务。

DHL: Agentic AI Reshapes Supply Chains and Workforce
DHL has released the eighth edition of its biennial flagship research report, the Logistics Trend Radar 8.0, revealing how artificial intelligence,
robotics and physical automation
are changing supply chain operations.
The report analyses how companies are shifting from simple digital assistance toward full operational autonomy.
“Supply chains are changing faster than ever as AI and workforce trends increasingly influence one another. The organisations that succeed will be those that understand these shifts early and are able to turn them into practical advantages for their business and their people,” says Katja Busch, Chief Commercial Officer at DHL and Head of DHL Customer Solutions & Innovation.
Amazon Invests $100m in Indiana Robotics Manufacturing
Amazon has announced plans to invest more than US$100m in a new 585,000 square-foot
advanced manufacturing
facility in Greenwood, Indiana.
The investment will create 300
skilled manufacturing
and engineering jobs, with average salaries of nearly US$100,000 annually.
According to Amazon, it supports more than 27,000 direct jobs and 40,000 indirect jobs across the state, contributing more than US$35bn to Indiana's GDP.
“We're thrilled to bring 300 advanced manufacturing jobs to Greenwood, Indiana, and to continue investing in growth and opportunities across the state,” says Holly Sullivan, Vice President of Economic Development at Amazon. “This facility represents a significant investment in the Indianapolis community that will create jobs with a median salary well above the regional average.”
Maersk has assumed direct management of PUMA's North American distribution network. Credit: PUMA
How Maersk Will Optimise PUMA's US Fulfilment Network
Maersk has assumed direct management of PUMA's North American distribution network, taking operational control of three automated fulfilment centres across California, Arizona and Indiana.
Totalling 2.3 million square feet, the trio of facilities supports PUMA's wholesale partners, retail stores and
ecommerce channels
The partnership aims to boost fulfilment performance, maximise throughput speed and streamline regional product movement by combining robotics technology with integrated logistics expertise.
“This next phase of our partnership strengthens our ability to move products more efficiently across channels, improve responsiveness to changing demand and create greater value from the investments we've made in our US distribution infrastructure,” says Helmut Leibbrand, Senior Vice President of Supply Chain Management and Logistics Americas at PUMA.

FedEx is an expert
in this, having transported two giant pandas from China to Georgia, US.

M&S and New Look Partner for Circular Textile Value Chains
The UK fashion and textile industry contributes £62bn (US$82.15bn) to the UK economy, according to Oxford Economics and the UK Fashion and Textile Association (UKFT).
According to the report, it supports 1.3 million jobs and is one of the largest sectors in the country.

title: LG Energy Solution to supply 46,100 round cells to Mercedes - electrive.com
content:
According to a media report, LG Energy Solution will supply round cells with a diameter of 46 millimeters and a height of 100 millimeters - a novel format - for Mercedes-Benz's next-gen EVs. Deliveries are set to begin in 2028.
Image: LG Energy Solution
This is according to a report by the usually well-informed South Korean portal
The Elec
, which specifies that the 46100 round cells are a new cylindrical battery cell format in the 46-series that LG Energy Solution has not yet unveiled. According to the portal, the company is expected to begin setting up production lines next year and start delivering the batteries from 2028.
The Elec
cites industry insiders for this news and notes that there are plans to establish a first production line for 46100 battery cells at LG Energy Solution’s Polish plant in Wrocław – with Mercedes-Benz as the customer. Additionally, LGES is reportedly considering investments in module assembly, where the cells will be combined into modules. However, this information has not been officially confirmed.
For context: the 46-series battery cells, particularly the 4680 round cells (with a height of 80 mm), are primarily used by several automakers – most notably Tesla. Formats such as 4695 and 46120 (with heights of 95 mm and 120 mm, respectively) are also available but less common. However, LGES is one of the suppliers with a broad portfolio of 46-series cells. At the end of last year, the South Korean company began producing 4695 cells at its Ochang plant, and by the end of this year,
earlier reports indicated
that production of “diverse 46-Series cylindrical cells, ranging from 4680 to 46120 cells” would start at the US plant in Arizona. However, it was previously unknown that LGES was also preparing a version with a height of 100 millimetres.
The Elec
also reports that LG Energy Solution is preparing a facility for the new 46100 cell type in Ochang to adapt it to the specifications of the planned mass-production line in Poland. It comes as little surprise that Mercedes-Benz is set to become the main customer. Since October 2024, the two companies have already signed four long-term supply agreements. However, the partnership is not exclusive: in April, the Stuttgart-based automaker also signed its first long-term supply contract for electric vehicle batteries
with Samsung SDI
. Additionally, CATL is part of the supplier network. Previously, the company had also sourced battery cells from SK On and Farasis.

title: 10,000-ton rare earth magnets production targeted by US firm
content: A Florida-based company has signed a letter of intent with Evolution Metals & Technologies Corp to deploy behind-the-meter hydrogen power supporting EM&T’s rare earth magnet and critical materials operations. The agreement puts VIVIFY’s hydrogen platforms to work for one of the most strategically important supply chains in the country, and it does so without waiting on the legacy grid.Rare earth permanent magnets drive electric vehiclesRare earth permanent magnets drive electric vehicles, medical imaging equipment, and defense systems. Miami-headquartered EM&T is building a non-China supply chain for them, scaling magnet production capacity to approximately 10,000 tons annually and developing a fully integrated U.S. industrial campus. That work runs on power, and large blocks of reliable power have become one of the hardest inputs for advanced manufacturers to secure, according to details available. “Every serious manufacturer in this country is asking the same question right now: where does the power come from? EM&T is rebuilding one of the most important supply chains America has,” said Jason Herring, founder and CEO of VIVIFY Technology. “Our job is to make sure power is never the thing that slows them down. The engineering is done. Now it goes to work.” VIVIFY revealed that its VIVIFY’s containerized hydrogen power unit, delivers up to 1MW per container and scales by adding modules. Water is the primary fuel input, output is 99% emission-free, and no ongoing fuel resupply is required. Rather than waiting on a single large installation or a utility interconnection timeline, capacity is added container by container as each phase of production comes online. The Flying Pig joins the flagship Hydrogen Oxygen Generator (HOG) and the Clean Air Technology (CAT) five-stage emissions control system in the VIVIFY Arsenal.The agreement marks VIVIFY’s first announced commitment with a publicly traded company and a direct application of its platforms to American manufacturing and national defense supply chains.Rare earth refining and magnet manufacturing are industrial processes that require substantial infrastructure and dependable energy supplies.For a company attempting to establish a domestic supply chain, electricity availability can therefore become an important consideration alongside access to raw materials, processing technology, manufacturing equipment and logistics.Evolution Metals’ LOI with VIVIFY is designed to explore whether hydrogen-based generation can provide some of that required energy infrastructure without depending exclusively on traditional grid expansion.The proposed approach could also allow the companies to evaluate grid-independent or grid-complementary configurations depending on the eventual site requirements and regulatory conditions.VIVIFY’s hydrogen technology could potentially provide a modular component of that infrastructure strategy. For VIVIFY, the proposed collaboration would place its hydrogen-energy technology in the context of a planned industrial-scale critical-materials operation.Whether the partnership ultimately moves from a non-binding LOI to commercial deployment will depend on technical, regulatory and economic considerations that have yet to be resolved.

title: Digital twins could make ammonia-powered ships safer from toxic leaks
content: The US, South Korea and Germany have recently joined forces in order to develop a new digital twin technology that could predict how toxic ammonia leaks spread aboard ships.The American Bureau of Shipping (ABS), Siemens and HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE), announced the agreement at Gastech 2026 in Bangkok. They reportedly signed the memorandum of understanding (MOU) at the end of the month. The initiative will bring together computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with digital twins to rapidly model ammonia dispersion following a leak. It could allow engineers to test a wide range of leak and accident scenarios early in the vessel design process. This could identify safety risks before construction begins.“By pairing CFD analysis with digital twin technology, this project gives designers a faster, more rigorous way to understand leak behavior,” Patrick Ryan, ABS CTO and Senior Vice President, pointed out. Tracking toxic leaksThe shipping industry has been exploring ammonia as an alternative marine fuel as it looks for new ways to power vessels. Green ammonia could significantly cut the sector’s reliance on fossil fuels and reduce emissions from shipping.Still, the fuel also poses safety challenges, particularly if it leaks. The chemical is highly corrosive, toxic when inhaled or touched, and flammable under specific concentrations. The new project aims to predict how it could spread after a leak.ABS, HD KSOE and Siemens signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU).Credit: ABSRyan stressed the partnership’s significance. “ABS is proud to bring our technical authority to this collaboration with HD KSOE and Siemens.” Each company will contribute a different part of the project.HD KSOE will develop ammonia safety systems and lead experimental research. Siemens will provide simulation analysis and digital twin technology, while ABS will supply a safety assessment methodology built around digital twins.Chang Kwangpil, head of the Future Technology Institute at HD KSOE, said AI and digital twin technologies are set to play an key role in shipbuilding research and development. “The AI transformation of the shipbuilding industry is not simply about applying new technologies; it is a process of innovating the way we work,” Kwangpil noted.Safer ship designsA digital twin is a virtual model that mirrors a real-world physical object, system, or process using live data. It can be utilized to simulate and study how it behaves under different conditions, such as potential failures, accidents, or environmental changes. Combining this method with CFD could model how ammonia moves through and around a vessel after a leak. Engineers can then study multiple potential accidents without physically recreating every scenario. The findings can be used to assess safety measures while a vessel is still being designed. Physics-based simulation and digital twins could play a key role in ensuring the safety and reliability of vessels. “Through close technical collaboration with HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering and ABS, we will accelerate safety validation for ammonia-fueled vessels and continue to support digital innovation across the global marine industry,” Byung Joon Oh, country manager of Siemens Digital Industries Software Korea, concluded in a press release. ABS is also working with the maritime industry on the safe use of ammonia as a marine fuel. “

title: GM brings 33% denser lithium manganese-rich EV battery to Tennessee
content: The race to build cheaper, longer-range electric cars has taken a leap forward in central Tennessee. Ultium Cells has announced that it will produce lithium manganese-rich (LMR) prismatic battery cells at its plant near Nashville. The company is a joint venture between General Motors and South Korea’s LG Energy Solution. Once operational, the facility is expected to become the world’s first commercial manufacturing site for this next-generation battery design.Upgrades to the Spring Hill plant will start later this year. Engineers expect to finish construction by 2028.Automakers have long struggled to balance battery price against driving range. Today, the global market relies heavily on two main chemistries: premium high-nickel packs that offer maximum range at a steep cost, and low-cost lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells that sacrifice range to keep prices down.Offers greater energy densityLMR prismatic cells are engineered to disrupt that equation. The new chemistry provides 33% greater energy density than standard LFP cells, yet it can be produced at roughly the same price point.For General Motors, integrating this technology provides an intermediate tier. High-nickel batteries will remain the benchmark for premium vehicles requiring maximum endurance. However, LMR cells will allow entry-level and mid-tier models to gain substantial driving range without inflated sticker prices.“High-nickel batteries will continue to give customers the highest range in our portfolio, while adding LMR positions us to leapfrog today’s more affordable chemistries and deliver lower costs with better performance,” said GM in a press release. Company executives note that this flexibility will help GM scale vehicle production more efficiently, broaden customer reach, and improve profit margins.Addressing the main bottleneckThe decision to scale up manufacturing follows a major scientific hurdle cleared just weeks ago.While LMR chemistry has held promise for years, it has suffered from a critical design flaw: gas buildup. In large electric vehicle packs, trapped gases create severe internal pressure. This swelling warps the battery’s internal structure and accelerates degradation, making large-format cells unsafe and short-lived.In September, researchers from LG Energy Solution and Seoul National University published a practical solution. The team discovered that gas formation is driven by volatile oxygen reactions during charge cycles.By fine-tuning the operational voltage window, the researchers stabilized how oxygen moves inside the cell. The results were striking. In laboratory evaluations, optimized 40 Ah-class cells maintained 92.2% of their original energy capacity after 883 charge and discharge cycles—a durability threshold suitable for automotive use.Tailoring specific packsBeyond the chemistry itself, the Spring Hill project signals a broader change in how modern battery plants operate.The expansion gives Ultium Cells the ability to manufacture multiple cell chemistries and geometric form factors on the same campus. This enables the joint venture to tailor specific packs to distinct vehicle types, from heavy pickup trucks to compact city cars.“Beyond flexing manufacturing might, bringing this new battery cell to market first is a milestone moment for keeping America competitive globally in EV and battery technology leadership,” concluded GM.

title: Laser-generated muons successfully penetrate concrete and lead shields
content: Superman’s X-ray vision isn’t actually that super. X-rays work well for seeing through thin objects or medical scans, but thick concrete walls and dense lead shields block them completely. Physicists have found a solution in muons, which are heavy subatomic particles created using powerful lasers that can easily pass through dense materials that stop X-rays in their tracks.A Romanian research team at the Extreme Light Infrastructure—Nuclear Physics (ELI-NP) facility, led in part by Mădălina Dobre, has successfully used an artificial, laser-driven muon beam to image an object for the first time.Artificially generated muon beams with adjustable properties offer significant utility for scanning dense objects that block other imaging techniques.Next-gen scanningCosmic muons naturally form in Earth’s upper atmosphere and penetrate deep into solid structures, enabling non-destructive imaging of hidden interiors. Earlier, “muography” mapped hidden internal structures, such as the secret chamber discovered inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in 2023. However, scan times remain impractically slow because the natural stream of these cosmic particles arrives so gradually. Facilities currently produce lower-energy beams using traditional particle accelerators, whereas higher-energy muons require laser-wakefield-accelerated electrons interacting with solid targets.Researchers at Romania’s Horia Hulubei National Institute have now solved this speed challenge by producing images with an artificial muon beam for the first time. Their laser-driven technique generates controlled particle streams on demand, opening the door to fast and reliable practical imaging.Dobre’s team produced the first image dominated by artificial, laser-driven muons using the high-power laser at Romania’s ELI-NP facility. The laser accelerated electrons through a gas, directing them into a solid target to create light bursts that generated muon pairs. After filtering out unwanted particles with plastic, paraffin, and a 2-meter-thick concrete wall, detectors located in a van recorded the shadow of a lead brick pile. Comparing these measurements with computer simulations confirmed that roughly 90% of the detected high-energy particles were muons matching the source model.“By comparing the data with Monte Carlo simulations, we confirm that the measured beam profile and object imaging are consistent with artificially produced muons of energy of a few GeV. To our knowledge, this represents the first demonstration of imaging dominated by an artificial, laser-driven muon beam,” the team wrote in the preprint study paper version. On-demand deep scans for infrastructureThe initial pictures aren’t sharp yet. They are grainy, low-resolution, and look more like crude shadows than high-definition scans.Yet, the proof of concept changes everything. Natural cosmic ray muography yields only about 1 muon per square centimeter per second. Laser-driven bursts can produce millions of particles in split seconds, drastically reducing scan times.Generating concentrated muon beams on demand shrinks a timeline that once took half a year down to mere minutes. Future iterations could allow engineers to scan aging bridges, help geologists map underground mineral deposits, and give border inspectors a way to spot heavily shielded nuclear material hidden deep inside shipping containers.Volcanologists could use the technology to map internal magma chambers and lava tubes to help predict eruptions.

title: New center boosts nuclear isotope output for deep-space missions
content: Canada is moving to expand its role in supplying nuclear isotopes that could power spacecraft on long-duration missions.The Nuclear Innovation Institute launched the Canadian Centre for Space Isotopes this week in Toronto. The organization will focus on research, policy, and partnerships across the nuclear and space industries.Radioisotope power systems convert heat from radioactive decay into electricity. They provide steady power without relying on sunlight, making them useful for missions traveling far from the Sun.Powering missions beyond MarsSolar panels become less effective as spacecraft move farther from the Sun. Radioisotope systems can continue generating power in regions where solar energy becomes difficult to collect.NASA has used the technology for decades on deep-space spacecraft and planetary rovers. These systems can also provide heat for hardware operating in extremely cold environments.Demand could grow as space agencies and commercial companies pursue longer missions. The supply of suitable isotopes, however, remains a major challenge for future spacecraft. Canada sees an opportunity in that gap. The country already has extensive experience producing medical isotopes and operating nuclear facilities.New isotope supply chainThe new center aims to connect that nuclear expertise with the specialized requirements of spaceflight. Its work will run through 2030 and support Canada’s broader effort to increase isotope production.Canada’s space sector generated $3.8 billion in federal GDP during 2024, according to the Canadian Space Agency. The industry has grown 14 percent since 2019 and supports more than 28,000 direct and indirect jobs.Former Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield supported the initiative during his keynote address in Toronto. He pointed to the growing need for dependable power as space activity expands.Hadfield said Canada’s engineering capabilities and raw materials could help the country compete in the emerging market.Jessica Linthorne, president and CEO of the Nuclear Innovation Institute, said the center will bring together nuclear specialists, space companies and researchers.The group will produce policy research and identify opportunities for Canadian industry. It will also pursue partnerships across the nuclear, aerospace and research sectors.Spacebound nuclear powerThe center plans to release a report in early 2027 examining how Canada could expand its position in space isotope production. Government officials have also linked the initiative to Ontario’s plan to double isotope production by 2030. Ontario already has an established nuclear workforce and major medical isotope capabilities.Energy and Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson said the nuclear sector could help meet demand for space technologies while creating domestic economic opportunities. Ontario Energy and Mines Minister Stephen Lecce said existing isotope expertise could support missions extending well beyond Mars.NII board chair James Scongack described the project as a meeting point between Canada’s space and nuclear capabilities. The engineering challenge extends beyond producing radioactive material. A future supply chain must provide consistent isotope production while meeting the specialized requirements of spacecraft power systems.Reliable nuclear power could become increasingly valuable as exploration pushes deeper into the solar system. For spacecraft operating far from Earth, dependable energy can determine how long instruments survive and how much science a mission can deliver.

title: Schneider tests quantum chip that boosts energy forecasts by 41%
content: Australian government-backed Silicon Quantum Computing (SQC), whose investors include telecom giant Telstra and Commonwealth Bank, has teamed up with global energy technology firm Schneider Electric to test a quantum-enhanced chip that improved household energy forecasting accuracy by an average of 20 percent, with gains reaching 41 percent.The companies have secured A$3.6 million (US$2.5 million) from the Australian government to move into the second stage of the Critical Technologies Challenge Program. The project, conducted with UNSW Sydney, will now expand testing to hundreds of Australian homes.SQC develops silicon-based quantum computing systems and manufactures quantum processor chips using atomic-scale engineering. Schneider Electric develops energy management and automation technologies used across homes, buildings, data centers, factories and power grids.The collaboration is targeting a growing challenge for power grids: predicting energy demand and supply as more homes add rooftop solar panels, batteries and electric vehicles. These resources can cause household power consumption and generation to change considerably throughout the day.Quantum boosts grid forecastsAt the center of the project is SQC’s Watermelon chip, an atomically engineered processor designed to generate quantum features that can be combined with conventional data used by existing models.Rather than replacing conventional computing systems, the approach uses the quantum processor alongside classical hardware. SQC says the additional quantum features can produce richer models with stronger predictive capabilities.During the first stage of the program, researchers applied Watermelon to next-day energy forecasting data covering a 12-month period. Compared with the classical benchmark, the quantum-enhanced approach produced an average 20% improvement in forecasting accuracy, with improvements reaching as high as 41%.“We have always believed that quantum processors would work alongside CPUs and GPUs to deliver real-world performance gains,” said Michelle Simmons, founder and CEO of SQC. “The results we have achieved with Schneider Electric demonstrate how quantum-enhanced AI can address practical challenges across the energy sector and time-series datasets more broadly.”The results are significant because even relatively small forecasting improvements can help utilities make better decisions about when energy should be generated, stored or consumed.Hundreds of homes nextThe second stage will test the technology on a much larger dataset covering hundreds of homes across Australia. The quantum system will also be integrated directly into Schneider Electric’s existing workflows, moving the project closer to a potential production environment.“The energy system is becoming more dynamic with variables like rooftop solar, EVs, and home batteries creating new levels of complexity,” said Colette Munro, Pacific Zone President at Schneider Electric.“Together with SQC, we’ve demonstrated how advanced energy technology has the potential to better manage this complexity, lowering costs for consumers and using energy more efficiently across the system.”SQC launched Watermelon in 2025 and has since deployed the system for applications including telecommunications, banking and high-frequency trading. The technology can be accessed through the cloud or purchased as hardware, including for data center deployment.The latest project will test whether the forecasting gains seen during the initial trial can be maintained as the technology moves from a limited dataset to hundreds of real-world household energy systems.

title: Tiny rice-sized GaN chip packs 3x more power, 20x better signals
content: Northrop Grumman has unveiled a new gallium nitride chip aimed at handling demanding radio-frequency workloads with less hardware.The FORTITUDE™ chip can combine signal switching and filtering inside a single device. Northrop Grumman says it delivers three times more power and 20 times better signal quality.That performance could matter across systems that operate in crowded or interference-heavy environments. The company lists satellites, radar, GPS, electronic warfare, and future 6G networks among potential applications.GaN gets new structureThe chip is also small enough to fit within a package roughly the size of a grain of rice. Its compact footprint could help engineers reduce weight and power demands inside larger systems.FORTITUDE uses a patented gallium nitride structure built from multiple ultra-thin layers. Northrop Grumman describes the architecture as a “superlattice.” The stacked layers control electron movement through the semiconductor while increasing charge density.The company says the structure can carry about 10 times the charge of standard GaN chips. That higher density helps the device handle more electrical power without simply increasing its physical size.Heat management also becomes important as RF hardware pushes higher power levels. The superlattice design aims to reduce energy losses during operation. The approach comes from years of Northrop Grumman research into microelectronics. The technology was previously known as the Super Lattice Castellated Field Effect Transistor.Switching and filtering togetherMost RF systems rely on multiple components to manipulate signals as they move through a circuit. FORTITUDE puts two important functions into the same semiconductor.The device can switch signals at subnanosecond speeds while filtering unwanted frequencies. That combination lets it shape electrical signals before they reach other parts of a system.Northrop Grumman says FORTITUDE can operate across frequencies ranging from kilohertz levels to 20 GHz. That broad range could support multiple radar and communications bands with fewer specialized components. The company says the chip can replace dozens of components in some system architectures. That could reduce weight and simplify the electronics surrounding the RF chain.More signal in crowded spectrumModern RF systems increasingly operate alongside other transmitters and sources of interference. Military platforms face particularly demanding conditions when several electronic systems compete for spectrum.FORTITUDE is designed to maintain cleaner signal performance under those conditions. Northrop Grumman says its architecture can deliver clearer data while consuming less power.The technology also targets commercial systems. Future communications networks could place greater demands on RF hardware as operators move toward higher frequencies and more complex signal environments.Northrop Grumman is developing FORTITUDE for both defense and commercial markets in the United States. Its potential applications span communications, sensing, and electronic warfare.The engineering challenge remains familiar even as the hardware changes. More information needs to move through increasingly crowded electromagnetic environments. FORTITUDE tackles that problem at the semiconductor level, combining more power and signal control inside a much smaller piece of hardware.

title: US Task Force 401 taps drone defenses that autonomously classify threats
content: Digital Force Technologies (DFT) has secured a US contract to supply counter-drone systems that combine sensor data, autonomous threat assessment and engagement capabilities in a single software-driven architecture. The San Diego-based company announced the $500 million Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) award from Joint Interagency Task Force 401 on September 29. It supports the task force’s Domestic Shield program, which aims to accelerate layered drone defenses for military installations, critical assets and personnel. DFT will provide its counter-unmanned aerial systems and counter-small unmanned aerial systems capabilities for force protection, base defense and counter-drone operations. The contract covers requirements within the continental United States and overseas. Sensor fusion at the tactical edge At the center of DFT’s systems is SeraphimOS, an edge-based software architecture designed to combine information from multiple sensors. According to the company, it autonomously assesses and classifies threats while delivering actionable information to operators in real time. The architecture brings sensing, decision-making and action together at the tactical edge. Its intended role is to help operators respond to drone threats while accommodating changes in equipment and mission requirements. “This award represents a significant milestone for DFT and reinforces the importance of rapidly delivering adaptable, mission-ready technology to the warfighter,” said Justin MacLaurin, President and CEO of Digital Force Technologies. “The UAS threat is evolving at an extraordinary pace, and defending our forces and critical infrastructure requires systems that can evolve just as quickly.” Open architecture connects sensors and effectors SeraphimOS uses an open architecture that supports integration with sensors, effectors, platforms and third-party systems. DFT said this allows it to configure capabilities for specific missions without requiring a closed technology stack supplied by a single vendor. That flexibility is central to the company’s approach as drone threats change. Operators can integrate new sensing and engagement capabilities as their requirements evolve. “Our SeraphimOS -powered mission systems bring sensing, decision and action together at the tactical edge, giving operators the flexibility to integrate new sensors, effectors and capabilities as the mission changes,” MacLaurin said. For counter-drone missions , the platform supports detection, tracking and identification through engagement using kinetic and non-kinetic effects. DFT also said SeraphimOS enables advanced orchestration of uncrewed systems. This includes coordinated sensing across multiple domains and autonomous operations in contested, disconnected, and degraded environments. Domestic Shield targets layered protection The award supports Domestic Shield ’s push to deploy layered counter-drone capabilities against rapidly evolving unmanned aerial threats. The initiative focuses on protecting military installations, critical assets and personnel. “Safeguarding our critical assets against increasingly agile drone threats demands flexible, highly mobile protection that can deploy rapidly where it is needed most,” said U.S. Army Brig. Gen. Matt Ross, director of Joint Interagency Task Force 401. “By continuing to provide capabilities on the marketplace through a streamlined framework, JIATF-401 is able to cut through red tape and rapidly deliver state-of-the-art counter-UAS solutions into the hands of warfighters,” he added . The announcement describes the systems’ intended capabilities but does not provide detection ranges, engagement distances, or performance results. It also does not specify deployment quantities or individual delivery orders under the IDIQ contract.

title: NTU and Singfilm Solar send perovskite solar cells to space aboard CRIMSON-1 satellite
content:
NTU and Singfilm Solar send perovskite solar cells to space aboard CRIMSON-1 satellite
Nanyang Technological University (NTU Singapore) has launched CRIMSON-1, a nanosatellite carrying perovskite solar cells developed together with NUS spin-off
Singfilm Solar
, marking the first time a Singapore-made perovskite solar module has flown in orbit. The satellite lifted off on October 1 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base, California, and was deployed about 520 km above Earth using Exolaunch's EXOpod Nova system.
The team from NTU Satellite Research Centre and their partners. Image credit: NTU
CRIMSON-1 is NTU's 14th research satellite, built by the university's Satellite Research Centre (SaRC). The 5 kg, shoebox-sized spacecraft is designed to run a year-long mission testing two technologies under real orbital conditions: the perovskite solar cells, and an onboard AI system that filters and analyzes satellite imagery before transmitting it to Earth, cutting down on the raw data scientists would otherwise need to process manually.
The flexible perovskite module, built on ultrathin glass, is mounted alongside the satellite's primary gallium arsenide panels, which will continue to power the spacecraft itself. The mission will measure how well the perovskite cells withstand the physical stresses of launch and the subsequent radiation, thermal cycling and vacuum conditions of low Earth orbit, along with their actual power output once in space. Gallium arsenide cells, the current standard for spacecraft, cost between US$250 and US$450 per watt; perovskite cells are thinner, lighter and have the potential to be manufactured far more cheaply, which is the core appeal for future satellite designs.
"This mission marks the first spaceflight of a flexible perovskite solar module built on ultrathin glass, and the first deployment of a Singapore-made solar module in orbit," said Hou Yi, Assistant Professor at NUS and founder of Singfilm Solar. NTU Deputy President Professor Christian Wolfrum added that "CRIMSON-1 carries next-generation perovskite solar cells and edge AI computing into orbit. These technologies can only be validated under real space conditions."
CRIMSON-1 is backed by Singapore's National Space Agency (NSAS) under its Space Access Programme, part of the national Space Technology Development Programme, which has allocated S$210 million (about US$157 million) to space technology R&D since 2022. The Infocomm Media Development Authority secured the satellite's spectrum and orbital resources through the UN's International Telecommunication Union. "Perovskite solar cells will provide a compelling advantage over conventional panels - their thin, lightweight properties make them particularly well suited for space applications, where every gram matters," said Ngiam Le Na, NSAS's chief executive.
NTU has previously flown perovskite cells in space on its
ARCADE satellite in 2023
, as part of a
broader slate of space projects under Singapore's Space Technology Program
. Singfilm Solar, which spun out of NUS, reported a record 22.6% power conversion efficiency for a perovskite solar panel in 2024.

title: Prussian blue framework pushes perovskite solar cells to 26.9% efficiency, holds up in 30×30 cm submodules
content:
Prussian blue framework pushes perovskite solar cells to 26.9% efficiency, holds up in 30×30 cm submodules
Researchers at Xiamen University, Jinan University, Tsinghua University, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Uppsala University in Sweden, the Institute of High Energy Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the Shanghai Advanced Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and
Guangdong Mellow Energy
have developed a Prussian blue-based strategy to control both crystallization and ion migration in perovskite solar cells, achieving a champion efficiency of 26.9% in small-area cells that held up at scale in large submodules.
The team incorporated a lattice-matched Prussian blue scaffold into the perovskite film as a structural template. Using in situ grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) measurements at the Beijing and Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facilities, they found that the Prussian blue framework converts the film's typically uncontrolled, homogeneous nucleation into a more ordered, heterogeneous process. It suppressed the formation of non-photoactive δ-FAPbI₃ phases in favor of the photoactive α-FAPbI₃ phase, promoted crystal growth along a preferred orientation, and relieved tensile strain in the film. Separately, the framework's redox-active Fe–C≡N–Fe network helped convert lead⁰ and iodine⁰ defects, while its rigid, open cage structure locked mobile cations in place, suppressing the ion migration that normally degrades perovskite devices under operation.
The strategy yielded champion power conversion efficiencies of 26.1% in n-i-p architecture and 26.9% in p-i-n architecture (26.2% certified) for small-area cells. Scaling up, the team reached 23.4% in 6×6 cm minimodules and a certified 22.9% in 30×30 cm submodules. Submodules with initial efficiencies of 20.2–21.0% showed no discernible decline relative to a silicon reference cell over five months of outdoor testing, alongside robust performance under accelerated aging.
